Pune : Ānandāśramamudraṇālaye 1904 (Ānandāśrama Sanskrit Series, 47).

body.text: Pātañjalayogaśāstram

children.text: yas tyaktvā rūpam ādyaṃ prabhavati jagato 'nekadhānugrahāya prakṣīṇakleśarāśir viṣamaviṣadharo 'nekavaktraḥ subhogī /
sarvajñānaprasūtir bhujagaparikaraḥ prītaye yasya nityaṃ devo 'hīśaḥ sa vo 'vyāt sitavimalatanur yogado yogayuktaḥ //1//

body.text: atha yogānuśāsanam || YS_1.1 ||

athety ayam adhikārārthaḥ. yogānuśāsanaṃ śāstram adhikṛtaṃ veditavyam. yogaḥ samādhiḥ. sa ca sārvabhaumaś cittasya dharmaḥ. kṣiptaṃ mūḍhaṃ vikṣiptam ekāgraṃ niruddham iti cittabhūmayaḥ. tatra vikṣipte cetasi vikṣepopasarjanībhūtaḥ samādhir na yogapakṣe vartate. yas tv ekāgre cetasi sadbhūtam arthaṃ pradyotayati kṣiṇoti ca kleśān karmabandhanāni ślathayati nirodham abhimukhaṃ karoti sa saṃprajñāto yoga ity ākhyāyate. sa ca vitarkānugato vicārānugata ānandānugato 'smitānugata ity upariṣṭān nivedayiṣyāmaḥ. sarvavṛttinirodhe tv asaṃprajñātaḥ samādhiḥ. 1.1
tasya lakṣaṇābhidhitsayedaṃ sūtraṃ pravavṛte ---

sarvaśabdāgrahaṇāt saṃprajñāto 'pi yoga ity ākhyāyate. cittaṃ hi prakhyāpravṛttisthitiśīlatvāt triguṇam.
  prakhyārūpaṃ hi cittasattvaṃ rajastamobhyāṃ saṃsṛṣṭam aiśvaryaviṣayapriyaṃ bhavati. tad eva tamasānuviddham adharmājñānāvairāgyānaiśvaryopagaṃ bhavati. tad eva prakṣīṇamohāvaraṇaṃ sarvataḥ pradyotamānam anuviddhaṃ rajomātrayā dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryopagaṃ bhavati.
  tad eva rajoleśamalāpetaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhaṃ sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātraṃ dharmameghadhyānopagaṃ bhavati. tat paraṃ prasaṃkhyānam ity ācakṣate dhyāyinaḥ. citiśaktir apariṇāminy apratisaṃkramā darśitaviṣayā śuddhā cānantā ca sattvaguṇātmikā ceyam ato viparītā vivekakhyātir iti. atas tasyāṃ viraktaṃ cittaṃ tām api khyātiṃ niruṇaddhi. tadavasthaṃ saṃskāropagaṃ bhavati. sa nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ. na tatra kiṃcit saṃprajñāyata ity asaṃprajñātaḥ. dvividhaḥ sa yogaś cittavṛttinirodha iti. 1.2
tadavasthe cetasi viṣayābhāvād buddhibodhātmā puruṣaḥ kiṃsvabhāva iti ---
svarūpapratiṣṭhā tadānīṃ citiśaktir yathā kaivalye. vyutthānacitte tu sati tathāpi bhavantī na tathā. 1.3
kathaṃ tarhi, darśitaviṣayatvāt ---

vyutthāne yāś cittavṛttayas tadaviśiṣṭavṛttiḥ puruṣaḥ. tathā ca sūtram ekam eva darśanaṃ khyātir eva darśanam iti. cittam ayaskāntamaṇikalpaṃ saṃnidhimātropakāri dṛśyatvena svaṃ bhavati puruṣasya svāminaḥ. tasmāc cittavṛttibodhe puruṣasyānādiḥ saṃbandho hetuḥ. 1.4
tāḥ punar niroddhavyā bahutve sati cittasya ---

kleśahetukāḥ karmāśayapracaye kṣetrībhūtāḥ kliṣṭāḥ. khyātiviṣayā guṇādhikāravirodhinyo 'kliṣṭāḥ. kliṣṭapravāhapatitā apy akliṣṭāḥ. kliṣṭacchidreṣv apy akliṣṭā bhavanti. akliṣṭacchideṣu kliṣṭā iti. tathājātīyakāḥ saṃskārā vṛttibhir eva kriyante. saṃskāraiś ca vṛttaya iti. evaṃ vṛttisaṃskāracakram aniśam āvartate. tad evaṃbhūtaṃ cittam avasitādhikāram ātmakalpena vyavatiṣṭhate pralayaṃ vā gacchatīti. tāḥ kliṣṭāś cākliṣṭāś ca pañcadhā vṛttayaḥ. 1.5
pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtayaḥ || YS_1.6 ||
pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni || YS_1.7 ||

indriyapraṇālikayā cittasya bāhyavastūparāgāt tadviṣayā sāmānyaviśeṣātmano 'rthasya viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānā vṛttiḥ pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam. phalam aviśiṣṭaḥ pauruṣeyaś cittavṛttibodhaḥ. pratisaṃvedī puruṣa ity upariṣṭād upapādayiṣyāmaḥ.
  anumeyasya tulyajātīyeṣv anuvṛtto bhinnajātīyebhyo vyāvṛttaḥ saṃbandho yas tadviṣayā sāmānyāvadhāraṇapradhānā vṛttir anumānam. yathā deśāntaraprāpter gatimac candratārakaṃ caitravat, vindhyaś cāprāptir agatiḥ. āptena dṛṣṭo 'numito vārthaḥ paratra svabodhasaṃkrāntaye śabdenopadiśyate, śabdāt tadarthaviṣayā vṛttiḥ śrotur āgamaḥ. yasyāśraddheyārtho vaktā na dṛṣṭānumitārthaḥ sa āgamaḥ plavate. mūlavaktari tu dṛṣṭānumitārthe nirviplavaḥ syāt. 1.7
viparyayo mithyājñānam atadrūpapratiṣṭham || YS_1.8 ||

sa kasmān na pramāṇam. yataḥ pramāṇena bādhyate. bhūtārthaviṣayatvāt pramāṇasya. tatra pramāṇena bādhanam apramāṇasya dṛṣṭam. tadyathā dvicandradarśanaṃ sadviṣayeṇaikacandradarśanena bādhyata iti. seyaṃ pañcaparvā bhavaty avidyā. avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśā iti. eta eva svasaṃjñābhis tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisro 'ndhatāmisra iti. ete cittamalaprasaṅgenābhidhāsyante. 1.8
śabdajñānānupātī vastuśūnyo vikalpaḥ || YS_1.9 ||

sa na pramāṇopārohī. na viparyayopārohī ca. vastuśūnyatve 'pi śabdajñānamāhātmyanibandhano vyavahāro dṛśyate. tad yathā caitanyaṃ puruṣasya svarūpam iti. yadā citir eva puruṣas tadā kim atra kena vyapadiśyate.
  bhavati ca vyapadeśe vṛttiḥ. yathā caitrasya gaur iti. tathā pratiṣiddhavastudharmo niṣkriyaḥ puruṣaḥ, tiṣṭhati bāṇaḥ sthāsyati sthita iti. gatinivṛttau dhātvarthamātraṃ gamyate. tathānutpattidharmā puruṣa iti, utpattidharmasyābhāvamātram avagamyate na puruṣānvayī dharmaḥ. tasmād vikalpitaḥ sa dharmas tena cāsti vyavahāra iti. 1.9
abhāvapratyayālambanā vṛttir nidrā || YS_1.10 ||

sā ca saṃprabodhe pratyavamarśāt pratyayaviśeṣaḥ. katham, sukham aham asvāpsam. prasannaṃ me manaḥ. prajñāṃ me viśāradīkaroti. duḥkham aham asvāpsam. styānaṃ me mano bhramaty anavasthitam gāḍhaṃ mūḍho 'ham asvāpsam. gurūṇi me gātrāṇi. klāntaṃ me cittam. alasaṃ muṣitam iva tiṣṭhatīti. sa khalv ayaṃ prabuddhasya pratyavamarśo na syād asati pratyayānubhave tadāśritāḥ smṛtayś ca tadviṣayā na syuḥ. tasmāt pratyayaviśeṣo nidrā. sā ca samādhāv itarapratyayavan niroddhavyeti. 1.10
anubhūtaviṣayāsaṃpramoṣaḥ smṛtiḥ || YS_1.11 ||

kiṃ pratyayasya cittaṃ smaraty āhosvid viṣayasyeti. grāhyoparaktaḥ pratyayo grāhyagrahaṇobhayākāranirbhāsas tajjātīyakaṃ saṃskāram ārabhate. sa saṃskāraḥ svavyañjakāñjanas tadākārām eva grāhyagrahaṇobhayātmikāṃ smṛtiṃ janayati.
  tatra grahaṇākārapūrvā buddhiḥ. grāhyākārapūrvā smṛtiḥ. sā ca dvayī --- bhāvitasmartavyā cābhāvitasmartavyā ca. svapne bhāvitasmartavyā. jāgratsamaye tv abhāvitasmartavyeti. sarvāḥ smṛtayaḥ pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtīnām anubhavāt prabhavanti. sarvāś caitā vṛttayaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmikāḥ. sukhaduḥkhamohāś ca kleśeṣu vyākhyeyāḥ. sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ. duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ. mohaḥ punar avidyeti. etāḥ sarvā vṛttayo niroddhavyāḥ. āsāṃ nirodhe saṃprajñāto vā samādhir bhavaty asaṃprajñāto veti. 1.11
athāsāṃ nirodhe ka upāya iti ---

children.translated_text: Their cessation [is achieved] through practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). || YS_1.12 ||

body.translated_text: Now, what is the means for their cessation? —

body.text: cittanadī nāmobhayatovāhinī vahati kalyāṇāya vahati pāpāya ca. yā tu kaivalyaprāgbhārā vivekaviṣayanimnā sā kalyāṇavahā. saṃsāraprāgbhārāvivekaviṣayaniṃnā pāpavahā. tatra vairāgyeṇa viṣayasrotaḥ khilīkriyate. vivekadarśanābhyāsena vivekasrota udghāṭyata ity ubhayādhīnaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ. 1.12
body.translated_text: The river of the mind (<s>citta</s>) flows both ways — it flows toward the good and it flows toward the bad. That which is inclined toward the state of isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) and flows toward the ground of discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka</s>) — that flows toward the good. That which is inclined toward <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) and flows toward the ground of non-discrimination — that flows toward the bad. Among these, through dispassion the current toward sense-objects is blocked; through the practice of discriminative vision, the current of discrimination is opened. Thus the cessation of mental modifications (<s>cittavṛttinirodha</s>) depends on both. 1.12

body.text: tatra sthitau yatno 'bhyāsaḥ || YS_1.13 ||
body.translated_text: Of these [two], practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) is the effort toward stability (<s>sthiti</s>). || YS_1.13 ||

body.text: cittasyāvṛttikasya praśāntavāhitā sthitiḥ. tadarthaḥ prayatno vīryam utsāhaḥ. tat saṃpipādayiṣayā tat sādhanānuṣṭhānam abhyāsaḥ. 1.13
body.translated_text: Stability is the undisturbed flow of the mind when it is free from modifications. The effort directed toward that — energy, enthusiasm — and the performance of the means for accomplishing it, is practice. 1.13

body.text: sa tu dīrghakālanairantaryasatkārāsevito dṛḍhabhūmiḥ || YS_1.14 ||
body.translated_text: But that [practice] becomes firmly grounded when attended to for a long time, without interruption, and with reverence. || YS_1.14 ||

body.text: dīrghakālāsevito nirantarāsevitaḥ satkārāsevitaḥ. tapasā brahmacaryeṇa vidyayā śraddhayā ca saṃpāditaḥ satkāravān dṛḍhabhūmir bhavati. vyutthānasaṃskāreṇa drāg ity evānabhibhūtaviṣaya ity arthaḥ. 1.14
body.translated_text: Attended to for a long time, attended to without interruption, attended to with reverence — accomplished through austerity (<s>tapas</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), and faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) — it becomes reverent and firmly grounded. [This means that] it is not quickly overwhelmed by the impressions of emergence (<s>vyutthānasaṃskāra</s>). 1.14

body.text: dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayavitṛṣṇasya vaśīkārasaṃjñā vairāgyam || YS_1.15 ||
body.translated_text: Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) is the consciousness of mastery (<s>vaśīkārasaṃjñā</s>) of one who is free from craving for seen and heard objects. || YS_1.15 ||

body.text: striyo 'nnapānam aiśvaryam iti dṛṣṭaviṣaye vitṛṣṇasya svargavaidehyaprakṛtilayatvaprāptāv ānuśravikaviṣaye vitṛṣṇasya divyādivyaviṣayasaṃprayoge 'pi cittasya viṣayadoṣadarśinaḥ prasaṃkhyānabalād anābhogātmikā heyopādeyaśūnyā vaśīkārasaṃjñā vairāgyam. 1.15
body.translated_text: One who is free from craving for seen objects such as women, food, drink, and power; and free from craving for heard objects such as the attainment of heaven, of bodiless existence, and of absorption into <s>Prakṛti</s> — for such a one, even in contact with divine and non-divine objects, the mind perceiving the defects in sense-objects, by the power of meditative discernment (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>), [attains] the consciousness of mastery, which is spontaneous, devoid of the categories of 'to be abandoned' and 'to be acquired' — that is dispassion. 1.15

body.text: tat paraṃ puruṣakhyāter guṇavaitṛṣṇyam || YS_1.16 ||
body.translated_text: The supreme [dispassion] is the freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s>, [arising] from the discernment of <s>Puruṣa</s>. || YS_1.16 ||

body.text: dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayadoṣadarśī viraktaḥ puruṣadarśanābhyāsāt tacchuddhipravivekāpyāyitabuddhir guṇebhyo vyaktāvyaktadharmakebhyo virakta iti. tad dvayaṃ vairāgyam. tatra yad uttaraṃ taj jñānaprasādamātram. yasyodaye sati yogī pratyuditakhyātir evaṃ manyate --- prāptaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ, kṣīṇāḥ kṣetavyāḥ kleśāḥ, chinnaḥ śliṣṭaparvā bhavasaṃkramaḥ, yasyāvicchedāj janitvā mriyate mṛtvā ca jāyata iti. jñānasyaiva parā kāṣṭhā vairāgyam. etasyaiva hi nāntarīyakaṃ kaivalyam iti. 1.16
body.translated_text: One who, seeing the defects in seen and heard objects, becomes dispassionate, and whose intellect is nourished by the practice of <s>Puruṣa</s>-discernment and the discrimination of its purity, becomes dispassionate toward the <s>guṇas</s> in both their manifest and unmanifest states. Thus there are two [types of] dispassion. Of these, the latter is nothing but the clarity of knowledge (<s>jñānaprasāda</s>). Upon its arising, the <s>yogin</s>, possessing manifest discernment (<s>khyāti</s>), thinks thus: 'What was to be attained has been attained; the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) that were to be diminished have been diminished; the chain of existence, whose links were joined, has been cut — for it was through its unbroken continuity that, having been born one dies, and having died one is born again.' The supreme limit of knowledge is dispassion. Indeed, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) is the necessary consequence of this alone. 1.16

body.text: athopāyadvayena niruddhacittavṛtteḥ katham ucyate saṃprajñātaḥ samādhir iti ---

children.translated_text: Cognitive [<s>samādhi</s>] is that which is accompanied by deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>), reflection (<s>vicāra</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), and I-am-ness (<s>asmitā</s>). || YS_1.17 ||

body.translated_text: Now, how is it said that the <s>samādhi</s> of one whose mental modifications have been ceased through these two means is 'cognitive' (<s>saṃprajñāta</s>)? —

body.text: vitarkaś cittasyālambane sthūla ābhogaḥ. sūkṣmo vicāraḥ. ānando hlādaḥ. ekātmikā saṃvid asmitā. tatra prathamaś catuṣṭayānugataḥ samādhiḥ savitarkaḥ. dvitīyo vitarkavikalaḥ savicāraḥ. tṛtīyo vicāravikalaḥ sānandaḥ. caturthas tadvikalo 'smitāmātra iti. sarva ete sālambanāḥ samādhayaḥ. 1.17
body.translated_text: Deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) is the gross engagement of the mind with its object. Reflection (<s>vicāra</s>) is the subtle [engagement]. Bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) is joy. I-am-ness (<s>asmitā</s>) is the unitary awareness. Among these, the first <s>samādhi</s>, accompanied by all four, is 'with deliberation' (<s>savitarka</s>). The second, lacking deliberation, is 'with reflection' (<s>savicāra</s>). The third, lacking reflection, is 'with bliss' (<s>sānanda</s>). The fourth, lacking even that, is 'I-am-ness alone' (<s>asmitāmātra</s>). All of these are <s>samādhis</s> with a support (<s>sālambana</s>). 1.17

body.text: athāsaṃprajñātaḥ samādhiḥ kimupāyaḥ kiṃsvabhāvo veti ---

children.translated_text: The other [<s>samādhi</s>], preceded by the practice of the cause of cessation, has only impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) remaining. || YS_1.18 ||

body.translated_text: Now, what is the means and what is the nature of non-cognitive <s>samādhi</s> (<s>asaṃprajñāta</s>)? —

body.text: sarvavṛttipratyastamaye saṃskāraśeṣo nirodhaś cittasya samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ. tasya paraṃ vairāgyam upāyaḥ. sālambano hy abhyāsas tatsādhanāya na kalpata iti virāmapratyayo nirvastuka ālambanīkriyate. sa cārthaśūnyaḥ. tadabhyāsapūrvakaṃ hi cittaṃ nirālambanam abhāvaprāptam iva bhavatīty eṣa nirbījaḥ samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ. 1.18
body.translated_text: When all modifications have subsided, the cessation of the mind in which only impressions remain — that <s>samādhi</s> is non-cognitive (<s>asaṃprajñāta</s>). The supreme dispassion is its means. For practice with a support does not suffice for its accomplishment. Rather, the cessation-cause (<s>virāmapratyaya</s>), which is objectless, is made into its support. And that too is devoid of [real] content. Through the practice of that, the mind, becoming supportless, reaches a state as if of non-existence — this is the seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) <s>samādhi</s>, the non-cognitive. 1.18

body.text: sa khalv ayaṃ dvividhaḥ --- upāyapratyayo bhavapratyayaś ca. tatropāyapratyayo yogināṃ bhavati ---

children.translated_text: That caused by [residual] existence belongs to the bodiless (<s>videha</s>) and those absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s>. || YS_1.19 ||

body.translated_text: Now, this [non-cognitive samādhi] is of two kinds: caused by means (<s>upāyapratyaya</s>) and caused by [residual] existence (<s>bhavapratyaya</s>). Of these, that caused by means belongs to <s>yogins</s> —

body.text: videhānāṃ devānāṃ bhavapratyayaḥ. te hi svasaṃskāramātropayogena cittena kaivalyapadam ivānubhavantaḥ svasaṃskāravipākaṃ tathājātīyakam ativāhayanti. tathā prakṛtilayāḥ sādhikāre cetasi prakṛtilīne kaivalyapadam ivānubhavanti, yāvan na punar āvartate 'dhikāravaśāc cittam iti. 1.19
body.translated_text: The <s>bhavapratyaya</s> [samādhi] belongs to bodiless gods. They, experiencing a state resembling <s>kaivalya</s> through the mind that employs only its own impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), pass through the ripening of those impressions in the corresponding form. Likewise, those absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s> experience a state resembling <s>kaivalya</s> when the mind dissolves into <s>Prakṛti</s> while still retaining its function — until the mind returns again due to the force of [residual] function. 1.19

body.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāpūrvaka itareṣām || YS_1.20 ||
body.translated_text: For others, it is preceded by faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). || YS_1.20 ||

body.text: upāyapratyayo yogināṃ bhavati. śraddhā cetasaḥ saṃprasādaḥ. sā hi jananīva kalyāṇī yoginaṃ pāti. tasya hi śraddadhānasya vivekārthino vīryam upajāyate. samupajātavīryasya smṛtir upatiṣṭhate. smṛtyupasthāne ca cittam anākulaṃ samādhīyate. samāhitacittasya prajñāviveka upāvartate. yena yathārthaṃ vastu jānāti. tadabhyāsāt tattadviṣayāc ca vairāgyād asaṃprajñātaḥ samādhir bhavati. 1.20
body.translated_text: For <s>yogins</s>, [samādhi] is caused by means. Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is the serenity of the mind. Like a benevolent mother, she protects the <s>yogin</s>. For one who has faith and seeks discrimination, energy arises. For one in whom energy has arisen, memory presents itself. When memory is present, the mind becomes undisturbed and is concentrated in <s>samādhi</s>. For one whose mind is concentrated, the discriminative wisdom (<s>prajñāviveka</s>) unfolds, by which one knows things as they really are. Through the practice of that, and through dispassion toward those very objects, the non-cognitive <s>samādhi</s> arises. 1.20

body.text: te khalu nava yogino mṛdumadhyādhimātropāyā bhavanti. tadyathā --- mṛdūpāyo madhyopāyo 'dhimātropāya iti. tatra mṛdūpāyas trividhaḥ --- mṛdusaṃvego madhyasaṃvegas tīvrasaṃvega iti. tathā madhyopāyas tathādhimātropāya iti. tatrādhimātropāyānām ---

children.translated_text: For those of keen intensity, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near. || YS_1.21 ||

body.translated_text: Now, these nine [types of] <s>yogins</s> have mild, moderate, and intense means. Namely: one of mild means, one of moderate means, and one of intense means. Among these, the one of mild means is threefold: of mild intensity, of moderate intensity, and of keen intensity. Likewise the one of moderate means, and the one of intense means. Among those of intense means —

body.text: samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṃ ca bhavatīti. 1.21
body.translated_text: The attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s> are [near]. 1.21

body.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāt tato 'pi viśeṣaḥ || YS_1.22 ||
body.translated_text: There is a further distinction owing to [the degrees being] mild, moderate, and intense. || YS_1.22 ||

body.text: mṛdutīvro madhyatīvro 'dhimātratīvra iti. tato 'pi viśeṣaḥ. tadviśeṣād api mṛdutīvrasaṃvegasyāsannaḥ tato madhyatīvrasaṃvegasyāsannataraḥ, tasmād adhimātratīvrasaṃvegasyādhimātropāyasyāpy āsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṃ ceti. 1.22
body.translated_text: Mildly keen, moderately keen, and intensely keen — hence there is a further distinction. Due to that distinction, for one of mildly keen intensity [samādhi] is near; for one of moderately keen intensity, nearer; and for one of intensely keen intensity with intense means, nearest — both the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s>. 1.22

body.text: kim etasmād evāsannatamaḥ samādhir bhavati. athāsya lābhe bhavaty anyo 'pi kaścid upāyo na veti ---

children.translated_text: Or, [it is attained] through devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). || YS_1.23 ||

body.translated_text: Is it from this alone that <s>samādhi</s> becomes nearest? Or is there some other means for its attainment? —

body.text: praṇidhānād bhaktiviśeṣād āvarjita īśvaras tam anugṛhṇāty abhidhyānamātreṇa. tadabhidhyānamātrād api yogina āsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṃ ca bhavatīti. 1.23
body.translated_text: Through devotion (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), through a special form of devotion (<s>bhaktiviśeṣa</s>), <s>Īśvara</s>, being favorably inclined, blesses that [yogin] through mere contemplation. Through that mere contemplation alone, the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s> become nearest for the <s>yogin</s>. 1.23

body.text: atha pradhānapuruṣavyatiriktaḥ ko 'yam īśvaro nāmeti ---

children.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>, untouched by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), actions (<s>karma</s>), results (<s>vipāka</s>), and their residual deposits (<s>āśaya</s>). || YS_1.24 ||

body.translated_text: Now, distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is this one called <s>Īśvara</s>? —

body.text:
avidyādayaḥ kleśāḥ. kuśalākuśalāni karmāṇi. tatphalaṃ vipākaḥ. tadanuguṇā vāsanā āśayāḥ. te ca manasi vartamānāḥ puruṣe vyapadiśyante, sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti. yathā jayaḥ parājayo vā yoddhṛṣu vartamānaḥ svāmini vyapadiśyate. yo hy anena bhogenāparāmṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ.
  kaivalyaṃ prāptās tarhi santi ca bahavaḥ kevalinaḥ. te hi trīṇi bandhanāni cchittvā kaivalyaṃ prāptā īśvarasya ca tatsaṃbandho na bhūto na bhāvī. yathā muktasya pūrvā bandhakoṭiḥ prajñāyate naivam īśvarasya. yathā vā prakṛtilīnasyottarā bandhakoṭiḥ saṃbhāvyate naivam īśvarasya. sa tu sadaiva muktaḥ sadaiveśvara iti.
  yo 'sau prakṛṣṭasattvopādānād īśvarasya śāśvatika utkarṣaḥ sa kiṃ sanimitta āhosvin nirnimitta iti. tasya śāstraṃ nimittam.
  śāstraṃ punaḥ kiṃnimittam, prakṛṣṭasattvanimittam.
body.translated_text: The afflictions are ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and the rest. Actions are wholesome and unwholesome. Their result is the ripening (<s>vipāka</s>). The latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) conforming to those are the residual deposits (<s>āśaya</s>). Though these subsist in the mind, they are attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>, for it is he who is the experiencer of their fruits — just as victory or defeat, though occurring among the warriors, is attributed to the king. That <s>Puruṣa</s> who is untouched by this experience is the special <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>. [Objection:] But there are many who have attained <s>kaivalya</s>, many liberated ones. They have cut the three bonds and attained <s>kaivalya</s>. But <s>Īśvara's</s> connection with those [bonds] neither existed [in the past] nor will exist [in the future]. Just as for a liberated soul a prior end of bondage is recognized — it is not so for <s>Īśvara</s>. And just as for one absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s> a later end of bondage is conceivable — it is not so for <s>Īśvara</s>. He is ever free, ever the Lord. Now, is that eternal supremacy of <s>Īśvara</s>, which arises from the excellence of His <s>sattva</s>, with or without a cause? His excellence has the scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) as its cause. And what is the cause of the scripture? The excellence of <s>sattva</s>.

body.text: etayoḥ śāstrotkarṣayor īśvarasattve vartamānayor anādiḥ saṃbandhaḥ. etasmād etad bhavati sadaiveśvaraḥ sadaiva mukta iti. tac ca tasyaiśvaryaṃ sāmyātiśayavinirmuktam. na tāvad aiśvaryāntareṇa tad atiśayyate. yad evātiśayi syāt tad eva tat syāt. tasmād yatra kāṣṭhāprāptir aiśvaryasya sa īśvara iti. na ca tatsamānam aiśvaryam asti. kasmāt, dvayos tulyayor ekasmin yugapatkāmite 'rthe navam idam astu purāṇam idam astv ity ekasya siddhāv itarasya prākāmyavighātād ūnatvaṃ prasaktam. dvayoś ca tulyayor yugapatkāmitārthaprāptir nāsti. arthasya viruddhatvāt. tasmād yasya sāmyātiśayair vinirmuktam aiśvaryaṃ sa eveśvaraḥ. sa ca puruṣaviśeṣa iti. 1.24
body.translated_text: Between this excellence [of sattva] and the scripture, which subsist in the being of <s>Īśvara</s>, there is a beginningless relationship. From this it follows that He is ever the Lord and ever free. And His sovereignty is free from equality and surpassing [by another]. For His sovereignty is not surpassed by any other sovereignty. Whatever would surpass it would itself be that [sovereignty]. Therefore, the one in whom sovereignty reaches its ultimate limit — He is <s>Īśvara</s>. Nor is there any sovereignty equal to His. Why? Because if two equals simultaneously desired a single object — one wishing it to be new, the other wishing it to be old — the accomplishment of one would entail the obstruction of the other's will, resulting in his inferiority. And for two equals, there is no simultaneous attainment of contradictory desired objects, since the object [cannot be both at once]. Therefore, the one whose sovereignty is free from equality and surpassing — He alone is <s>Īśvara</s>. And He is the special <s>Puruṣa</s>. 1.24

body.text: kiṃ ca ---

children.translated_text: In Him, the seed of omniscience is unsurpassed. || YS_1.25 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text:
yad idam atītānāgatapratyutpannapratyekasamuccayātīndriyagrahaṇam alpaṃ bahv iti sarvajñabījam etad vivardhamānaṃ yatra niratiśayaṃ sa sarvajñaḥ. asti kāṣṭhāprāptiḥ sarvajñabījasya sātiśayatvāt parimāṇavad iti. yatra kāṣṭhāprāptir jñānasya sa sarvajñaḥ. sa ca puruṣaviśeṣa iti.
  sāmānyamātropasaṃhāre ca kṛtopakṣayam anumānaṃ na viśeṣapratipattau samartham iti. tasya saṃjñādiviśeṣapratipattir āgamataḥ paryanveṣyā. tasyātmānugrahābhāve 'pi bhūtānugrahaḥ prayojanam. jñānadharmopadeśena kalpapralayamahāpralayeṣu saṃsāriṇaḥ puruṣān uddhariṣyāmīti. tathā coktam --- ādividvān nirmāṇacittam adhiṣṭhāya kāruṇyād bhagavān paramarṣir āsuraye jijñāsamānāya tantraṃ provāceti. 1.25
body.translated_text: This cognition — whether of past, future, or present, whether individual or collective, whether supersensory — whether small or great, is the seed of omniscience. Where this seed, when fully developed, reaches its utmost, that is the omniscient one. There is a culmination point for the seed of omniscience, because it has degrees, like measurement. Where knowledge reaches its culmination, that is the omniscient one. And he is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>. [Now] drawing together the general [discussion] —

body.text: sa eṣaḥ ---

children.translated_text: The teacher even of the ancients, because [He is] not limited by time. [<s>YS</s> 1.26]

body.translated_text: That [<s>Īśvara</s>] is —

body.text: pūrve hi guravaḥ kālenāvacchidyante. yatrāvacchedārthena kālo nopāvartate sa eṣa pūrveṣām api guruḥ. yathāsya sargasyādau prakarṣagatyā siddhas tathātikrāntasargādiṣv api pratyetavyaḥ. 1.26
body.translated_text: The former teachers are limited by time. Where time does not apply for the purpose of limitation — He is the teacher even of the ancients. Just as He is established as accomplished through supreme attainment at the beginning of this creation, so too it should be understood regarding the beginnings of previous creations. [1.26]

body.text: tasya vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ || YS_1.27 ||
body.translated_text: His designator is <s>Praṇava</s> [<s>Oṃ</s>]. [<s>YS</s> 1.27]

body.text:
vācya īśvaraḥ praṇavasya. kim asya saṃketakṛtaṃ vācyavācakatvam atha pradīpaprakāśavad avasthitam iti.
  sthito 'sya vācyasya vācakena saha saṃbandhaḥ. saṃketas tv īśravasya sthitam evārtham abhinayati. yathāvasthitaḥ pitṛputrayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ saṃketenāvadyotyate, ayam asya pitā, ayam asya putra iti. sargāntareṣv api vācyavācakaśaktyapekṣas tathaiva saṃketaḥ kriyate. saṃpratipattinityatayā nityaḥ śabdārthasaṃbandha ity āgaminaḥ pratijānate. 1.27
body.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> is the designated [meaning] of <s>Praṇava</s>. Is the relation of designated and designator between them a matter of convention, or is it established [inherently] like a lamp and its light? The relation between this designated [meaning] and the designator is established [inherently]. Convention merely indicates the already-established meaning of <s>Īśvara</s>. Just as the relation between father and son is established [inherently], and convention merely makes it known — 'this is his father, this is his son.'

body.text: vijñātavācyavācakatvasya yoginaḥ ---

children.translated_text: Its repetition and contemplation of its meaning. [<s>YS</s> 1.28]

body.translated_text: For the yogin who has understood [this] relation of designated and designator —

children.text: praṇavasya japaḥ praṇavābhidheyasya ceśvarasya bhāvanam. tad asya yoginaḥ praṇavaṃ japataḥ praṇavārthaṃ ca bhāvayataś cittam ekāgraṃ saṃpadyate. tathā coktam ---
children.translated_text: The repetition (<s>japa</s>) of <s>Praṇava</s> and the contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of <s>Īśvara</s>, who is denoted by <s>Praṇava</s>. For this yogin who repeats <s>Praṇava</s> and contemplates the meaning of <s>Praṇava</s>, the mind becomes one-pointed. And thus it has been said —
'From self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) one should attain yoga; from yoga one should pursue self-study.
Through the perfection of self-study and yoga, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) is revealed.' [1.28]

body.text: kiṃ cāsya bhavati ---

children.translated_text: From that, the attainment of inward consciousness and also the absence of obstacles. [<s>YS</s> 1.29]

body.translated_text: Moreover, what results for this [yogin] —

body.text: ye tāvad antarāyā vyādhiprabhṛtayas te tāvad īśvarapraṇidhānān na bhavanti. svarūpadarśanam apy asya bhavati. yathaiveśvaraḥ puruṣaḥ śuddhaḥ prasannaḥ kevalo 'nupasargas tathāyam api buddheḥ pratisaṃvedī yaḥ puruṣas tam adhigacchati. 1.29
body.translated_text: The obstacles beginning with disease — those do not arise through devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (<s>īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>). The vision of one's own true nature also arises for this [yogin]. Just as <s>Īśvara</s> is a <s>Puruṣa</s> who is pure, serene, absolute, and unafflicted, so too this [yogin] attains that <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the experiencer of <s>buddhi</s>. [1.29]

body.text: atha ke 'ntarāyā ye cittasya vikṣepāḥ. ke punas te kiyanto veti ---

children.translated_text: Disease, dullness, doubt, negligence, laziness, non-abstention, erroneous perception, non-attainment of a [meditative] stage, and instability — these are the distractions of the mind; they are the obstacles. [<s>YS</s> 1.30]

children.text: navāntarāyāś cittasya vikṣepāḥ. sahaite cittavṛttibhir bhavanti. eteṣām abhāve na bhavanti pūrvoktāś cittavṛttayaḥ. vyādhir dhāturasakaraṇavaiṣamyam. styānam akarmaṇyatā cittasya. saṃśaya ubhayakoṭispṛg vijñānaṃ syād idam evaṃ naivaṃ syād iti. pramādaḥ samādhisādhanānām abhāvanam. ālasyaṃ kāyasya cittasya ca gurutvād apravṛttiḥ. aviratiś cittasya viṣayasaṃprayogātmā gardhaḥ. bhrāntidarśanaṃ viparyayajñānam. alabdhabhūmikatvaṃ samādhibhūmer alābhaḥ. anavasthitatvaṃ yal labdhāyāṃ bhūmau cittasyāpratiṣṭhā. samādhipratilambhe hi sati tadavasthitaṃ syād iti. ete cittavikṣepā nava yogamalā yogapratipakṣā yogāntarāyā ity abhidhīyante. 1.30
children.translated_text: There are nine obstacles, which are distractions of the mind. These exist together with the mental fluctuations (<s>cittavṛtti</s>). In the absence of these, the previously mentioned mental fluctuations do not occur. Disease (<s>vyādhi</s>) is the imbalance of the bodily constituents (<s>dhātu</s>), fluids (<s>rasa</s>), and organs (<s>karaṇa</s>). Dullness (<s>styāna</s>) is the incapacity for action of the mind. Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) is cognition touching both alternatives — 'Could it be thus, or not thus?' Negligence (<s>pramāda</s>) is the non-cultivation of the means to <s>samādhi</s>. Laziness (<s>ālasya</s>) is [the inertia] of body and mind.

body.translated_text: Now, what are the obstacles that are the distractions of the mind? And how many are they?

body.text: duḥkhadaurmanasyāṅgamejayatvaśvāsapraśvāsā vikṣepasahabhuvaḥ || YS_1.31 ||
body.translated_text: Pain, dejection, trembling of the body, and [disturbed] inhalation and exhalation are the accompaniments of distraction. [<s>YS</s> 1.31]

body.text: duḥkham ādhyātmikam ādhibhautikam ādhidaivikaṃ ca. yenābhihatāḥ prāṇinas tadapaghātāya prayatante tad duḥkham. daurmanasyam icchāvighātāc cetasaḥ kṣobhaḥ. yad aṅgāny ejayati kampayati tad aṅgamejayatvam. prāṇo yad bāhyaṃ vāyum ācāmati sa śvāsaḥ. yat kauṣṭhyaṃ vāyuṃ niḥsārayati sa praśvāsaḥ. ete vikṣepasahabhuvo vikṣiptacittasyaite bhavanti. samāhitacittasyaite na bhavanti. 1.31
body.translated_text: Pain (<s>duḥkha</s>) is of three kinds: arising from oneself (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), from beings (<s>ādhibhautika</s>), and from divine [causes] (<s>ādhidaivika</s>). That which strikes living beings, who then strive to remove it — that is pain. Dejection (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is the agitation of the mind from the frustration of desire. That which causes the limbs to shake and tremble — that is trembling of the body (<s>aṅgamejayatva</s>). The inhalation (<s>śvāsa</s>) is when one draws in the external air through the nostrils. The exhalation (<s>praśvāsa</s>) is when one expels the internal air. These are the accompaniments of distraction.

body.text: athaite vikṣepāḥ samādhipratipakṣās tābhyām evābhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ niroddhavyāḥ. tatrābhyāsasya viṣayam upasaṃharann idam āha ---

children.translated_text: For the prevention of these, the practice of [concentration on] a single reality. [<s>YS</s> 1.32]

body.translated_text: Now, these distractions, which are opposed to <s>samādhi</s>, should be restrained by those very two — practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). Herein, presenting the object of practice, he says —

body.text:
vikṣepapratiṣedhārtham ekatattvāvalambanaṃ cittam abhyaset. yasya tu pratyarthaniyataṃ pratyayamātraṃ kṣaṇikaṃ ca cittaṃ tasya sarvam eva cittam ekāgraṃ nāsty eva vikṣiptam. yadi punar idaṃ sarvataḥ pratyāhṛtyaikasminn arthe samādhīyate tadā bhavaty ekāgram ity ato na pratyarthaniyatam.
  yo 'pi sadṛśapratyayapravāhena cittam ekāgraṃ manyate tasyaikāgratā yadi pravāhacittasya dharmas tadaikaṃ nāsti pravāhacittaṃ kṣaṇikatvāt. atha pravāhāṃśasyaiva pratyayasya dharmaḥ, sa sarvaḥ sadṛśapratyayapravāhī vā visadṛśapratyayapravāhī vā pratyarthaniyatatvād ekāgra eveti vikṣiptacittānupapattiḥ. tasmād ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ cittam iti.
  yadi ca cittenaikenānanvitāḥ svabhāvabhinnāḥ pratyayā jāyerann atha katham anyapratyayadṛṣṭasyānyaḥ smartā bhavet. anyapratyayopacitasya ca karmāśayasyānyaḥ pratyaya upabhoktā bhavet. kathaṃcit samādhīyamānam apy etad gomayapāyasīyanyāyam ākṣipati.
  kiṃ ca svātmānubhavāpahnavaś cittasyānyatve prāpnoti. katham, yad aham adrākṣaṃ tat spṛśāmi yac cāsprākṣaṃ tat paśyāmīty aham iti pratyayaḥ sarvasya pratyayasya bhede sati pratyayiny abhedenopasthitaḥ. ekapratyayaviṣayo 'yam abhedātmāham iti pratyayaḥ katham atyantabhinneṣu citteṣu vartamānaḥ sāmānyam ekaṃ pratyayinam āśrayet. svānubhavagrāhyaś cāyam abhedātmāham iti pratyayaḥ. na ca pratyakṣasya māhātmyaṃ pramāṇāntareṇābhibhūyate. pramāṇāntaraṃ ca pratyakṣabalenaiva vyavahāraṃ labhate. tasmād ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ ca cittam. 1.32
body.translated_text: For the prevention of distractions, the mind should be practiced in relying upon a single reality (<s>ekatattvāvalambana</s>). For one whose mind has a cognition that is determined by each individual object and is momentary, all of that mind is indeed one-pointed — there is no distraction at all. But if this [mind] is withdrawn from everything and concentrated upon a single object, then it becomes one-pointed — therefore it is not determined by each individual object. And one who —

body.text: yasya cittasyāvasthitasyedaṃ śāstreṇa parikarma nirdiśyate tat katham ---

children.translated_text: The purification of the mind [comes] through the cultivation of friendliness, compassion, joy, and equanimity toward [those experiencing] happiness, suffering, merit, and demerit [respectively]. [<s>YS</s> 1.33]

children.text: tatra sarvaprāṇiṣu sukhasaṃbhogāpanneṣu maitrīṃ bhāvayet. duḥkhiteṣu karuṇām. puṇyātmakeṣu muditām. apuṇyaśīleṣūpekṣām. evam asya bhāvayataḥ śuklo dharma upajāyate. tataś ca cittaṃ prasīdati. prasannam ekāgraṃ sthitipadaṃ labhate. 1.33
children.translated_text: Therein, toward all beings who have attained the enjoyment of happiness, one should cultivate friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>). Toward those in suffering, compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). Toward those of meritorious nature, joy (<s>muditā</s>). Toward those of demeritorious conduct, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). For one who cultivates thus, pure <s>dharma</s> arises. And from that, the mind becomes serene. The serene [mind], one-pointed, attains the ground of stability. [1.33]

body.translated_text: How is this discipline prescribed by the <s>śāstra</s> for the mind that has become steady?

body.text: pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṃ vā prāṇasya || YS_1.34 ||
body.translated_text: Or, by exhalation and retention of breath (<s>prāṇa</s>). [<s>YS</s> 1.34]

body.text: kauṣṭhyasya vāyor nāsikāpuṭābhyāṃ prayatnaviśeṣād vamanaṃ pracchardanam, vidhāraṇaṃ prāṇāyāmas tābhyāṃ vā manasaḥ sthitiṃ saṃpādayet. 1.34
body.translated_text: The expulsion of the internal air through the nostrils with special effort is exhalation (<s>pracchardana</s>); retention is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. By these two, one may bring about the stability of the mind. [1.34]

body.text: viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanī || YS_1.35 ||
body.translated_text: Or, a sensory activity, having arisen, causes the stability of the mind. [<s>YS</s> 1.35]

body.text: nāsikāgre dhārayato 'sya yā divyagandhasaṃvit sā gandhapravṛttiḥ. jihvāgre rasasaṃvit. tāluni rūpasaṃvit. jihvāmadhye sparśasaṃvit. jihvāmūle śabdasaṃvid ity etā vṛttaya utpannāś cittaṃ sthitau nibadhnanti, saṃśayaṃ vidhamanti, samādhiprajñāyāṃ ca dvārībhavantīti. etena candrādityagrahamaṇipradīparaśmyādiṣu pravṛttir utpannā viṣayavaty eva veditavyā yady api hi tattacchāstrānumānācāryopadeśair avagatam arthatattvaṃ sadbhūtam eva bhavati. eteṣāṃ yathābhūtārthapratipādanasāmarthyāt, tathāpi yāvad ekadeśo 'pi kaścin na svakaraṇasaṃvedyo bhavati tāvat sarvaṃ parokṣam ivāpavargādiṣu sūkṣmeṣv artheṣu na dṛḍhāṃ buddhim utpādayati. tasmāc chāstrānumānācāryopadeśopodbalanārtham evāvaśyaṃ kaścid arthaviśeṣaḥ pratyakṣīkartavyaḥ. tatra tadupadiṣṭārthaikadeśapratyakṣatve sati sarvaṃ sūkṣmaviṣayam api āpavargāc chraddhīyate. etadartham evedaṃ cittaparikarma nirdiśyate. aniyatāsu vṛttiṣu tadviṣayāyāṃ vaśīkārasaṃjñāyām upajātāyāṃ samarthaṃ syāt tasya tasyārthasya pratyakṣīkaraṇāyeti. tathā ca sati śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhayo 'syāpratibandhena bhaviṣyantīti. 1.35
body.translated_text: When concentrating on the tip of the nose, one's perception of divine scent — that is the activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) regarding smell. At the tip of the tongue, the perception of taste. At the palate, the perception of form. At the middle of the tongue, the perception of touch. At the root of the tongue, the perception of sound. These activities, when arisen, bind the mind in stability, dispel doubt, and become gateways to the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>. By this, the activity arisen regarding the moon, sun, planets, gems, lamplight, and other such [objects] should be understood as pertaining to [sense] objects. Although the truth of things ascertained through the respective scriptures, inference, and the instruction of teachers is indeed real — by virtue of their capacity to convey things as they truly are — nevertheless, as long as even one particular aspect has not been perceived by one's own faculties, everything remains as if indirect and does not produce firm conviction regarding subtle matters such as liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) and the like. Therefore, to reinforce [what is known through] scripture, inference, and the instruction of teachers, some particular object must necessarily be directly perceived. When even one aspect of what is taught therein becomes directly perceptible, then everything, even regarding subtle objects, is trusted, up to [and including] liberation. For this very purpose, this discipline of the mind is taught. When, among the uncontrolled activities, the mastery (<s>vaśīkāra</s>) pertaining to that [specific] object arises, [the mind] becomes capable of directly perceiving each and every object. And when this is so, faith, vigor, memory, and <s>samādhi</s> will arise for him without obstruction. 1.35

body.text: viśokā vā jyotiṣmatī || YS_1.36 ||
body.translated_text: Or [the mind attains stability through] the luminous [perception] that is free from sorrow. || <s>YS</s> 1.36 ||

body.text: pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthitinibandhanīty anuvartate. hṛdayapuṇḍarīke dhārayato yā buddhisaṃvit, buddhisattvaṃ hi bhāsvaram ākāśakalpaṃ, tatra sthitivaiśāradyāt pravṛttiḥ sūryendugrahamaṇiprabhārūpākāreṇa vikalpate. tathāsmitāyāṃ samāpannaṃ cittaṃ nistaraṅgamahodadhikalpaṃ śāntam anantam asmitāmātraṃ bhavati. yatredam uktam --- "tam aṇumātram ātmānam anuvidyāsmīty evaṃ tāvat saṃprajānīte" iti. eṣā dvayī viśokā viṣayavatī, asmitāmātrā ca pravṛttir jyotiṣmatīty ucyate. yayā yoginaś cittaṃ sthitipadaṃ labhata iti. 1.36
body.translated_text: 'The activity, when arisen, binds the mind in stability' — this continues [from the previous sūtra]. When concentrating on the lotus of the heart, there arises the perception of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). The essence of <s>buddhi</s> is luminous and resembles space. Through the steadiness attained there, the activity manifests in the form of the radiance of the sun, moon, planets, and gems. Similarly, when the mind has entered into [the meditation on] pure 'I-am-ness' (<s>asmitā</s>), it becomes calm, infinite, and consisting of mere 'I-am-ness,' like a great ocean without waves. As it is said: 'Having found that atomic self, one first knows "I am" thus.' This twofold [activity] — the one pertaining to objects and the one consisting of mere 'I-am-ness' — free from sorrow, is called 'luminous' (<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>), by which the mind of the <s>yogin</s> attains the state of stability. 1.36

body.text: vītarāgaviṣayaṃ vā cittam || YS_1.37 ||
body.translated_text: Or [the mind attains stability when] directed upon a consciousness free from attachment. || <s>YS</s> 1.37 ||

body.text: vītarāgacittālambanoparaktaṃ vā yoginaś cittaṃ sthitipadaṃ labhata iti. 1.37
body.translated_text: Or the mind of the <s>yogin</s>, colored by taking as its support the consciousness of one free from attachment (<s>vītarāga</s>), attains the state of stability. 1.37

body.text: svapnanidrājñānālambanaṃ vā || YS_1.38 ||
body.translated_text: Or [the mind attains stability when] supported by the knowledge [arising in] dream or sleep. || <s>YS</s> 1.38 ||

body.text: svapnajñānālambanaṃ vā nidrājñānālambanaṃ vā tadākāraṃ yoginaś cittaṃ sthitipadaṃ labhata iti. 1.38
body.translated_text: Or, taking the knowledge arising in dream as its support, or the knowledge of [deep] sleep as its support, the mind of the <s>yogin</s>, assuming that form, attains the state of stability. 1.38

body.text: yathābhimatadhyānād vā || YS_1.39 ||
body.translated_text: Or through meditation on whatever is agreeable. || <s>YS</s> 1.39 ||

body.text: yad evābhimataṃ tad eva dhyāyet. tatra labdhasthitikam anyatrāpi sthitipadaṃ labhata iti. 1.39
body.translated_text: One should meditate on whatever is agreeable to oneself. Having gained stability therein, [the mind] attains the state of stability elsewhere as well. 1.39

body.text: paramāṇuparamamahattvānto 'sya vaśīkāraḥ || YS_1.40 ||
body.translated_text: His mastery extends from the most minute atom to the infinitely great. || <s>YS</s> 1.40 ||

body.text: sūkṣme niviśamānasya paramāṇvantaṃ sthitipadaṃ labhata iti. sthūle niviśamānasya paramamahattvāntaṃ sthitipadaṃ cittasya. evaṃ tām ubhayīṃ koṭim anudhāvato yo 'syāpratīghātaḥ sa paro vaśīkāraḥ. tadvaśīkārāt paripūrṇaṃ yoginaś cittaṃ na punar abhyāsakṛtaṃ parikarmāpekṣata iti. 1.40
body.translated_text: When the mind enters into the subtle, it attains the state of stability extending down to the ultimate atom. When the mind enters into the gross, the stability of mind [extends] up to the infinitely great. Thus, when it pursues both extremes, its unobstructedness — that is the supreme mastery (<s>vaśīkāra</s>). Through that mastery, the mind of the <s>yogin</s> is complete and no longer requires the preparatory work of practice. 1.40

body.text: atha labdhasthitikasya cetasaḥ kiṃsvarūpā kiṃviṣayā vā samāpattir iti, tad ucyate ---

children.text: kṣīṇavṛtter abhijātasyeva maṇer grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā samāpattiḥ || YS_1.41 ||
children.translated_text: When the fluctuations have dwindled, [the mind], like a precious gem, has the quality of taking on the color of whatever it rests upon — whether the knower, the instrument of knowing, or the knowable. This is <s>samāpatti</s> (cognitive absorption). || <s>YS</s> 1.41 ||

children.text:
kṣīṇavṛtter iti pratyastamitapratyayasyety arthaḥ. abhijātasyeva maṇer iti dṛṣṭāntopādānam. yathā sphaṭika upāśrayabhedāt tattadrūpoparakta upāśrayarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate tathā grāhyālambanoparaktaṃ cittaṃ grāhyasamāpannaṃ grāhyasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate. bhūtasūkṣmoparaktaṃ bhūtasūkṣmasamāpannaṃ bhūtasūkṣmasvarūpābhāsaṃ bhavati. tathā sthūlālambanoparaktaṃ sthūlarūpasamāpannaṃ sthūlarūpābhāsaṃ bhavati. tathā viśvabhedoparaktaṃ viśvabhedasamāpannaṃ viśvarūpābhāsaṃ bhavati.
  tathā grahaṇeṣv apīndriyeṣv api draṣṭavyam. grahaṇālambanoparaktaṃ grahaṇasamāpannaṃ grahaṇasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate. tathā grahītṛpuruṣālambanoparaktaṃ grahītṛpuruṣasamāpannaṃ grahītṛpuruṣasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate. tathā muktapuruṣālambanoparaktaṃ muktapuruṣasamāpannaṃ muktapuruṣasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsata iti. tad evam abhijātamaṇikalpasya cetaso grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu puruṣendriyabhūteṣu yā tatsthatadañjanatā teṣu sthitasya tadākārāpattiḥ sā samāpattir ity ucyate. 1.41
children.translated_text: 'When the fluctuations have dwindled' means when mental modifications have subsided. 'Like a precious gem' is the use of an illustration. Just as a crystal, according to the different supports [placed near it], is colored by the form of each support and shines forth in the form of that support — so the mind, colored by taking the knowable as its object, having entered into the knowable, shines forth in the form of the knowable. Colored by the subtle elements, having entered into the subtle elements, it becomes a reflection of the form of the subtle elements. Similarly, colored by a gross object, having entered into the gross, it becomes a reflection of the gross form. Likewise, colored by the universal distinctions, having entered into the universal distinctions, it becomes a reflection of the universal form. Similarly, it should be seen regarding the instruments of knowing — the senses as well. Colored by taking the senses as its object, having entered into the senses, it shines forth in the form of the senses. Likewise, colored by taking the knowing <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) as its object, having entered into the knowing <s>Puruṣa</s>, it shines forth in the form of the knowing <s>Puruṣa</s>. Likewise, colored by taking the liberated <s>Puruṣa</s> as its object, having entered into the liberated <s>Puruṣa</s>, it shines forth in the form of the liberated <s>Puruṣa</s>. Thus, the mind — like a well-polished gem — in respect of the knower, the instrument of knowing, and the knowable, that is, <s>Puruṣa</s>, the senses, and the elements, has the quality of resting upon and taking on the color of these: it is called <s>samāpatti</s> — the assuming of the form of these while abiding in them. 1.41

body.translated_text: Now, what is the nature and what is the object of the cognitive absorption (<s>samāpatti</s>) of a mind that has attained stability? This is explained:

body.text: tatra śabdārthajñānavikalpaiḥ saṃkīrṇā savitarkā samāpattiḥ || YS_1.42 ||
body.translated_text: Among these, the cognitive absorption mixed with the conceptual distinctions of word, meaning, and knowledge is <s>savitarkā samāpatti</s> (absorption with deliberation). || <s>YS</s> 1.42 ||

body.text: tadyathā gaur iti śabdo gaur ity artho gaur iti jñānam ity avibhāgena vibhaktānām api grahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam. vibhajyamānāś cānye śabdadharmā anye 'rthadharmā anye vijñānadharmā ity eteṣāṃ vibhaktaḥ panthāḥ. tatra samāpannasya yogino yo gavādyarthaḥ samādhiprajñāyāṃ samārūḍhaḥ sa cec chabdārthajñānavikalpānuviddha upāvartate sā saṃkīrṇā samāpattiḥ savitarkety ucyate. 1.42
body.translated_text: For example: 'cow' as a word, 'cow' as an object, 'cow' as a cognition — though these are distinct, their apprehension is seen to be undifferentiated. But when analyzed: the properties of the word are different, the properties of the object are different, and the properties of the cognition are different — their paths are separate. Among these, when for the absorbed <s>yogin</s> an object such as a cow has arisen in the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>, if it returns pervaded by the conceptual distinctions of word, meaning, and knowledge — that mixed absorption is called <s>savitarkā</s> (with deliberation). 1.42

body.text: yadā punaḥ śabdasaṃketasmṛtipariśuddhau śrutānumānajñānavikalpaśūnyāyāṃ samādhiprajñāyāṃ svarūpamātreṇāvasthito 'rthas tatsvarūpākāramātratayaivāvacchidyate. sā ca nirvitarkā samāpattiḥ. tat paraṃ pratyakṣam. tac ca śrutānumānayor bījam. tataḥ śrutānumāne prabhavataḥ. na ca śrutānumānajñānasahabhūtaṃ tad darśanam. tasmād asaṃkīrṇaṃ praṃmāṇāntareṇa yogino nirvitarkasamādhijaṃ darśanam iti. nirvitarkāyāḥ samāpatter asyāḥ sūtreṇa lakṣaṇaṃ dyotyate ---

children.translated_text: When memory is purified, [the mind], as if empty of its own form, shining forth as the object alone — that is <s>nirvitarkā</s> (without deliberation). || <s>YS</s> 1.43 ||

body.translated_text: But when, in the purification of memory from verbal conventions, the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s> is empty of the conceptual distinctions of knowledge [derived from] scripture and inference, and the object abides merely in its own essential form — [the mind] is delimited only by the form of that essential nature. That is <s>nirvitarkā samāpatti</s> (absorption without deliberation). That is the supreme direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). And that is the seed of scriptural [knowledge] and inference. From it, scripture and inference arise. But that vision is not co-existent with knowledge born of scripture and inference. Therefore, the vision born of the <s>yogin</s>'s <s>nirvitarka samādhi</s> is unmixed with any other means of knowledge. The characteristic of this <s>nirvitarkā samāpatti</s> is indicated by the [following] <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text:
yā śabdasaṃketaśrutānumānajñānavikalpasmṛtipariśuddhau grāhyasvarūpa.uparaktā prajñā svam iva prajñāsvarūpaṃ grahaṇātmakaṃ tyaktvā padārthamātrasvarūpā grāhyasvarūpāpanneva bhavati sā tadā nirvitarkā samāpattiḥ.
  tathā ca vyākyātaṃ tasyā ekabuddhyupakramo hy arthātmāṇupracayaviśeṣātmā gavādir ghaṭādir vā lokaḥ.
  sa ca saṃsthānaviśeṣo bhūtasūkṣmāṇāṃ sādhāraṇo dharma ātmabhūtaḥ phalena vyaktenānumitaḥ svavyañjakāñjanaḥ prādurbhavati. dharmāntarasya kapālāder udaye ca tirobhavati. sa eṣa dharmo 'vayavīty ucyate. yo 'sāv ekaś ca mahāṃś cāṇīṃyaś ca sparśavāṃś ca kriyādharmakaś cānityaś ca tenāvayavinā vyavahārāḥ kriyante.
  yasya punar avastukaḥ sa pracayaviśeṣaḥ. sūkṣmaṃ ca kāraṇam anupalabhyam avikalpasya tasyāvayavyabhāvād atadrūpapratiṣṭhaṃ mithyājñānam iti prāyeṇa sarvam eva prāptaṃ mithyājñānam iti. tadā ca samyagjñānam api kiṃ syād viṣayābhāvāt. yad yad upalabhyate tat tad avayavitvenāmnātam. tasmād asty avayavī yo mahattvādivyavahārāpannaḥ samāpatter nirvitarkāyā viṣayī bhavati. 1.43
body.translated_text: When, in the purification of memory from the conceptual distinctions of verbal conventions and knowledge [from] scripture and inference, the wisdom colored by the form of the knowable — abandoning, as it were, its own form as wisdom (which is essentially the act of grasping) — becomes as if it has assumed the very form of the object alone, the essential form of the knowable: that is then <s>nirvitarkā samāpatti</s>. And it has been explained thus: the world — such as a cow, a pot, and the like — whose essential nature is a particular configuration of atoms, is the starting point of a single cognition. That particular configuration, being the common property and essential nature of the subtle elements, inferred through its manifest effect, manifests tinged by its own indicators. And upon the arising of other properties, such as a potsherd, it disappears. This property is called the composite whole (<s>avayavin</s>). That which is one, great, minute, tangible, possessing the property of action, and impermanent — through such a composite whole, transactions are carried out. But for one who [holds that] this particular configuration is unreal — and the subtle cause is unperceivable — since, for the one free of conceptualization, there is no composite whole, [the conclusion is that] all cognition whose basis is not of that [true] nature is predominantly false knowledge. But then, would right knowledge also be impossible, due to the absence of objects? Whatever is perceived is designated as a composite whole. Therefore the composite whole exists — that which enters into transactions such as 'greatness' and the like becomes the object of <s>nirvitarkā samāpatti</s>. 1.43

body.text: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā || YS_1.44 ||
body.translated_text: By this [explanation], the <s>savicārā</s> (with reflection) and <s>nirvicārā</s> (without reflection) [absorptions], whose object is the subtle, are [also] explained. || <s>YS</s> 1.44 ||

body.text:
tatra bhūtasūkṣmakeṣv abhivyaktadharmakeṣu deśakālanimittānubhavāvacchinneṣu yā samāpattiḥ sā savicārety ucyate. tatrāpy ekabuddhinirgrāhyam evoditadharmaviśiṣṭaṃ bhūtasūkṣmam ālambanībhūtaṃ samādhiprajñāyām upatiṣṭhate.
  yā punaḥ sarvathā sarvataḥ śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānavacchinneṣu sarvadharmānupātiṣu sarvadharmātmakeṣu samāpattiḥ sā nirvicārety ucyate. evaṃsvarūpaṃ hi tadbhūtasūkṣmam etenaiva svarūpeṇālambanībhūtam eva samādhiprajñāsvarūpam uparañjayati.
  prajñā ca svarūpaśūnyevārthamātrā yadā bhavati tadā nirvicārety ucyate. tatra mahadvastuviṣayā savitarkā nirvitarkā ca, sūkṣmavastuviṣayā savicārā nirvicārā ca. evam ubhayor etayaiva nirvitarkayā vikalpahānir vyākhyāteti. 1.44
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>samāpatti</s> (absorption) upon subtle elements (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>) whose properties are manifest, delimited by space, time, cause, and experience, is called <s>savicāra</s> (with reflection). In that state too, the subtle element, characterized by properties that have arisen, graspable by a single cognition, presents itself as the object in the wisdom born of <s>samādhi</s>. But the <s>samāpatti</s> upon those [subtle elements] whose properties — quiescent, arisen, and indeterminate — are undelimited in every way and from every perspective, which follow all <s>dharmas</s> and whose nature is all <s>dharmas</s>, is called <s>nirvicāra</s> (without reflection). For the subtle element of such nature, in that very form as object, colors the nature of the wisdom born of <s>samādhi</s>. And when the wisdom becomes as if empty of its own form, being merely the object, then it is called <s>nirvicāra</s>. Among these, <s>savitarka</s> and <s>nirvitarka</s> have a gross object as their domain; <s>savicāra</s> and <s>nirvicāra</s> have a subtle object. Thus, the abandonment of conceptual construction in both is explained by this <s>nirvitarka</s> itself. (1.44)

body.text: sūkṣmaviṣayatvaṃ cāliṅgaparyavasānam || YS_1.45 ||
body.translated_text: And the range of the subtle object extends up to the unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>). (YS 1.45)

body.text: pārthivasyāṇor gandhatanmātraṃ sūkṣmo viṣayaḥ. āpyasya rasatanmātram. taijasasya rūpatanmātram. vāyavīyasya sparśatanmātram. ākāśasya śabdatanmātram iti. teṣām ahaṃkāraḥ. asyāpi liṅgamātraṃ sūkṣmo viṣayaḥ. liṅgamātrasyāpy aliṅgaṃ sūkṣmo viṣayaḥ. na cāliṅgāt paraṃ sūkṣmam asti. nanv asti puruṣaḥ sūkṣma iti satyam. yathā liṅgāt param aliṅgasya saukṣmyaṃ na caivaṃ puruṣasya. kiṃtu, liṅgasyānvayikāraṇaṃ puruṣo na bhavati, hetus tu bhavatīti. ataḥ pradhāne saukṣmyaṃ niratiśayaṃ vyākhyātam. 1.45
body.translated_text: The subtle object of the earth-atom is the <s>tanmātra</s> of smell; of the water-atom, the <s>tanmātra</s> of taste; of the fire-atom, the <s>tanmātra</s> of form; of the air-atom, the <s>tanmātra</s> of touch; of space, the <s>tanmātra</s> of sound. Of these, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle) [is the subtle object]. And of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>liṅgamātra</s> (the sheer manifest principle) is the subtle object. And of <s>liṅgamātra</s>, <s>aliṅga</s> (the unmanifest) is the subtle object. And there is nothing subtler than <s>aliṅga</s>. But is not <s>Puruṣa</s> subtle? True, but just as <s>aliṅga</s> is subtler than <s>liṅga</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s> is not so [in the same way]. Rather, <s>Puruṣa</s> is not the material cause of <s>liṅga</s>, but is its purpose. Therefore, the unsurpassed subtlety is declared to reside in <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). (1.45)

body.text: tā eva sabījaḥ samādhiḥ || YS_1.46 ||
body.translated_text: These very [four types of absorption] constitute <s>samādhi</s> with seed (<s>sabīja</s>). (YS 1.46)

body.text: tāś catasraḥ samāpattayo bahirvastubījā iti samādhir api sabījaḥ. tatra sthūle 'rthe savitarko nirvitarkaḥ, sūkṣme 'rthe savicāro nirvicāra iti caturdhopasaṃkhyātaḥ samādhir iti. 1.46
body.translated_text: These four <s>samāpattis</s>, having an external object as their seed, constitute <s>samādhi</s> with seed. In this regard, the <s>samādhi</s> is reckoned as fourfold: <s>savitarka</s> and <s>nirvitarka</s> regarding a gross object, and <s>savicāra</s> and <s>nirvicāra</s> regarding a subtle object. (1.46)

body.text: nirvicāravaiśāradye 'dhyātmaprasādaḥ || YS_1.47 ||
body.translated_text: Upon the proficiency in <s>nirvicāra</s>, there arises inner clarity (<s>adhyātmaprasāda</s>). (YS 1.47)

body.text: aśuddhyāvaraṇamalāpetasya prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya rajastamobhyām anabhibhūtaḥ svacchaḥ sthitipravāho vaiśāradyam. yadā nirvicārasya samādher vaiśāradyam idaṃ jāyate tadā yogino bhavaty adhyātmaprasādo bhūtārthaviṣayaḥ kramānanurodhī sphuṭaḥ prajñālokaḥ. tathā coktam --- "prajñāprasādam āruhya aśocyaḥ śocato janān / bhūmiṣṭhān iva śailasthaḥ sarvān prājño 'nupaśyati". 1.47
body.translated_text: When the <s>sattva</s> of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), whose nature is illumination, is freed from the impurity, covering, and stain of <s>aśuddhi</s>, and is not overwhelmed by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — the pure and steady flow is proficiency (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). When this proficiency of the <s>nirvicāra samādhi</s> arises, then there comes to the <s>yogin</s> inner clarity — a luminous insight (<s>prajñāloka</s>) whose object is reality, which does not follow sequence, and which is distinct. As it has been said: 'Having ascended the tower of wisdom, free from sorrow, the wise one looks down upon all sorrowing people, as one standing on a mountain looks upon those standing on the ground.' (1.47)

body.text: ṛtaṃbharā tatra prajñā || YS_1.48 ||
body.translated_text: The wisdom that arises there is truth-bearing (<s>ṛtaṃbharā</s>). (YS 1.48)

body.text:
tasmin samāhitacittasya yā prajñā jāyate tasyā ṛtaṃbhareti saṃjñā bhavati. anvarthā ca sā, satyam eva bibharti na ca tatra viparyāsajñānagandho 'py astīti. tathā coktam ---
  "āgamenānumānena dhyānābhyāsarasena ca /
  tridhā prakalpayan prajñāṃ labhate yogam uttamam" iti. 1.48
body.translated_text: The wisdom that arises in one whose mind is concentrated — its designation is '<s>ṛtaṃbharā</s>' (truth-bearing). And it is aptly named, for it bears only truth, and there is not even a trace of erroneous knowledge in it. As it has been said: 'By scripture, by inference, and by the delight of the practice of meditation — developing wisdom in these three ways, one attains the highest <s>yoga</s>.' (1.48)

body.text: sā punaḥ ---

children.translated_text: has a different object from the wisdoms born of scripture and inference, because its object is the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>). (YS 1.49)

body.translated_text: Moreover, that [wisdom] —

body.text:
śrutam āgamavijñānaṃ tat sāmānyaviṣayam. na hy āgamena śakyo viśeṣo 'bhidhātum, kasmāt, na hi viśeṣeṇa kṛtasaṃketaḥ śabda iti. tathānumānaṃ sāmānyaviṣayam eva. yatra prāptis tatra gatir yatrāprāptis tatra na bhavati gatir ity uktam. anumānena ca sāmānyenopasaṃhāraḥ. tasmāc chrutānumānaviṣayo na viśeṣaḥ kaścid astīti.
  na cāsya sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭasya vastuno lokapratyakṣeṇa grahaṇam asti. na cāsya viśeṣasyāpramāṇakasyābhāvo 'stīti samādhiprajñānirgrāhya eva sa viśeṣo bhavati bhūtasūkṣmagato vā puruṣagato vā. tasmāc chrutānumānaprajñābhyām anyaviṣayā sā prajñā viśeṣārthatvād iti. 1.49
body.translated_text: <s>Śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge) is knowledge from scripture; it has the general (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object. For the particular cannot be conveyed by scripture. Why? Because words are not conventionally connected with the particular. Likewise, inference has only the general as its object. Where there is attainment, there is going; where there is no attainment, there is no going — so it is said. And inference makes a generalization. Therefore, neither scriptural nor inferential knowledge has any particular as its object. Nor can this object — subtle, concealed, or remote — be grasped by ordinary perception. But the non-existence of this particular, which has no other means of valid knowledge, cannot be maintained; therefore, the particular — whether residing in the subtle elements or in <s>Puruṣa</s> — is graspable only by the wisdom born of <s>samādhi</s>. Hence, that wisdom has a different object from the wisdoms born of scripture and inference, because its object is the particular. (1.49)

body.text: samādhiprajñāpratilambhe yoginaḥ prajñākṛtaḥ saṃskāro navo navo jāyate ---

children.translated_text: The impression born of that [truth-bearing wisdom] obstructs other impressions. (YS 1.50)

body.translated_text: Upon attaining the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>, new and ever-new impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are born from wisdom for the <s>yogin</s> —

body.text: samādhiprajñāprabhavaḥ saṃskāro vyutthānasaṃskārāśayaṃ bādhate. vyutthānasaṃskārābhibhavāt tatprabhavāḥ pratyayā na bhavanti. pratyayanirodhe samādhir upatiṣṭhate. tataḥ samādhijā prajñā, tataḥ prajñākṛtāḥ saṃskārā iti navo navaḥ saṃskārāśayo jāyate. tataś ca prajñā, tataś ca saṃskārā iti. katham asau saṃskārātiśayaś cittaṃ sādhikāraṃ na kariṣyatīti. na te prajñākṛtāḥ saṃskārāḥ kleśakṣayahetutvāc cittam adhikāraviśiṣṭaṃ kurvanti. cittaṃ hi te svakāryād avasādayanti. khyātiparyavasānaṃ hi cittaceṣṭitam iti. 1.50
body.translated_text: The impression arising from the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s> counteracts the store of impressions from the extroverted state (<s>vyutthāna</s>). Through the suppression of extroverted impressions, the cognitions arising from them no longer occur. With the cessation of cognitions, <s>samādhi</s> presents itself. From that, the wisdom born of <s>samādhi</s>; from that, impressions created by wisdom — thus, an ever-new store of impressions is born. From that comes wisdom, and from that come impressions. How will this excess of impressions not make the mind continue functioning? Those wisdom-created impressions do not render the mind to have further function, because they are the cause of the destruction of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Rather, they cause the mind to withdraw from its own activity. For the activity of the mind culminates in discernment (<s>khyāti</s>). (1.50)

body.text: kiṃ cāsya bhavati ---

children.text: tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ || YS_1.51 ||
children.translated_text: Upon the cessation even of that, from the cessation of all, there arises seedless <s>samādhi</s> (<s>nirbīja</s>). (YS 1.51)

children.text:
sa na kevalaṃ samādhiprajñāvirodhī prajñākṛtānām api saṃskārāṇāṃ pratibandhī bhavati. kasmāt, nirodhajaḥ saṃskāraḥ samādhijān saṃskārān bādhata iti.
  nirodhasthitikālakramānubhavena nirodhacittakṛtasaṃskārāstitvam anumeyam. vyutthānanirodhasamādhiprabhavaiḥ saha kaivalyabhāgīyaiḥ saṃskāraiś cittaṃ svasyāṃ prakṛtāv avasthitāyāṃ pravilīyate. tasmāt te saṃskārāś cittasyādhikāravirodhino na sthitihetavo bhavantīti. yasmād avasitādhikāraṃ saha kaivalyabhāgīyaiḥ saṃskāraiś cittaṃ nivartate, tasmin nivṛtte puruṣaḥ svarūpamātrapratiṣṭho 'taḥ śuddhaḥ kevalo mukta ity ucyata iti. 1.51
children.translated_text: That [seedless samādhi] not only opposes the wisdom of [sabīja] <s>samādhi</s> but also obstructs even the impressions created by wisdom. Why? Because the impression born of cessation counteracts the impressions born of <s>samādhi</s>. From the experience of the temporal sequence of the state of cessation, the existence of impressions created by the mind in cessation can be inferred. Together with the impressions conducive to <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation), along with those arising from the extroverted state, cessation, and <s>samādhi</s>, the mind dissolves into its own original nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) when it has settled. Therefore, those impressions do not serve as causes for the continuity of the mind, as they oppose its further functioning. Since the mind, its function completed, ceases together with the impressions conducive to <s>kaivalya</s>, and upon its cessation, <s>Puruṣa</s> — established solely in its own nature — is therefore called pure, alone, and liberated. (1.51)

body.translated_text: Furthermore, what happens to it?

body.text: iti śrīpātañjale sāṃkhyapravacane yogaśāstre śrīmadvyāsabhāṣye prathamaḥ samādhipādaḥ 1.
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter on <s>Samādhi</s> (<s>Samādhipāda</s>) in the venerable <s>Vyāsa</s>'s commentary on the <s>Yoga Śāstra</s>, the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana</s> of <s>Patañjali</s>. (1)

body.text: uddiṣṭaḥ samāhitacittasya yogaḥ. kathaṃ vyutthitacitto 'pi yogayuktaḥ syād ity etad ārabhyate ---

children.translated_text: Austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to the Lord (<s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>) constitute <s>Kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of action). (YS 2.1)

body.translated_text: The <s>yoga</s> of the concentrated mind has been described. Now, how even one whose mind is in the extroverted state may be engaged in <s>yoga</s> — that is undertaken here:

body.text:
nātapasvino yogaḥ sidhyati. anādikarmakleśavāsanācitrā pratyupasthitaviṣayajālā cāśuddhir nāntareṇa tapaḥ saṃbhedam āpadyata iti tapasa upādānam. tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam anenāsevyam iti manyate.
  svādhyāyaḥ praṇavādipavitrāṇāṃ japo mokṣaśāstrādhyayanaṃ vā. īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ sarvakriyāṇāṃ paramagurāv arpaṇaṃ tatphalasaṃnyāso vā. 2.1
body.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> does not succeed for one who does not practice austerity. The impurity — colored by beginningless impressions of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), with the web of sense objects presented before it — does not come to dissolution without austerity; therefore, austerity is taken up. And this [austerity] should be practiced so that it purifies the mind without causing harm, it is considered. <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is the repetition of sacred syllables beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) or the study of scriptures on liberation. <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) is the offering of all actions to the Supreme Teacher, or the renunciation of their fruits. (2.1)

body.text: sa hi kriyāyogaḥ ---

children.translated_text: is for the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> and for the purpose of attenuating the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). (YS 2.2)

body.translated_text: That <s>Kriyāyoga</s> indeed —

body.text: sa hy āsevyamānaḥ samādhiṃ bhāvayati kleśāṃś ca pratanūkaroti. pratanūkṛtān kleśān prasaṃkhyānāgninā dagdhabījakalpān aprasavadharmiṇaḥ kariṣyatīti. teṣāṃ tanūkaraṇāt punaḥ kleśair aparāmṛṣṭā sattvapuruṣānyatāmātrakhyātiḥ sūkṣmā prajñā samāptādhikārā pratiprasavāya kalpiṣyata iti. 2.2
body.translated_text: When practiced, it cultivates <s>samādhi</s> and attenuates the <s>kleśas</s>. The attenuated <s>kleśas</s>, rendered like burnt seeds by the fire of discriminative insight (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>), it will render incapable of germination. Through this attenuation of the <s>kleśas</s>, the subtle wisdom — untouched by the <s>kleśas</s>, being the discrimination of the mere difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, having completed its function — will be ready for involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>). (2.2)

body.text: atha ke kleśāḥ kiyanto veti ---

children.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), egoism (<s>asmitā</s>), attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and clinging to life (<s>abhiniveśa</s>) are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). (YS 2.3)

body.translated_text: Now, what are the <s>kleśas</s> and how many are they?

body.text: kleśā iti pañca viparyayā ity arthaḥ. te spandamānā guṇādhikāraṃ draḍhayanti, pariṇāmam avasthāpayanti, kāryakāraṇasrota unnamayanti, parasparānugrahatantrībhūtvā karmavipākaṃ cābhinirharantīti. 2.3
body.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> — meaning the five misconceptions (<s>viparyaya</s>). When active, they strengthen the dominion of the <s>guṇas</s>, establish the process of transformation, cause the current of cause and effect to rise, and — becoming interdependent through mutual support — they bring about the fruition of <s>karma</s>. (2.3)

body.text: avidyā kṣetram uttareṣāṃ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām || YS_2.4 ||
body.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the field of the others — whether dormant, attenuated, intermittent, or fully active. (YS 2.4)

body.text:
atrāvidyā kṣetraṃ prasavabhūmir uttarareṣām asmitādīnāṃ caturvidhavikalpānāṃ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām. tatra kā prasuptiḥ. cetasi śaktimātrapratiṣṭhānāṃ bījabhāvopagamaḥ. tasya prabodha ālambane saṃmukhībhāvaḥ. prasaṃkhyānavato dagdhakleśabījasya saṃmukhībhūte 'py ālambane nāsau punar asti, dagdhabījasya kutaḥ praroha iti. ataḥ kṣīṇakleśaḥ kuśalaś caramadeha ity ucyate. tatraiva sā dagdhabījabhāvā pañcamī kleśāvasthā nānyatreti. satāṃ kleśānāṃ tadā bījasāmarthyaṃ dagdham iti viṣayasya saṃmukhībhāve 'pi sati na bhavaty eṣāṃ prabodha ity uktā prasuptir dagdhabījānām aprarohaś ca.
  tanutvam ucyate --- pratipakṣabhāvanopahatāḥ kleśās tanavo bhavanti. tathā vicchidya vicchidya tena tenātmanā punaḥ punaḥ samudācarantīti vicchinnāḥ. kathaṃ, rāgakāle krodhasyādarśanāt. na hi rāgakāle krodhaḥ samudācarati. rāgaś ca kvacid dṛśyamāno na viṣayāntare nāsti. naikasyāṃ striyāṃ caitro rakta ity anyāsu strīṣu viraktaḥ, kiṃtu tatra rāgo labdhavṛttir anyatra tu bhaviṣyadvṛttir iti. sa hi tadā prasuptatanuvicchinno bhavati.
  viṣaye yo labdhavṛttiḥ sa udāraḥ. sarva evaite kleśaviṣayatvaṃ nātikrāmanti. kas tarhi vicchinnaḥ prasuptas tanur udāro vā kleśa iti, ucyate --- satyam evaitat, kiṃtu viśiṣṭānām evaiteṣāṃ vicchinnāditvam. yathaiva pratipakṣabhāvanāto nivṛttas tathaiva svavyañjakāñjanenābhivyakta iti. sarva evāmī kleśā avidyābhedāḥ. kasmāt, sarveṣv avidyaivābhiplavate. yad avidyayā vastv ākāryate tad evānuśerate kleśā viparyāsapratyayakāla upalabhyante kṣīyamāṇāṃ cāvidyām anu kṣīyanta iti. 2.4
body.translated_text:
Here, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the field, the ground of production, for the subsequent [afflictions] beginning with <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), in their fourfold varieties: dormant (<s>prasupta</s>), attenuated (<s>tanu</s>), interrupted (<s>vicchinna</s>), and fully active (<s>udāra</s>). What is dormancy among these? It is the assuming of a seed-state for those [afflictions] resting as mere potency in the mind. Their awakening is the coming face-to-face with an object. For one who possesses discriminative knowledge (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>) and whose affliction-seeds are burned, even when an object comes face-to-face, that [affliction] no longer exists—for how can a burned seed sprout? Therefore one whose afflictions are destroyed is called a proficient one (<s>kuśala</s>) in his last body. That fifth state of the afflictions—the state of having burned seeds—exists only there [in that person] and nowhere else. When the seed-potency of afflictions that exist [in potential] is burned, even when the object comes face-to-face, their awakening does not occur—thus dormancy and the non-sprouting of burned seeds have been stated.
  Attenuation is now explained: afflictions struck by the cultivation of their antidotes become attenuated. Likewise, being interrupted again and again, they arise again and again in various forms—thus they are 'interrupted.' How so? Because during the time of passion (<s>rāga</s>), anger is not seen. For anger does not arise during the time of passion. And passion, though seen with regard to one object, does not cease to exist with regard to another. Just because <s>Caitra</s> is passionate toward one woman does not mean he is free from passion toward other women; rather, in the former case passion has obtained its activity, while in the latter it has a future activity. Thus [passion] is then dormant, attenuated, or interrupted.
  That which has obtained its activity with regard to an object is fully active (<s>udāra</s>). All of these do not go beyond the condition of being objects of the afflictions. Then which affliction is interrupted, dormant, attenuated, or fully active? It is said: this is indeed true, but these states of being interrupted and so forth belong to them only when they are differentiated. Just as [an affliction] is turned back by the cultivation of its antidote, so too it is manifested by the collyrium of its own revealing conditions. All these afflictions are varieties of <s>avidyā</s>. Why? Because <s>avidyā</s> pervades them all. The very object that is fashioned by <s>avidyā</s> is what the afflictions follow; they are found during the time of erroneous cognition, and as <s>avidyā</s> diminishes, they diminish accordingly. [2.4]

body.text: tatrāvidyāsvarūpam ucyate ---

children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the perception of the eternal, pure, blissful, and the Self in the non-eternal, impure, painful, and the non-Self. [YS 2.5]

body.translated_text: Now the essential nature of <s>avidyā</s> is stated:

children.text: anitye kārye nityakhyātiḥ. tadyathā --- dhruvā pṛthivī, dhruvā sacandratārakā dyauḥ, amṛtā divaukasa iti. tathāśucau paramabībhatse kāye, ---
children.translated_text: In the impermanent effect, [there is] the perception of permanence. For example: 'The earth is eternal,' 'The sky with its moon and stars is eternal,' 'The celestial beings are immortal.' Likewise, regarding the body, which is supremely loathsome, [there is the misperception of purity]:
"By reason of its origin, its seed, its sustenance, its excretions, and its death,

children.text: kāyam ādheyaśaucatvāt paṇḍitā hy aśuciṃ viduḥ" //
children.translated_text: the wise know the body to be impure, because its purity is merely superimposed."

body.text:
iti aśucau śucikhyātir dṛśyate. naveva śaśāṅkalekhā kamanīyeyaṃ kanyā madhvamṛtāvayavanirmiteva candraṃ bhittvā niḥsṛteva jñāyate, nīlotpalapatrāyatākṣī hāvagarbhābhyāṃ locanābhyāṃ jīvalokam āśvāsayantīveti kasya kenābhisaṃbandhaḥ. bhavati caivam aśucau śuciviparyāsapratyaya iti. etenāpuṇye puṇyapratyayas tathaivānarthe cārthapratyayo vyākhyātaḥ.
  tathā duḥkhe sukhakhyātiṃ vakṣyati --- "pariṇāmatāpasaṃskāraduḥkhair guṇavṛttivirodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ" iti. tatra sukhakhyātir avidyā. tathānātmany ātmakhyātir bāhyopakaraṇeṣu cetanācetaneṣu bhogādhiṣṭhāne vā śarīre puruṣopakaraṇe vā manasy anātmany ātmakhyātir iti. tathaitad atroktam --- "vyaktam avyaktaṃ vā sattvam ātmatvenābhipratītya tasya saṃpadam anu nandaty ātmasaṃpadaṃ manvānas tasya vyāpadam anu śocaty ātmavyāpadaṃ manvānaḥ sa sarvo 'pratibuddhaḥ" iti. eṣā catuṣpadā bhavaty avidyā mūlam asya kleśasaṃtānasya karmāśayasya ca savipākasyeti.
  tasyāś cāmitrāgoṣpadavadvastusatattvaṃ vijñeyam. yathā nāmitro mitrābhāvo na mitramātraṃ kiṃtu tadviruddhaḥ sapatnaḥ. yathā vāgoṣpadaṃ na goṣpadābhāvo na goṣpadamātraṃ kiṃtu deśa eva tābhyām anyad vastvantaram. evam avidyā na pramāṇaṃ na pramāṇābhāvaḥ kiṃtu vidyāviparītaṃ jñānāntaram avidyeti. 2.5
body.translated_text:
Thus, in the impure, the perception of purity is seen. 'This maiden is lovely like a new crescent moon, as if fashioned from honey, nectar, and youth, as if she emerged by splitting open the moon; with eyes elongated like blue lotus petals, she seems to reassure the living world with her two glances pregnant with coquetry'—whose connection is with what? Thus there is the erroneous cognition of purity in the impure. By this, the cognition of merit in the non-meritorious and likewise the cognition of purpose in the purposeless are explained.
  Likewise, regarding the perception of pleasure in pain, it will be stated: 'Due to the suffering of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>), burning anguish (<s>tāpa</s>), and latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and due to the conflict of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>, everything is indeed suffering for the discerning one.' Therein, the perception of pleasure [in what is actually pain] is <s>avidyā</s>. Likewise, the perception of the Self in the non-Self—whether in external instruments, animate or inanimate, or in the body which is the seat of enjoyment, or in the mind which is the instrument of <s>Puruṣa</s>—[this is] the perception of the Self in the non-Self. As it has been stated here: 'Having identified as the Self either the manifest or the unmanifest <s>sattva</s> (being), one rejoices at its prosperity thinking it is one's own prosperity, and grieves at its adversity thinking it is one's own adversity—such a one is entirely unawakened.' This <s>avidyā</s> has four aspects and is the root of this stream of afflictions (<s>kleśa-saṃtāna</s>) and of the store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) together with its fruition.
  And its true nature (<s>vastu-satattva</s>) should be understood as being like an enemy or a puddle. Just as an enemy is not the absence of a friend, nor merely a non-friend, but rather an adversary opposed to a friend; and just as a puddle is not the absence of a cow's hoofprint, nor merely a hoofprint, but rather a different thing altogether from both—so <s>avidyā</s> is not valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), nor the absence of valid knowledge, but rather a different kind of cognition that is the opposite of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge)—this is <s>avidyā</s>. [2.5]

body.text: dṛgdarśanaśaktyor ekātmatevāsmitā || YS_2.6 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Asmitā</s> (egoism) is the apparent identity of the power of seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and the power of the seen (<s>darśana</s>). [YS 2.6]

body.text: puruṣo dṛkśaktir buddhir darśanaśaktir ity etayor ekasvarūpāpattir ivāsmitā kleśa ucyate. bhoktṛbhogyaśaktyor atyantavibhaktayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayor avibhāgaprāptāv iva satyāṃ bhogaḥ kalpate. svarūpapratilambhe tu tayoḥ kaivalyam eva bhavati kuto bhoga iti. tathā coktam --- "buddhitaḥ paraṃ puruṣam ākāraśīlavidyādibhir vibhaktam apaśyan kuryāt tatrātmabuddhiṃ mohena" iti. 2.6
body.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is the power of seeing (<s>dṛkśakti</s>); <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is the power of the seen (<s>darśanaśakti</s>). The seeming attainment of a single nature by these two is called the affliction of <s>asmitā</s> (egoism). When the powers of the enjoyer and the enjoyed, which are utterly distinct and utterly unmixed, seem to have reached a state of non-differentiation, enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) is imagined. But when their true natures are recovered, there is only <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)—whence then enjoyment? As it has been said: 'Not seeing <s>Puruṣa</s> as distinct from <s>buddhi</s> in form, character, knowledge, and so forth, one would, through delusion, attribute the notion of Self to that [buddhi].' [2.6]

body.text: sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ || YS_2.7 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) is that which follows upon pleasure. [YS 2.7]

body.text: sukhābhijñasya sukhānusmṛtipūrvaḥ sukhe tatsādhane vā yo gardhas tṛṣṇā lobhaḥ sa rāga iti. 2.7
body.translated_text: In one who has experienced pleasure, preceded by the recollection of pleasure, the craving, thirst, or greed for pleasure or its means—that is <s>rāga</s> (attachment). [2.7]

body.text: duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ || YS_2.8 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Dveṣa</s> (aversion) is that which follows upon pain. [YS 2.8]

body.text: duḥkhābhijñasya duḥkhānusmṛtipūrvo duḥkhe tatsādhane vā yaḥ pratigho manyur jighāṃsā krodhaḥ sa dveṣaḥ. 2.8
body.translated_text: In one who has experienced pain, preceded by the recollection of pain, the hostility, anger, desire to harm, or wrath toward pain or its means—that is <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion). [2.8]

body.text: svarasavāhī viduṣo 'pi tathā rūḍho 'bhiniveśaḥ || YS_2.9 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) flows on by its own momentum and is firmly established even in the wise. [YS 2.9]

body.text:
