sarvasya prāṇina iyam ātmāśīr nityā bhavati mā na bhūvaṃ bhūyāsam iti. na cānanubhūtamaraṇadharmakasyaiṣā bhavaty ātmāśīḥ. etayā ca pūrvajanmānubhavaḥ pratīyate. sa cāyam abhiniveśaḥ kleśaḥ svarasavāhī kṛmer api jātamātrasya pratyakṣānumānāgamair asaṃbhāvito maraṇatrāsa ucchedadṛṣṭyātmakaḥ pūrvajanmānubhūtaṃ maraṇaduḥkham anumāpayati.
  yathā cāyam atyantamūḍheṣu dṛśyate kleśas tathā viduṣo 'pi vijñātapūrvāparāntasya rūḍhaḥ. kasmāt samānā hi tayoḥ kuśalākuśalayor maraṇaduḥkhānubhavād iyaṃ vāsaneti. 2.9
body.translated_text:
In every living being, there is this eternal self-blessing: 'May I not cease to be; may I continue to exist.' And this self-blessing cannot arise in one who has not [previously] experienced the nature of death. And by this [observation], experience from previous births is inferred. This <s>abhiniveśa</s>, an affliction flowing on by its own momentum, is the terror of death—even in a newborn worm—having the nature of the view of annihilation (<s>uccheda-dṛṣṭi</s>), which is not accountable by perception, inference, or scripture, and which causes one to infer the suffering of death experienced in previous births.
  And just as this affliction is seen in the utterly deluded, so too it is firmly established even in the wise who know their past and future ends. Why? Because this <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) born from the experience of the suffering of death is common to both the virtuous and the non-virtuous. [2.9]

body.text: te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ || YS_2.10 ||
body.translated_text: These [afflictions] in their subtle form are to be abandoned by involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>). [YS 2.10]

body.text: te pañca kleśā dagdhabījakalpā yoginaś caritādhikāre cetasi pralīne saha tenaivāstaṃ gacchanti. 2.10
body.translated_text: These five afflictions, in a state like that of burned seeds, when the yogin's mind, having completed its purpose, dissolves—they vanish along with it. [2.10]

body.text: sthitānāṃ tu bījabhāvopagatānām ---

children.translated_text: Their activities (<s>vṛttis</s>) are to be abandoned by meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). [YS 2.11]

body.translated_text: But for those [afflictions] that remain, having assumed a seed-state:

body.text: kleśānāṃ yā vṛttayaḥ sthūlās tāḥ kriyāyogena tanūkṛtāḥ satyaḥ prasaṃkhyānena dhyānena hātavyā yāvat sūkṣmīkṛtā yāvad dagdhabījakalpā iti. yathā vastrāṇāṃ sthūlo malaḥ pūrvaṃ nirdhūyate paścāt sūkṣmo yatnenopāyena cāpanīyate tathā svalpapratipakṣāḥ sthūlā vṛttayaḥ kleśānāṃ, sūkṣmās tu mahāpratipakṣā iti. 2.11
body.translated_text: The gross activities of the afflictions—having first been attenuated by <s>kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action), while still existing—are to be abandoned by discriminative meditation (<s>prasaṃkhyāna-dhyāna</s>), until they are made subtle, until they reach the state of burned seeds. Just as the gross dirt of garments is first shaken off, and then the subtle [dirt] is removed with effort and skill, so too the gross activities of the afflictions have a weak antidote, while the subtle ones have a powerful antidote. [2.11]

body.text: kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ || YS_2.12 ||
body.translated_text: The store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>), rooted in the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), is to be experienced in the seen or unseen births. [YS 2.12]

body.text: tatra puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayaḥ kāmalobhamohakrodhabhavaḥ. sa dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaś cādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaś ca. tatra tīvrasaṃvegena mantratapaḥsamādhibhir nirvartita īśvaradevatāmaharṣimahānubhāvānām ārādhanād vā yaḥ pariniṣpannaḥ sa sadyaḥ paripacyate puṇyakarmāśaya iti. tathā tīvrakleśena bhītavyādhitakṛpaṇeṣu viśvāsopagateṣu vā mahānubhāveṣu vā tapasviṣu kṛtaḥ punaḥ punar apakāraḥ sa cāpi pāpakarmāśayaḥ sadya eva paripacyate. yathā nandīśvaraḥ kumāro manuṣyapariṇāmaṃ hitvā devatvena pariṇataḥ. tathā nahuṣo 'pi devānām indraḥ svakaṃ pariṇāmaṃ hitvā tiryaktvena pariṇata iti. tatra nārakāṇāṃ nāsti dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśayaḥ. kṣīṇakleśānām api nāsty adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśaya iti. 2.12
body.translated_text: Therein, the store of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> arises from desire, greed, delusion, anger, and [attachment to] existence. It is to be experienced either in the present birth or in a future birth. Among these, that which is brought to completion through intense fervor, by <s>mantras</s>, austerities, and <s>samādhi</s>, or through the propitiation of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), deities, great sages, and the greatly powerful—that meritorious store of <s>karma</s> ripens immediately. Likewise, harm done repeatedly with intense affliction to the frightened, the sick, the wretched, those who have come in trust, or to the greatly powerful ascetics—that sinful store of <s>karma</s> also ripens immediately. For example, <s>Nandīśvara</s>, the youth, abandoning a human transformation, was transformed into a divine being. And <s>Nahuṣa</s>, though he was <s>Indra</s> of the gods, abandoning his own transformation, was transformed into an animal. Among these, for beings in the hells, there is no store of <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the present birth. And for those whose afflictions are destroyed, there is no store of <s>karma</s> to be experienced in a future birth. [2.12]

body.text: sati mūle tadvipāko jātyāyurbhogāḥ || YS_2.13 ||
body.translated_text: As long as the root exists, there is its fruition as birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and experience (<s>bhoga</s>). [YS 2.13]

body.text:
satsu kleśeṣu karmāśayo vipākārambhī bhavati nocchinnakleśamūlaḥ. yathā tuṣāvanaddhāḥ śālitaṇḍulā adagdhabījabhāvāḥ prarohasamarthā bhavanti, nāpanītatuṣā dagdhabījabhāvā vā tathā kleśāvanaddhaḥ karmāśayo vipākaprarohī bhavati, nāpanītakleśo na prasaṃkhyānadagdhakleśabījabhāvo veti. sa ca vipākas trividho jātir āyur bhoga iti.
  tatredaṃ vicāryate --- kim ekaṃ karmaikasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam athaikaṃ karmānekaṃ janmākṣipatīti. dvitīyā vicāraṇā --- kim anekaṃ karmānekaṃ janma nirvartayati athānekaṃ karmaikaṃ janma nirvartayatīti. na tāvad ekaṃ karmaikasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam. kasmāt, anādikālapracitasyāsaṃkhyeyasyāvaśiṣṭasya karmaṇaḥ sāṃpratikasya ca phalakramāniyamād anāśvāso lokasya prasaktaḥ, sa cāniṣṭa iti. na caikaṃ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam. kasmāt, anekeṣu karmasu ekaikam eva karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam ity avaśiṣṭasya vipākakālābhāvaḥ prasaktaḥ, sa cāpy aniṣṭa iti. na cānekaṃ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam. kasmāt, tad anekaṃ janma yugapan na saṃbhavatīti krameṇaiva vācyam. tathā ca pūrvadoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ.
  tasmāj janmaprāyaṇāntare kṛtaḥ puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayapracayo vicitraḥ pradhānopasarjanabhāvenāvasthitaḥ prāyaṇābhivyakta ekapraghaṭṭakena maraṇaṃ prasādhya saṃmūrchita ekam eva janma karoti. tac ca janma tenaiva karmaṇā labdhāyuṣkaṃ bhavati. tasminn āyuṣi tenaiva karmaṇā bhogaḥ saṃpadyata iti. asau karmāśayo janmāyurbhogahetutvāt trivipāko 'bhidhīyata iti. ata ekabhavikaḥ karmāśaya ukta iti.
  dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyas tv ekavipākārambhī bhogahetutvād dvivipākārambhī vāyurbhogahetutvān nandīśvaravan nahuṣavad veti. kleśakarmavipākānubhavanirvartitābhis tu vāsanābhir anādikālasaṃmūrchitam idaṃ cittaṃ vicitrīkṛtam iva sarvato matsyajālaṃ granthibhir ivātatam ity etā anekabhavapūrvikā vāsanāḥ. yas tv ayaṃ karmāśaya eṣa evaikabhavika ukta iti. ye saṃskārāḥ smṛtihetavas tā vāsanās tāś cānādikālīnā iti.
  yas tv asāv ekabhavikaḥ karmāśayaḥ sa niyatavipākaś cāniyatavipākaś ca. tatra dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya niyatavipākasyaivāyaṃ niyamo na tv adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyāniyatavipākasya kasmāt. yo hy adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyo 'niyatavipākas tasya trayī gatiḥ --- kṛtasyāvipakvasya nāśaḥ, pradhānakarmaṇy āvāpagamanaṃ vā, niyatavipākapradhānakarmaṇābhibhūtasya vā ciram avasthānam iti.
  tatra kṛtasyāvipakvasya nāśo yathā śuklakarmodayād ihaiva nāśaḥ kṛṣṇasya. yatredam uktam --- "dve dve ha vai karmaṇī veditavye pāpakasyaiko rāśiḥ puṇyakṛto 'pahanti tad icchasva karmāṇi sukṛtāni kartum ihaiva te karma kavayo vedayante."
  pradhānakarmaṇy āvāpagamanam. yatredam uktaṃ --- "syāt svalpaḥ saṃkaraḥ saparihāraḥ sapratyavamarṣaḥ kuśalasya nāpakarṣāyālam. kasmāt, kuśalaṃ hi me bahv anyad asti yatrāyam āvāpaṃ gataḥ svarge 'py apakarṣam alpaṃ kariṣyati" iti.
  niyatavipākapradhānakarmaṇābhibhūtasya vā ciram avasthānam. katham iti, adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyaiva niyatavipākasya karmaṇaḥ samānaṃ maraṇam abhivyaktikāraṇam uktam. na tv adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyāniyatavipākasya. yat tv adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaṃ karmāniyatavipākaṃ tan naśyed āvāpaṃ vā gacched abhibhūtaṃ vā ciram apy upāsīta, yāvat samānaṃ karmābhivyañjakaṃ nimittam asya na vipākābhimukhaṃ karotīti. tadvipākasyaiva deśakālanimittānavadhāraṇād iyaṃ karmagatiś citrā durvijñānā ceti. na cotsargasyāpavādān nivṛttir ity ekabhavikaḥ karmāśayo 'nujñāyata iti. 2.13
body.translated_text: When afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) exist, the store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) becomes capable of initiating fruition (<s>vipāka</s>), but not when the root of afflictions has been severed. Just as unhusked rice grains, with their seed-nature unburnt, are capable of sprouting, but not when the husks have been removed or the seed-nature has been burnt — so too, the store of <s>karma</s> enveloped by afflictions is capable of producing the sprout of fruition, but not when afflictions have been removed, nor when the seed-nature of afflictions has been burnt by discriminative knowledge (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>). And that fruition is threefold —

body.text: te hlādaparitāpaphalāḥ puṇyāpuṇyahetutvāt || YS_2.14 ||
body.translated_text: They [the results of action] bear the fruit of pleasure and pain, because their cause is merit and demerit. [<s>YS</s> 2.14]

body.text: te janmāyurbhogāḥ puṇyahetukāḥ sukhaphalā apuṇyahetukā duḥkhaphalā iti. yathā cedaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratikūlātmakam evaṃ viṣayasukhakāle 'pi duḥkham asty eva pratikūlātmakaṃ yoginaḥ. 2.14
body.translated_text: Birth, lifespan, and experience (<s>bhoga</s>) — those caused by merit bear the fruit of happiness; those caused by demerit bear the fruit of suffering. And just as this suffering is of an adverse nature, so too even at the time of sensory pleasure, suffering of an adverse nature exists for the yogin. [2.14]

body.text: kathaṃ, tad upapādyate ---

children.text: pariṇāmatāpasaṃskāraduḥkhair guṇavṛttivirodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ || YS_2.15 ||
children.translated_text: For the discerning one (<s>vivekin</s>), everything is indeed suffering, due to the suffering of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>), anguish (<s>tāpa</s>), and latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and due to the conflict of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>. [<s>YS</s> 2.15]

children.text:
sarvasyāyaṃ rāgānuviddhaś cetanācetanasādhanādhīnaḥ sukhānubhava iti tatrāsti rāgajaḥ karmāśayaḥ. tathā ca dveṣṭi duḥkhasādhanāni muhyati ceti dveṣamohakṛto 'py asti karmāśayaḥ. tathā coktam --- "nānupahatya bhūtāny upabhogaḥ saṃbhavatīti hiṃsākṛto 'py asti śarīraḥ karmāśayaḥ" iti. viṣayasukhaṃ cāvidyety uktam.
  yā bhogeṣv indriyāṇāṃ tṛpter upaśāntis tat sukham. yā laulyād anupaśāntis tad duḥkham. na cendriyāṇāṃ bhogābhyāsena vaitṛṣṇyaṃ kartuṃ śakyam. kasmāt, yato bhogābhyāsam anu vivardhante rāgāḥ kauśalāni cendriyāṇām iti. tasmād anupāyaḥ sukhasya bhogābhyāsa iti. sa khalv ayaṃ vṛścikaviṣabhīta ivāśīviṣeṇa daṣṭo yaḥ sukhārthī viṣayānuvāsito mahati duḥkhapaṅke nimagna iti. eṣā pariṇāmaduḥkhatā nāma pratikūlā sukhāvasthāyām api yoginam eva kliśnāti.
  atha kā tāpaduḥkhatā, sarvasya dveṣānuviddhaś cetanācetanasādhanādhīnas tāpānubhava iti tatrāsti dveṣajaḥ karmāśayaḥ. sukhasādhanāni ca prārthayamānaḥ kāyena vācā manasā ca parispandate tataḥ param anugṛhṇāty upahanti ceti parānugrahapīḍābhyāṃ dharmādharmāv upacinoti. sa karmāśayo lobhān mohāc ca bhavatīty eṣā tāpaduḥkhatocyate. kā punaḥ saṃskāraduḥkhatā, sukhānubhavāt sukhasaṃskārāśayo duḥkhānubhavād api duḥkhasaṃskārāśaya iti. evaṃ karmabhyo vipāke 'nubhūyamāne sukhe duḥkhe vā punaḥ karmāśayapracaya iti.
  evam idam anādi duḥkhasroto viprasṛtaṃ yoginam eva pratikūlātmakatvād udvejayati. kasmāt, akṣipātrakalpo hi vidvān iti. yathorṇātantur akṣipātre nyastaḥ sparśena duḥkhayati na cānyeṣu gātrāvayaveṣu, evam etāni duḥkhāny akṣipātrakalpaṃ yoginam eva kliśnanti netaraṃ pratipattāram. itaraṃ tu svakarmopahṛtaṃ duḥkham upāttam upāttaṃ tyajantaṃ tyaktaṃ tyaktam upādadānam anādivāsanāvicitrayā cittavṛttyā samantato 'nuviddham ivāvidyayā hātavya evāhaṃkāramamakārānupātinaṃ jātaṃ jātaṃ bāhyādhyātmikobhayanimittās triparvāṇas tāpā anuplavante. tad evam anādinā duḥkhasrotasā vyuhyamānam ātmānaṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā yogī sarvaduḥkhakṣayakāraṇaṃ samyagdarśanaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadyata iti.
  guṇavṛttivirodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ. prakhyāpravṛttisthitirūpā buddhiguṇāḥ parasparānugrahatantrī bhūtvā śāntaṃ ghoraṃ mūḍhaṃ vā pratyayaṃ triguṇam evārabhante. calaṃ ca guṇavṛttam iti kṣiprapariṇāmi cittam uktam. rūpātiśayā vṛttyatiśayāś ca paraspareṇa virudhyante, sāmānyāni tv atiśayaiḥ saha pravartante. evam ete guṇā itaretarāśrayeṇopārjitasukhaduḥkhamohapratyayāḥ sarve sarvarūpā bhavantīti, guṇapradhānabhāvakṛtas tv eṣāṃ viśeṣa iti. tasmād duḥkham eva sarvaṃ vivekina iti.
  tad asya mahato duḥkhasamudāyasya prabhavabījam avidyā. tasyāś ca samyagdarśanam abhāvahetuḥ. yathā cikitsāśāstraṃ caturvyūham --- rogo rogahetur ārogyaṃ bhaiṣajyam iti. evam idam api śāstram caturvyūham eva. tadyathā --- saṃsāraḥ saṃsārahetur mokṣo mokṣopāya iti. tatra duḥkhabahulaḥ saṃsāro heyaḥ. pradhānapuruṣayoḥ saṃyogo heyahetuḥ. saṃyogasyātyantikī nivṛttir hānam. hānopāyaḥ samyagdarśanam.
  tatra hātuḥ svarūpam upādeyaṃ vā heyaṃ vā na bhavitum arhatīti hāne tasyocchedavādaprasaṅga upādāne ca hetuvādaḥ. ubhayapratyākhyāne śāśvatavāda ity etat samyagdarśanam. 2.15
children.translated_text: Every experience of pleasure is pervaded by attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and depends on conscious and unconscious means — therefore there exists a store of <s>karma</s> born of attachment. Similarly, one hates the means of suffering and is deluded — therefore there also exists a store of <s>karma</s> produced by aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) and delusion (<s>moha</s>). And thus it has been said: 'Since enjoyment is not possible without harming beings, there is a store of <s>karma</s> born of <s>hiṃsā</s> [violence].'

body.translated_text: How so? That is explained —

body.text: tad etac chāstraṃ caturvyūham ity abhidhīyate ---

children.translated_text: The suffering that is yet to come is to be avoided. [<s>YS</s> 2.16]

body.translated_text: This teaching is said to have a fourfold arrangement —

body.text: duḥkham atītam upabhogenātivāhitaṃ na heyapakṣe vartate. vartamānaṃ ca svakṣaṇe bhogārūḍham iti na tat kṣaṇāntare heyatām āpadyate. tasmād yad evānāgataṃ duḥkhaṃ tad evākṣipātrakalpaṃ yoginaṃ kliśnāti netaraṃ pratipattāram. tad eva heyatām āpadyate. 2.16
body.translated_text: Suffering that is past has been exhausted through experience and does not fall within what is to be avoided. And present [suffering], having mounted its own moment of experience, does not become avoidable in another moment. Therefore, only the suffering that is yet to come — that alone, like a disease yet to manifest, afflicts the yogin, and no other experiencing subject. That alone becomes what is to be avoided.

body.text: tasmād yad eva heyam ity ucyate tasyaiva kāraṇaṃ pratinirdiśyate ---

children.translated_text: The conjunction of the seer and the seen is the cause of what is to be avoided. [<s>YS</s> 2.17]

body.translated_text: Therefore, the cause of that very thing which is called 'to be avoided' is indicated —

body.text:
draṣṭā buddheḥ pratisaṃvedī puruṣaḥ. dṛśyā buddhisattvopārūḍhāḥ sarve dharmāḥ. tad etad dṛśyam ayaskāntamaṇikalpaṃ saṃnidhimātropakāri dṛśyatvena svaṃ bhavati puruṣasya dṛśirūpasya svāminaḥ, anubhavakarmaviṣayatām āpannaṃ yataḥ. anyasvarūpeṇa pratilabdhātmakaṃ svatantram api parārthatvāt paratantram.
  tayor dṛgdarśanaśaktyor anādir arthakṛtaḥ saṃyogo heyahetur duḥkhasya kāraṇam ity arthaḥ. tathā coktam --- tatsaṃyogahetuvivarjanāt syād ayam ātyantiko duḥkhapratīkāraḥ. kasmāt, duḥkhahetoḥ parihāryasya pratīkāradarśanāt. tadyathā --- pādatalasya bhedyatā, kaṇṭakasya bhettṛtvaṃ, parihāraḥ kaṇṭakasya pā(pa)dānadhiṣṭhānaṃ pādatrāṇavyavahitena vādhiṣṭhānam, etat trayaṃ yo veda loke sa tatra pratīkāram ārabhamāṇo bhedajaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāpnoti. kasmāt, tritvopalabdhisāmarthyād iti. atrāpi tāpakasya rajasaḥ sattvam eva tapyam. kasmāt, tapikriyāyāḥ karmasthatvāt, sattve karmaṇi tapikriyā nāpariṇāmini niṣkriye kṣetrajñe, darśitaviṣayatvāt. sattve tu tapyamāne tadākārānurodhī puruṣo 'py anutapyata iti. 2.17
body.translated_text: The seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) is <s>Puruṣa</s>, the experiencer of <s>buddhi</s>. The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) is all <s>dharmas</s> [phenomena] that have mounted upon the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s>. This seen, like a loadstone, by its mere proximity becomes the seen for <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose nature is seeing and who is the master — having become the object of the function of experience. With a nature other [than its own], it is perceived —

body.text: dṛśyasvarūpam ucyate ---

children.translated_text: The seen has the character of luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), activity (<s>kriyā</s>), and stability (<s>sthiti</s>); it consists of the elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and the senses (<s>indriya</s>); and its purpose is experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). [<s>YS</s> 2.18]

children.text:
prakāśaśīlaṃ sattvam. kriyāśīlaṃ rajaḥ sthitiśīlaṃ tama iti. ete guṇāḥ parasparoparaktapravibhāgāḥ pariṇāminaḥ saṃyogaviyogadharmāṇa itaretaropāśrayeṇopārjitamūrtayaḥ parasparāṅgāṅgitve 'py asaṃbhinnaśaktipravibhāgās tulyajātīyātulyajātīyaśaktibhedānupātinaḥ pradhānavelāyām upadarśitasaṃnidhānā guṇatve 'pi ca vyāpāramātreṇa pradhānāntarṇītānumitāstitāḥ puruṣārthakartavyatayā prayuktasāmarthyāḥ saṃnidhimātropakāriṇo 'yaskāntamaṇikalpāḥ pratyayam antareṇaikatamasya vṛttim anuvartamānāḥ pradhānaśabdavācyā bhavanti. etad dṛśyam ity ucyate.
  tad etad bhūtendriyātmakaṃ bhūtabhāvena pṛthivyādinā sūkṣmasthūlena pariṇamate. tathendriyabhāvena śrotrādinā sūkṣmasthūlena pariṇamata iti. tat tu nāprayojanam api tu prayojanam urarīkṛtya pravartata iti bhogāpavargārthaṃ hi tad dṛśyaṃ puruṣasyeti. tatreṣṭāniṣṭaguṇasvarūpāvadhāraṇam avibhāgāpannaṃ bhogo bhoktuḥ svarūpāvadhāraṇam apavarga iti. dvayor atiriktam anyad darśanaṃ nāsti. tathā coktam --- ayaṃ tu khalu triṣu guṇeṣu kartṛṣv akartari ca puruṣe tulyātulyajātīye caturthe tatkriyāsākṣiṇy upanīyamānān sarvabhāvān upapannān anupaśyann adarśanam anyac chaṅkata iti.
  tāv etau bhogāpavargau buddhikṛtau buddhāv eva vartamānau kathaṃ puruṣe vyapadiśyete iti. yathā vijayaḥ parājayo vā yoddhṛṣu vartamānaḥ svāmini vyapadiśyate, sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti, evaṃ bandhamokṣau buddhāv eva vartamānau puruṣe vyapadiśyete, sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti. buddher eva puruṣārthāparisamāptir bandhas tadarthāvasāyo mokṣa iti. etena grahaṇadhāraṇohāpohatattvajñānābhiniveśā buddhau vartamānāḥ puruṣe 'dhyāropitasadbhāvāḥ. sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti. 2.18
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> has the nature of illumination. <s>Rajas</s> has the nature of activity. <s>Tamas</s> has the nature of inertia. These <s>guṇas</s>, mutually colored and differentiated, are subject to transformation, possessing the properties of conjunction and disjunction, acquiring form through mutual dependence, and although each being part and whole of the others, having undivided powers of differentiation — they follow the distinction of powers both similar and dissimilar in kind. At the time of [being] the primary cause (<s>pradhāna</s>), they are present as indicated; and even when in the state of being secondary, their existence is inferred as being contained within the primary cause by mere operation. Endowed with the capacity to serve the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, like a magnet-stone that benefits by mere proximity, following the activity of one or another without [requiring] cognition — they are called by the word <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature). This is what is called 'the seen' (<s>dṛśya</s>). This [seen], having the nature of elements and senses, transforms in the form of elements — earth and the rest — both subtle and gross. Likewise it transforms in the form of senses — hearing and the rest — both subtle and gross. But it does not operate without purpose; rather, having accepted a purpose, it operates. For that seen is for the sake of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Among these, the ascertainment of the essential nature of the desired and undesired <s>guṇas</s>, when undifferentiated, is experience (<s>bhoga</s>) for the experiencer. The ascertainment of the essential nature [of <s>Puruṣa</s>] is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). There is no other seeing beyond these two. And thus it is said: 'This [<s>Puruṣa</s>], indeed, regarding the three <s>guṇas</s> which are the agents and the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is not an agent, the fourth — being a witness of their actions, whether of similar or dissimilar kind — seeing all states of existence as they are, suspects no other vision.' Now, these two — experience and liberation — being effected by <s>buddhi</s> and occurring in <s>buddhi</s> alone, how are they attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>? Just as victory or defeat, occurring among the soldiers, is attributed to the master — for he is the one who experiences their fruit — so too bondage and liberation, occurring in <s>buddhi</s> alone, are attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>, for he is the one who experiences their fruit. The non-completion of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose by <s>buddhi</s> is bondage; the completion of that purpose is liberation. By this, grasping, retention, rejection, and the attachment to knowledge of reality — all occurring in <s>buddhi</s> — have their existence superimposed upon <s>Puruṣa</s>, for he is the one who experiences their fruit. 2.18

body.translated_text: The nature of the seen is stated —

body.text: dṛśyānāṃ guṇānāṃ svarūpabhedāvadhāraṇārtham idam ārabhyate ---

children.translated_text: The specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), the merely indicated (<s>liṅgamātra</s>), and the unindicated (<s>aliṅga</s>) — these are the stages of the <s>guṇas</s>. || <s>YS</s> 2.19 ||

body.translated_text: In order to ascertain the essential distinction of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> constituting the seen, this is undertaken:

body.text:
tatrākāśavāyvagnyudakabhūmayo bhūtāni śabdasparśarūparasagandhatanmātrāṇām aviśeṣāṇāṃ viśeṣāḥ. tathā śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇāni buddhīndriyāṇi, vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāḥ karmendriyāṇi, ekādaśaṃ manaḥ sarvārtham, ity etāny asmitālakṣaṇasyāviśeṣasya viśeṣāḥ. guṇānām eṣa ṣoḍaśako viśeṣapariṇāmaḥ.
  ṣaḍ aviśeṣāḥ. tadyathā --- śabdatanmātraṃ sparśatanmātraṃ rūpatanmātraṃ rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātraṃ ceti ekadvitricatuḥpañcalakṣaṇāḥ śabdādayaḥ pañcāviśeṣāḥ, ṣaṣṭhaś cāviśeṣo 'smitāmātra iti. ete sattāmātrasyātmano mahataḥ ṣaḍaviśeṣapariṇāmāḥ. yat tat paramaviśeṣebhyo liṅgamātraṃ mahattattvaṃ tasminn ete sattāmātre mahaty ātmany avasthāya vivṛddhikāṣṭhām anubhavanti.
  pratisaṃsṛjyamānāś ca tasminn eva sattāmātre mahaty ātmany avasthāya yat tan niḥsattāsattaṃ niḥsadasan nirasad avyaktam aliṅgaṃ pradhānaṃ tat pratiyanti. eṣa teṣāṃ liṅgamātraḥ pariṇāmo niḥsattāsattaṃ cāliṅgapariṇāma iti.
  aliṅgāvasthāyāṃ na puruṣārtho hetur nāliṅgāvasthāyām ādau puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṃ bhavatīti. na tasyāḥ puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṃ bhavatīti. nāsau puruṣārthakṛteti nityākhyāyate. trayāṇāṃ tv avasthāviśeṣāṇām ādau puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṃ bhavati. sa cārtho hetur nimittaṃ kāraṇaṃ bhavatīty anityākhyāyate. guṇās tu sarvadharmānupātino na pratyastam ayante nopajāyante. vyaktibhir evātītānāgatavyayāgamavatībhir guṇānvayinībhir upajananāpāyadharmakā iva pratyavabhāsante. yathā devadatto daridrāti. kasmāt yato 'sya mriyante gāva iti, gavām eva maraṇāt tasya daridrāṇaṃ na svarūpahānād iti samaḥ samādhiḥ.
  liṅgamātram aliṅgasya pratyāsannaṃ, tatra tat saṃsṛṣṭaṃ vivicyate kramān ativṛttayaḥ. tathā ṣaḍ aviśeṣā liṅgamātre saṃsṛṣṭā vivicyante pariṇāmakramaniyamāt. tathā teṣv aviśeṣeṣu bhūtendriyāṇi saṃsṛṣṭāni vivicyante. tathā coktaṃ purastāt. na viśeṣebhyaḥ paraṃ tattvāntaram astīti viśeṣāṇāṃ nāsti tattvāntarapariṇāmaḥ. teṣāṃ tu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyāyiṣyante. 2.19
body.translated_text: Among these, space, wind, fire, water, and earth — the elements — are the specific forms (<s>viśeṣa</s>) of the non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>) subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) — sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. Similarly, the cognitive senses (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) — hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell — and the active senses (<s>karmendriya</s>) — speech, hands, feet, excretion, and generation — and the eleventh, the mind (<s>manas</s>), which serves all purposes: these are the specific forms of the non-specific characterized as 'I-am-ness' (<s>asmitā</s>). This is the sixteenfold specific transformation of the <s>guṇas</s>. There are six non-specific forms: namely, the subtle element of sound, the subtle element of touch, the subtle element of form, the subtle element of taste, and the subtle element of smell — with one, two, three, four, and five characteristics respectively — these are the five non-specific, and the sixth non-specific is the mere 'I-am-ness.' These are the six non-specific transformations of the great principle (<s>mahat</s>), whose nature is pure existence. That which is the 'merely indicated' (<s>liṅgamātra</s>) — the great principle (<s>mahattattva</s>) — beyond the primary specifics: abiding in that great self whose nature is mere existence, [the non-specifics] experience the pinnacle of development. And when being reabsorbed, abiding in that very great self of mere existence, they return to that which is neither existence nor non-existence, neither real nor unreal, the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the unindicated (<s>aliṅga</s>), <s>pradhāna</s>. This is their transformation into the merely indicated, and the transformation into the unindicated is neither existence nor non-existence. In the unindicated state, the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is not the cause [of activity]; in the unindicated state, at the beginning, the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> does not become the cause. It is not made for <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose — hence it is called eternal. But for the three particular states, at the beginning, the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> becomes the cause. And that purpose, being a cause, condition, and reason, is called non-eternal. The <s>guṇas</s>, however, which follow all properties, neither set nor arise. Through their particular manifestations — which have the properties of past and future, of loss and acquisition, following the <s>guṇas</s> — they appear as if having the properties of arising and ceasing. Just as [we say] '<s>Devadatta</s> becomes poor' — why? — because his cows die. From the death of the cows alone comes his poverty, not from the loss of his own nature. The same resolution [applies here]. The 'merely indicated' is proximate to the unindicated; therein, [the non-specifics] are merged and distinguished in succession, transcending [each stage]. Similarly, the six non-specifics, merged in the merely indicated, are distinguished due to the regularity of the order of transformation. Similarly, the elements and senses, merged in those non-specifics, are distinguished. And this has been stated previously. Since there is no further principle beyond the specifics, the specifics have no transformation into another principle. But their transformations of property, characteristic, and state will be explained. 2.19

body.text: vyākhyātaṃ dṛśyam atha draṣṭuḥ svarūpāvadhāraṇārtham idam ārabhyate ---

children.translated_text: The seer is mere seeing-power; though pure, it witnesses mental modifications. || <s>YS</s> 2.20 ||

body.translated_text: The seen has been explained. Now, in order to ascertain the essential nature of the seer, this is undertaken:

body.text:
dṛśimātra iti dṛkśaktir eva viśeṣaṇāparāmṛṣṭety arthaḥ. sa puruṣo bhuddheḥ pratisaṃvedī. sa buddher na sarūpo nātyantaṃ virūpa iti. na tāvat sarūpaḥ kasmāt. jñātājñātaviṣayatvāt pariṇāminī hi buddhiḥ. tasyāś ca viṣayo gavādir ghaṭādir vā jñātaś cājñātaś ceti pariṇāmitvaṃ darśayati.
  sadājñātaviṣayatvaṃ tu puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvaṃ paridīpayati kasmāt. na hi buddhiś ca nāma puruṣaviṣayaś ca syād agṛhītā gṛhītā ceti siddhaṃ puruṣasya sadājñātaviṣayatvaṃ tataś cāpariṇāmitvam iti. kiṃ ca parārthā buddhiḥ saṃhatyakāritvāt, svārthaḥ puruṣa iti. tathā sarvārthādhyavasāyakatvāt triguṇā buddhis triguṇatvād acetaneti. guṇānāṃ tūpadraṣṭā puruṣa ity ato na sarūpaḥ.
  astu tarhi virūpa iti. nātyantaṃ virūpaḥ kasmāt. śuddho 'py asau pratyayānupaśyo yataḥ. pratyayaṃ bauddham anupaśyati, tam anupaśyann atadātmāpi tadātmaka iva pratyavabhāsate. tathā coktam --- apariṇāminī hi bhoktṛśaktir apratisaṃkramā ca pariṇāminy arthe pratisaṃkrānteva tadvṛttim anupatati, tasyāś ca prāptacaitanyopagraharūpāyā buddhivṛtter anukāramātratayā buddhivṛttyaviśiṣṭā hi jñānavṛttir ity ākhyāyate. 2.20
body.translated_text: 'Mere seeing-power' (<s>dṛśimātra</s>) means: the power of seeing itself, not qualified by anything else — this is the meaning. That <s>Puruṣa</s> is the one who perceives <s>buddhi</s>. He is neither identical in nature with <s>buddhi</s> nor completely different from it. First, he is not identical — why? Because <s>buddhi</s> has objects that are both known and unknown; for <s>buddhi</s> is subject to transformation. Its objects — a cow, a pot, and the like — are sometimes known and sometimes unknown, which demonstrates its transformative nature. But <s>Puruṣa</s>'s having an always-known object reveals his non-transformative nature — why? Because <s>buddhi</s> cannot be both an object of <s>Puruṣa</s> and at the same time ungrasped and grasped — therefore it is established that <s>Puruṣa</s> has an always-known object, and hence is non-transformative. Furthermore, <s>buddhi</s> exists for another's purpose, because it acts in combination; <s>Puruṣa</s> exists for his own purpose. Moreover, because <s>buddhi</s> ascertains all objects and is composed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, being three-<s>guṇa</s>-natured, it is insentient. But <s>Puruṣa</s> is the witness of the <s>guṇas</s> — therefore he is not identical. Then let him be completely different. He is not completely different — why? Because, though pure, he witnesses mental modifications. He witnesses the cognitive [modifications] of <s>buddhi</s>; and witnessing them, though not being of their nature, he appears as if he were of their nature. And thus it is said: 'The power of the experiencer is non-transformative and non-transferring; yet, in a transforming object, as if transferred, it follows its [<s>buddhi</s>'s] activity. And that cognitive activity of <s>buddhi</s>, which has assumed the form of borrowed consciousness — because [the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s>] is merely an imitation of it, the cognitive activity is declared to be indistinguishable from the activity of <s>buddhi</s>.' 2.20

body.text: tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā || YS_2.21 ||
body.translated_text: The nature of the seen exists solely for the sake of that [seer]. || <s>YS</s> 2.21 ||

body.text: dṛśirūpasya puruṣasya karmarūpatām āpannaṃ dṛśyam iti tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā bhavati. svarūpaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. svarūpaṃ tu pararūpeṇa pratilabdhātmakaṃ bhogāpavargārthatāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ puruṣeṇa na dṛśyata iti. svarūpahānād asya nāśaḥ prāpto na tu vinaśyati. 2.21
body.translated_text: The seen, having assumed the character of an object for <s>Puruṣa</s> whose nature is seeing — the nature of the seen exists solely for the sake of that [seer]; its own nature exists [only for that purpose] — this is the meaning. Its own nature, which has acquired its identity through another's form, is not seen by <s>Puruṣa</s> when the purpose of experience and liberation has been accomplished. From the loss of its own form, its destruction is arrived at — yet it does not [truly] perish. 2.21

body.text: kasmāt ---

children.text: kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt || YS_2.22 ||
children.translated_text: Though destroyed for the one whose purpose is fulfilled, it is not destroyed, because it is common to others. || <s>YS</s> 2.22 ||

body.translated_text: Why [does it not perish]?

body.text: kṛtārtham ekaṃ puruṣaṃ prati dṛśyaṃ naṣṭam api nāśaṃ prāptam apy anaṣṭaṃ tadanyapuruṣasādhāraṇatvāt. kuśalaṃ puruṣaṃ prati nāśaṃ prāptam apy akuśalān puruṣān prati na kṛtārtham iti teṣāṃ dṛśeḥ karmaviṣayatām āpannaṃ labhata eva pararūpeṇātmarūpam iti. ataś ca dṛgdarśanaśaktyor nityatvād anādiḥ saṃyogo vyākhyāta iti. tathā coktam --- dharmiṇām anādisaṃyogād dharmamātrāṇām apy anādiḥ saṃyoga iti. 2.22
body.translated_text: For one <s>Puruṣa</s> whose purpose is fulfilled, the seen has reached destruction, yet it is not destroyed — because it is common to other <s>Puruṣas</s>. For a skilled <s>Puruṣa</s>, it has reached destruction, but for unskilled <s>Puruṣas</s> it has not fulfilled its purpose — therefore for them, [the seen], having assumed the character of being the object of seeing, indeed acquires its own form through another's form. And because the powers of seeing and the seen are eternal, the beginningless conjunction has been explained. And thus it is said: 'Because the conjunction of property-bearers is beginningless, the conjunction of mere properties too is beginningless.' 2.22

body.text: saṃyogasvarūpābhidhitsayedaṃ sūtraṃ pravavṛte ---

children.translated_text: Conjunction is the cause of the apprehension of the essential nature of the powers of the owned and the owner. || <s>YS</s> 2.23 ||

body.translated_text: With the intention of describing the essential nature of conjunction, this <s>sūtra</s> proceeds:

body.text:
puruṣaḥ svāmī dṛśyena svena darśanārthaṃ saṃyuktaḥ. tasmāt saṃyogād dṛśyasyopalabdhir yā sa bhogaḥ. yā tu draṣṭuḥ svarūpopalabdhiḥ so 'pavargaḥ. darśanakāryāvasānaḥ saṃyoga iti darśanaṃ viyogasya kāraṇam uktam. darśanam adarśanasya pratidvandvīty adarśanaṃ saṃyoganimittam uktam. nātra darśanaṃ mokṣakāraṇam adarśanābhāvād eva bandhābhāvaḥ sa mokṣa iti. darśanasya bhāve bandhakāraṇasyādarśanasya nāśa ity ato darśanaṃ jñānaṃ kaivalyakāraṇam uktam.
  kiṃcedam adarśanaṃ nāma, kiṃ guṇānām adhikāra āhosvid dṛśirūpasya svāmino darśitaviṣayasya pradhānacittasyānutpādaḥ. svasmin dṛśye vidyamāne yo darśanābhāvaḥ.
  kim arthavattā guṇānām. athāvidyā svacittena saha niruddhā svacittasyotpattibījam. kiṃ sthitisaṃskārakṣaye gatisaṃskārābhivyaktiḥ. yatredam uktaṃ pradhānaṃ sthityaiva vartamānaṃ vikārākaraṇād apradhānaṃ syāt.
  tathā gatyaiva vartamānaṃ vikāranityatvād apradhānaṃ syāt. ubhayathā cāsya vṛttiḥ pradhānavyavahāraṃ labhate nānyathā. kāraṇāntareṣv api kalpiteṣv eva samānaś carcaḥ. darśanaśaktir evādarśanam ity eke, "pradhānasyātmakhyāpanārthā pravṛttiḥ" iti śruteḥ.
  sarvabodhyabodhasamarthaḥ prākpravṛtteḥ puruṣo na paśyati sarvakāryakaraṇasamarthaṃ dṛśyaṃ tadā na dṛśyata iti. ubhayasyāpy adarśanaṃ dharma ity eke. tatredaṃ dṛśyasya svātmabhūtam api puruṣapratyayāpekṣaṃ darśanaṃ dṛśyadharmatvena bhavati. tathā puruṣasyānātmabhūtam api dṛśyapratyayāpekṣaṃ puruṣadharmatvenevādarśanam avabhāsate. darśanaṃ jñānam evādarśanam iti kecid abhidadhati. ity ete śāstragatā vikalpāḥ. tatra vikalpabahutvam etat sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ guṇānāṃ saṃyoge sādhāraṇaviṣayam. 2.23
body.translated_text:
<s>Puruṣa</s>, the owner, is conjoined with the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), which is his own, for the purpose of seeing (<s>darśana</s>). From that conjunction, the perception of the seen — that is <s>bhoga</s> (experience). The perception of the seer's own nature — that is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). The conjunction [ceases] when the purpose of seeing has been fulfilled — thus seeing is stated to be the cause of separation. Seeing is the counterpart of non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>) — thus non-seeing is stated to be the cause of conjunction. Here, seeing is not the cause of liberation; rather, from the very absence of non-seeing, there is the absence of bondage — that is liberation. When seeing exists, the non-seeing that is the cause of bondage is destroyed — therefore seeing, [that is,] knowledge, is stated to be the cause of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation).
What then is this 'non-seeing'? Is it the [continued] functioning of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of <s>prakṛti</s>)? Or is it the non-arising of the <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) and mind that have displayed their object to the seer-natured owner? Is it the absence of seeing when one's own seen [object] exists?
Is it the purposefulness of the <s>guṇas</s>? Or is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), together with one's own mind when it has ceased, the seed for the mind's [re-]arising? Or is it the manifestation of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) of activity upon the destruction of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of stability? Regarding this it is said: <s>pradhāna</s>, existing merely in a state of stability, would become non-primary (<s>apradhāna</s>) through not producing transformations.
Likewise, existing merely in a state of activity, it would become non-primary through the perpetuity of transformations. Its functioning in both ways obtains the designation 'primary' (<s>pradhāna</s>), and not otherwise. Even when other causes are posited, the same discussion applies. 'The power of seeing itself is non-seeing' — [say] some, on the basis of the <s>śruti</s>: 'The activity of <s>pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of revealing the Self.'
Before [its] activity, <s>Puruṣa</s>, capable of knowing all that is to be known, does not see; the seen, capable of producing all effects and instruments, at that time is not seen. Non-seeing is a property of both — [say] some. In this regard: the seeing of the seen, though belonging to its own nature, depends on the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> and exists as a property of the seen. Likewise, the non-seeing of <s>Puruṣa</s>, though not belonging to his own nature, depends on the cognition of the seen and appears as if it were a property of <s>Puruṣa</s>. 'Seeing is knowledge; the very same [in its absence] is non-seeing' — [say] some. These are the various alternatives found in the <s>śāstra</s>. Among them, this multiplicity of alternatives pertains to the common domain — the conjunction of the <s>guṇas</s> with all <s>puruṣas</s>. [YS 2.23]

body.text: yas tu pratyakcetanasya svabuddhisaṃyogaḥ ---
body.translated_text: But the conjunction of the inward-facing consciousness with its own <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) —

body.text: tasya hetur avidyā || YS_2.24 ||
body.translated_text: Its cause is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). || <s>YS</s> 2.24 ||

body.text:
viparyayajñānavāsanety arthaḥ. viparyayajñānavāsanāvāsitā ca na kāryaniṣṭhāṃ puruṣakhyātiṃ buddhiḥ prāpnoti sādhikārā punar āvartate. sā tu puruṣakhyātiparyavasānāṃ kāryaniṣṭhāṃ prāpnoti, caritādhikārā nivṛttādarśanā bandhakāraṇābhāvān na punar āvartate.
  atra kaścit paṇḍakopākhyānenodghāṭayati --- mugdhayā bhāryayābhidhīyate --- paṇḍakāryaputra, apatyavatī me bhaginī kimarthaṃ nāma nāham iti, sa tām āha --- mṛtas te 'ham apatyam utpādayiṣyāmīti. tathedaṃ vidyamānaṃ jñānaṃ cittanivṛttiṃ na karoti, vinaṣṭaṃ kariṣyatīti kā pratyāśā. tatrācāryadeśīyo vakti --- nanu buddhinivṛttir eva mokṣo 'darśanakāraṇābhāvād buddhinivṛttiḥ. tac cādarśanaṃ bandhakāraṇaṃ darśanān nivartate. tatra cittanivṛttir eva mokṣaḥ, kimartham asthāna evāsya mativibhramaḥ. 2.24
body.translated_text:
The meaning is: the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyayajñāna</s>). The <s>buddhi</s> that is pervaded by the <s>vāsanā</s> of erroneous knowledge does not attain the culminating <s>puruṣakhyāti</s> (perception of <s>Puruṣa</s>) and, its function still remaining, revolves again. But that [<s>buddhi</s>] which attains the culminating <s>puruṣakhyāti</s>, having completed its function, with non-seeing removed, does not revolve again due to the absence of the cause of bondage.
Here, someone illustrates with the story of the eunuch — the foolish wife says: 'O son of the eunuch, my sister has children; why should I not?' He replies: 'When I am dead, I shall produce offspring for you.' Just so, existing knowledge does not bring about the cessation of the mind — what hope is there that it will do so when destroyed? To this, one of the rank of teacher says: Indeed, the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> itself is liberation — the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> [comes] from the absence of the cause of non-seeing. And that non-seeing, which is the cause of bondage, ceases through seeing. Therefore, the cessation of the mind itself is liberation — why this confusion of understanding in an inappropriate place? [YS 2.24]

body.text: heyaṃ duḥkhaṃ heyakāraṇaṃ ca saṃyogākhyaṃ sanimittam uktam ataḥ paraṃ hānaṃ vaktavyam ---

children.text: tadabhāvāt saṃyogābhāvo hānaṃ taddṛśeḥ kaivalyam || YS_2.25 ||
children.translated_text: From the absence of that [non-seeing], the absence of conjunction — that is abandonment (<s>hāna</s>). That is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) for the seer. || <s>YS</s> 2.25 ||

body.translated_text: The suffering that is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>) and its cause, called conjunction, together with its cause, have been stated. Now the abandonment (<s>hāna</s>) must be stated —

body.text: tasyādarśanasyābhāvād buddhipuruṣasaṃyogābhāva ātyantiko bandhanoparama ity arthaḥ. etad dhānam. taddṛśeḥ kaivalyaṃ puruṣasyāmiśrībhāvaḥ punar asaṃyogo guṇair ity arthaḥ. duḥkhakāraṇanivṛttau duḥkhoparamo hānam, tadā svarūpapratiṣṭhaḥ puruṣa ity uktam. 2.25
body.translated_text: From the absence of that non-seeing, the absolute cessation of the conjunction of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, the complete cessation of bondage — this is the meaning. This is <s>hāna</s> (abandonment). '<s>Kaivalya</s> of the seer' means the unmixed state of <s>Puruṣa</s> — the non-conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> again — this is the meaning. With the cessation of the cause of suffering, suffering ceases — that is <s>hāna</s>; then <s>Puruṣa</s> is established in his own nature — thus it has been stated. [YS 2.25]

body.text: atha hānasya kaḥ prāptyupāya iti ---

children.translated_text: Unwavering discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is the means of abandonment (<s>hānopāya</s>). || <s>YS</s> 2.26 ||

body.translated_text: Now, what is the means of attaining this abandonment? —

body.text: sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayo vivekakhyātiḥ. sā tv anivṛttamithyājñānā plavate. yadā mithyājñānaṃ dagdhabījabhāvaṃ vandhyaprasavaṃ saṃpadyate tadā vidhūtakleśarajasaḥ sattvasya pare vaiśāradye parasyāṃ vaśīkārasaṃjñāyāṃ vartamānasya vivekapratyayapravāho nirmalo bhavati. sā vivekakhyātir aviplavā hānopāyaḥ. tato mithyājñānasya dagdhabījabhāvopagamaḥ punaś cāprasava ity eṣa mokṣasya mārgo hānasyopāya iti. 2.26
body.translated_text: <s>Vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative perception) is the cognition of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. But when erroneous knowledge has not ceased, it wavers. When erroneous knowledge attains the state of a burned seed, incapable of sprouting, then for <s>sattva</s> whose dust of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) has been shaken off, standing at the highest lucidity (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), in the supreme state called <s>vaśīkāra</s> (mastery), the stream of discriminative cognition becomes pure. That unwavering <s>vivekakhyāti</s> is the means of abandonment. Thereby, erroneous knowledge attains the state of a burned seed and ceases to sprout again — this is the path to liberation, the means of abandonment. [YS 2.26]

body.text: tasya saptadhā prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā || YS_2.27 ||
body.translated_text: For that [yogin], wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) has seven stages at the final ground. || <s>YS</s> 2.27 ||

body.text:
tasyeti pratyuditakhyāteḥ pratyāmnāyaḥ. saptadheti aśuddhyāvaraṇamalāpagamāc cittasya pratyayāntarānutpāde sati saptaprakāraiva prajñā vivekino bhavati.
  tadyathā --- parijñātaṃ heyaṃ nāsya punaḥ parijñeyam asti. kṣīṇā heyahetavo na punar eteṣāṃ kṣetavyam asti. sākṣātkṛtaṃ nirodhasamādhinā hānam. bhāvito vivekakhyātirūpo hānopāya iti. eṣā catuṣṭayī kāryā vimuktiḥ prajñāyāḥ. cittavimuktis tu trayī caritādhikārā buddhiḥ. guṇā giriśikharataṭacyutā iva grāvāṇo niravasthānāḥ svakāraṇe pralayābhimukhāḥ saha tenāstaṃ gacchanti. na caiṣāṃ pravilīnānāṃ punar asty utpādaḥ prayojanābhāvād iti. etasyām avasthāyāṃ guṇasaṃbandhātītaḥ svarūpamātrajyotir amalaḥ kevalī puruṣa iti. etāṃ saptavidhāṃ prāntabhūmiprajñām anupaśyan puruṣaḥ kuśala ity ākhyāyate. pratiprasave 'pi cittasya muktaḥ kuśala ity eva bhavati guṇātītatvād iti. 2.27
body.translated_text:
'For that' refers to the one in whom discriminative perception has arisen. 'Sevenfold': when the impurity and covering defilement of the mind have been removed, and no other cognition arises, the wisdom of the discriminator becomes sevenfold.
Namely: (1) That which is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>) has been fully known — there is nothing more to be known. (2) The causes of what is to be abandoned have been destroyed — there is nothing more to be destroyed. (3) Abandonment has been directly realized through the <s>samādhi</s> of cessation (<s>nirodhasamādhi</s>). (4) The means of abandonment in the form of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> has been cultivated. This is the fourfold liberation pertaining to action (<s>kāryavimukti</s>) of wisdom. The threefold liberation of the mind (<s>cittavimukti</s>) is: (5) <s>Buddhi</s> has completed its function. (6) The <s>guṇas</s>, like boulders fallen from a mountain peak, without foothold, facing dissolution in their cause, vanish along with it. (7) There is no further arising for them once they have dissolved, due to the absence of purpose. In this state, <s>Puruṣa</s>, having transcended the connection with the <s>guṇas</s>, is pure, a mere light of his own nature, undefiled, alone (<s>kevalin</s>). The <s>puruṣa</s> who perceives this sevenfold wisdom of the final ground is called 'proficient' (<s>kuśala</s>). Even in the dissolution of the mind, the liberated one remains proficient, having transcended the <s>guṇas</s>. [YS 2.27]

body.text: siddhā bhavati vivekakhyātir hānopāya iti, na ca siddhir antareṇa sādhanam ity etad ārabhyate ---

children.text: yogāṅgānuṣṭhānād aśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptir ā vivekakhyāteḥ || YS_2.28 ||
children.translated_text: From the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, the light of knowledge [shines forth] up to discriminative perception (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>). || <s>YS</s> 2.28 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative perception), the means of abandonment, is established [as the goal]; but there is no attainment without a means [of practice] — hence this is commenced:

children.text: yogāṅgāny aṣṭāv abhidhāyiṣyamāṇāni. teṣām anuṣṭhānāt pañcaparvaṇo viparyayasyāśuddhirūpasya kṣayo nāśaḥ. tatkṣaye samyagjñānasyābhivyaktiḥ. yathā yathā ca sādhanāny anuṣṭhīyante tathā tathā tanutvam aśuddhir āpadyate. yathā yathā ca kṣīyate tathā tathā kṣayakramānurodhinī jñānasyāpi dīptir vivardhate. sā khalv eṣā vivṛddhiḥ prakarṣam anubhavatyā vivekakhyāteḥ, ā guṇapuruṣasvarūpavijñānād ity arthaḥ. yogāṅgānuṣṭhānam aśuddher viyogakāraṇam. yathā paraśuś chedyasya. vivekakhyātes tu prāptikāraṇaṃ yathā dharmaḥ sukhasya nānyathā kāraṇam. kati caitāni kāraṇāni śāstre bhavanti. navaivety āha. tadyathā ---
children.translated_text: The limbs of <s>yoga</s> are eight, and will be enumerated. From their practice, the destruction, the annihilation, of the fivefold impurity in the form of <s>viparyaya</s> (erroneous perception) [occurs]. Upon its destruction, right knowledge becomes manifest. And as the means are practiced, so impurity progressively becomes attenuated. And as it diminishes, so the light of knowledge, following the order of its diminution, progressively increases. This increase reaches its culmination up to <s>vivekakhyāti</s>, up to the knowledge of the true nature of the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — this is the meaning. The practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s> is the cause of separation from impurity — like an axe is [the cause of separation] from what is to be cut. But it is the cause of attainment of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> — as <s>dharma</s> (merit) is [the cause] of happiness, not otherwise. How many such causes are there in the <s>śāstra</s>? Nine, it is said. Namely —
'Production, stability, manifestation, transformation, cognition, attainment,
separation, alteration, and sustenance — cause is remembered as ninefold.'

body.text:
tatrotpattikāraṇaṃ mano bhavati vijñānasya, sthitikāraṇaṃ manasaḥ puruṣārthatā, śarīrasyevāhāra iti. abhivyaktikāraṇaṃ yathā rūpasyālokas tathā rūpajñānam, vikārakāraṇaṃ manaso viṣayāntaram. yathāgniḥ pākyasya. pratyayakāraṇaṃ dhūmajñānam agnijñānasya. prāptikāraṇaṃ yogāṅgānuṣṭhānaṃ vivekakhyāteḥ.
  viyogakāraṇaṃ tad evāśuddheḥ. anyatvakāraṇaṃ yathā suvarṇasya suvarṇakāraḥ. evam ekasya strīpratyayasyāvidyā mūḍhatve dveṣo duḥkhatve rāgaḥ sukhatve tattvajñānaṃ mādhyasthye. dhṛtikāraṇaṃ śarīram indriyāṇām. tāni ca tasya. mahābhūtāni śarīrāṇām, tāni ca parasparaṃ sarveṣāṃ tairyagyaunamānuṣadaivatāni ca parasparārthatvād ity evaṃ nava kāraṇāni. tāni ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ padārthāntareṣv api yojyāni. yogāṅgānuṣṭhānaṃ tu dvidhaiva kāraṇatvaṃ labhata iti. 2.28
body.translated_text:
Among these: the cause of production — mind is [the cause of production] of cognition. The cause of stability — for the mind, it is serving <s>Puruṣa's</s> purpose, as food is for the body. The cause of manifestation — as light [manifests] form, so [knowledge manifests] cognition of form. The cause of transformation — a different object [transforms] the mind, as fire [transforms] what is to be cooked. The cause of cognition — knowledge of smoke is [the cause of] knowledge of fire. The cause of attainment — the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s> is [the cause of attainment of] <s>vivekakhyāti</s>.
The cause of separation — the same [practice] is [the cause of separation] from impurity. The cause of alteration — as a goldsmith [is the cause of alteration] of gold; so, for a single cognition pertaining to a woman, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) [produces] delusion, <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) [arises] regarding suffering, <s>rāga</s> (attachment) regarding pleasure, and <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) [produces] equanimity. The cause of sustenance — the body [sustains] the sense organs, and they [sustain] it. The great elements [sustain] bodies, and they sustain each other. [Bodies] of animals, humans, and gods all serve mutual purposes — thus there are nine causes. These should be applied to other categories as appropriate. The practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s> obtains a twofold causality. [YS 2.28]

body.text: tatra yogāṅgāny avadhāryante ---

children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), <s>āsana</s> (posture), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) — these are the eight limbs. || <s>YS</s> 2.29 ||

children.text: yathākramam eṣām anuṣṭhānaṃ svarūpaṃ ca vakṣyāmaḥ. 2.29
children.translated_text: We shall explain their practice and nature in order. [YS 2.29]

body.translated_text: There, the limbs of <s>yoga</s> are determined —

body.text: tatra ---

children.translated_text: Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>) are the restraints (<s>yamas</s>). (YS 2.30)

body.translated_text: Among these —

body.text:
tatrāhiṃsā sarvathā sarvadā sarvabhūtānām anabhidrohaḥ. uttare ca yamaniyamās tanmūlās tatsiddhiparatayaiva tatpratipādanāya pratipādyante. tadavadātarūpakaraṇāyaivopādīyante. tathā coktam --- sa khalv ayaṃ brāhmaṇo yathā yathā vratāni bahūni samāditsate tathā tathā pramādakṛtebhyo hiṃsānidānebhyo nivartamānas tām evāvadātarūpām ahiṃsāṃ karoti.
  satyaṃ yathārthe vāṅmanase. yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathānumitaṃ tathā vāṅ manaś ceti. paratra svabodhasaṃkrāntaye vāg uktā, sā yadi na vañcitā bhrāntā vā pratipattivandhyā vā bhaved iti. eṣā sarvabhūtopakārārthaṃ pravṛttā na bhūtopaghātāya. yadi caivam apy abhidhīyamānā bhūtopaghātaparaiva syān na satyaṃ bhavet pāpam eva bhavet tena puṇyābhāsena puṇyapratirūpakeṇa kaṣṭaṃ tamaḥ prāpnuyāt. tasmāt parīkṣya sarvabhūtahitaṃ satyaṃ brūyāt.
  steyam aśāstrapūrvakaṃ dravyāṇāṃ parataḥ svīkaraṇaṃ, tatpratiṣedhaḥ punar aspṛhārūpam asteyam iti. brahmacaryaṃ guptendriyasyopasthasya saṃyamaḥ. viṣayāṇām arjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṃsādoṣadarśanād asvīkaraṇam aparigraha ity ete yamāḥ. 2.30
body.translated_text: Among these, non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is the absence of hostility toward all beings, in all ways, at all times. The subsequent restraints and observances (<s>yama-niyamas</s>), having their root in that [non-violence] and being directed toward its perfection, are taught for the purpose of establishing it. They are adopted for the purpose of making it pure in form. And thus it has been said: 'This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> undertakes many vows in order that,

body.text: te tu ---

children.translated_text: When not limited by class (<s>jāti</s>), place (<s>deśa</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), or circumstance (<s>samaya</s>), [the restraints] are universal [and constitute] the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>). (YS 2.31)

body.translated_text: they, however —

body.text: tatrāhiṃsā jātyavacchinnā matsyavadhakasya matsyeṣv eva nānyatra hiṃsā. saiva deśāvacchinnā na tīrthe haniṣyāmīti. saiva kālāvacchinnā na caturdaśyāṃ na puṇye 'hani haniṣyāmīti. saiva tribhir uparatasya samayāvacchinnā devabrāhmaṇārthe nānyathā haniṣyāmīti. yathā ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ yuddha eva hiṃsā nānyatreti. ebhir jātideśakālasamayair anavacchinnā ahiṃsādayaḥ sarvathaiva paripālanīyāḥ. sarvabhūmiṣu sarvaviṣayeṣu sarvathaivāviditavyabhicārāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam ity ucyante. 2.31
body.translated_text: Among these, non-violence limited by class: a fisherman's violence is only toward fish, not elsewhere. The same, limited by place: 'I shall not kill at a sacred ford.' The same, limited by time: 'I shall not kill on the fourteenth day of the lunar fortnight, nor on an auspicious day.' The same, limited by circumstance, when one has desisted from the [first] three: 'I shall kill only for the sake of gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, not otherwise.'

body.text: śaucasaṃtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ || YS_2.32 ||
body.translated_text: Purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to the Lord (<s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>) are the observances (<s>niyamas</s>). (YS 2.32)

children.text: tatra śaucaṃ mṛjjalādijanitaṃ medhyābhyavaharaṇādi ca bāhyam. ābhyantaraṃ cittamalānām ākṣālanam. saṃtoṣaḥ saṃnihitasādhanād adhikasyānupāditsā. tapo dvaṃdvasahanam. dvaṃdvāś ca jighatsāpipāse śītoṣṇe sthānāsane kāṣṭhamaunākāramaune ca. vratāni caiṣāṃ yathāyogaṃ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇasāṃtapanādīni. svādhyāyo mokṣaśāstrāṇām adhyayanaṃ praṇavajapo vā. īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ tasmin paramagurau sarvakarmārpaṇam.
children.translated_text: Among these, external purity is that produced by earth, water, and the like, and the eating of pure food, and so forth. Internal [purity] is the cleansing of the impurities of the mind. Contentment is the absence of desire to acquire more than the means at hand. Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the endurance of opposites (<s>dvandva</s>). The opposites are: hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, silence of [mere] wood and silence of [verbal] form. And the observances (<s>vrata</s>) [are described thus] —

children.text: śayyāsanastho 'tha pathi vrajan vā svasthaḥ parikṣīṇavitarkajālaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Whether seated on a bed or a seat, or walking on a path,
self-possessed, with the net of discursive thoughts exhausted,

seeing the destruction of the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
let him be ever yoked [in yoga], partaking of the immortal enjoyment.

body.text: yatredam uktaṃ tataḥ pratyakcetanādhigamo 'py antarāyābhāvaś ceti. 2.32
body.translated_text: Here it is said: 'From that [comes] also the realization of the inward-directed consciousness, and also the absence of obstacles.' (2.32)

body.text: eteṣāṃ yamaniyamānām ---

children.translated_text: When disturbed by discursive thoughts (<s>vitarka</s>), [one should practice] the cultivation of the opposite (<s>pratipakṣabhāvana</s>). (YS 2.33)

body.translated_text: For these restraints and observances —

body.text: yadāsya brāhmaṇasya hiṃsādayo vitarkā jāyeran haniṣyāmy aham apakāriṇam anṛtam api vakṣyāmi dravyam apy asya svīkariṣyāmi dāreṣu cāsya vyavāyī bhaviṣyāmi parigraheṣu cāsya svāmī bhaviṣyāmīti. evam unmārgapravaṇavitarkajvareṇātidīptena bādhyamānas tatpratipakṣān bhāvayet. ghoreṣu saṃsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā śaraṇam upāgataḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradānena yogadharmaḥ. sa khalv ahaṃ tyaktvā vitarkān punas tān ādadānas tulyaḥ śvavṛtteneti bhāvayet. yathā śvā vāntāvalehī tathā tyaktasya punar ādadāna iti. evamādi sūtrāntareṣv api yojyam. 2.33
body.translated_text: When discursive thoughts of violence and the like arise in this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — 'I shall kill this person who has harmed me; I shall speak falsehood too; I shall appropriate this person's property; I shall have intercourse with his wife; I shall become the owner of his possessions' — thus, being afflicted by the greatly blazing fever of discursive thoughts inclined toward the wrong path, at that time [he should cultivate the opposite].

body.text: vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam || YS_2.34 ||
body.translated_text: Discursive thoughts of violence and the like — whether performed, caused to be performed, or approved — preceded by greed, anger, or delusion, whether mild, moderate, or intense — [all] bear the fruit of endless suffering and ignorance; thus one should cultivate the opposite. (YS 2.34)

body.text:
tatra hiṃsā tāvat --- kṛtā kāritānumoditeti tridhā. ekaikā punas tridhā lobhena māṃsacarmārthena krodhenāpakṛtam aneneti mohena dharmo me bhaviṣyatīti. lobhakrodhamohāḥ punas trividhā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā iti. evaṃ saptaviṃśatir bhedā bhavanti hiṃsāyāḥ. mṛdumadhyādhimātrāḥ punas tridhā --- mṛdumṛdur madhyamṛdus tīvramṛdur iti. tathā mṛdumadhyo madhyamadhyas tīvramadhya iti. tathā mṛdutīvro madhyatīvro 'dhimātratīvra iti. evam ekāśītibhedā hiṃsā bhavati. sā punar niyamavikalpasamuccayabhedād asaṃkhyeyā, prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvād iti. evam anṛtādiṣv api yojyam.
  te khalv amī vitarkā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam. duḥkham ajñānaṃ cānantaṃ phalaṃ yeṣām iti pratipakṣabhāvanam. tathā ca hiṃsakas tāvat prathamaṃ vadhyasya vīryam ākṣipati. tataś ca śastrādinipātena duḥkhayati. tato jīvitād api mocayati. tato vīryākṣepād asya cetanācetanam upakaraṇaṃ kṣīṇavīryaṃ bhavati. duḥkhotpādān narakatiryakpretādiṣu duḥkham anubhavati, jīvitavyaparopaṇāt pratikṣaṇaṃ ca jīvitātyaye vartamāno maraṇam icchann api duḥkhavipākasya niyatavipākavedanīyatvāt kathaṃcid evocchvasiti. yadi ca kathaṃcit puṇyāvāpagatā hiṃsā bhavet tatra sukhaprāptau bhaved alpāyur iti. evam anṛtādiṣv api yojyaṃ yathāsaṃbhavam. evaṃ vitarkāṇāṃ cāmum evānugataṃ vipākam aniṣṭaṃ bhāvayan na vitarkeṣu manaḥ praṇidadhīta. 2.34
body.translated_text: Among these, violence first: it is threefold as performed, caused to be performed, and approved. Each of these is again threefold: through greed — for the sake of meat or hide; through anger — 'this one has harmed me'; through delusion — 'this will be meritorious for me.' Greed, anger, and delusion are each again threefold: mild, moderate, and intense. Thus there are twenty-seven divisions of violence.

body.text: pratipakṣabhāvanād dhetor heyā vitarkā yadāsya syur aprasavadharmāṇas tadā tatkṛtam aiśvaryaṃ yoginaḥ siddhisūcakaṃ bhavati. tadyathā ---

children.translated_text: When one is established in non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), in one's presence there is the abandonment of hostility [by all beings]. (YS 2.35)

body.translated_text: Through the cultivation of the opposite, the discursive thoughts that are to be abandoned — when they become incapable of producing [results] — then the mastery produced by that becomes the indicator of the <s>yogin's</s> spiritual attainments (<s>siddhi</s>). Namely:

body.text: sarvaprāṇināṃ bhavati. 2.35
body.translated_text: [This occurs] for all living beings. (2.35)

body.text: satyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kriyāphalāśrayatvam || YS_2.36 ||
body.translated_text: When one is established in truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), actions and their fruits become dependent [on one's words]. (YS 2.36)

body.text: dhārmiko bhūyā iti bhavati dhārmikaḥ, svargaṃ prāpnuhīti svargaṃ prāpnoti amoghāsya vāg bhavati. 2.36
body.translated_text: 'May you become righteous' — and one becomes righteous. 'May you attain heaven' — and one attains heaven. One's speech becomes infallible. (2.36)

body.text: asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ sarvaratnopasthānam || YS_2.37 ||
body.translated_text: When one is established in non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), all jewels present themselves. (YS 2.37)

body.text: sarvadiksthāny asyopatiṣṭhante ratnāni. 2.37
body.translated_text: Jewels situated in all directions present themselves to him. (2.37)

body.text: brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṃ vīryalābhaḥ || YS_2.38 ||
body.translated_text: When one is established in celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), [there is] the acquisition of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). (YS 2.38)

body.text: yasya lābhād apratighān guṇān utkarṣayati. siddhaś ca vineyeṣu jñānam ādhātuṃ samartho bhavatīti. 2.38
body.translated_text: From that acquisition, one develops irresistible qualities to their highest degree. And having attained perfection, one becomes capable of imparting knowledge to those who are to be trained. (2.38)

body.text: aparigrahasthairye janmakathaṃtāsaṃbodhaḥ || YS_2.39 ||
body.translated_text: When one is firm in non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>), [there arises] the knowledge of the 'how' and 'wherefore' of births. (YS 2.39)

body.text: asya bhavati ko 'ham āsaṃ katham aham āsaṃ kiṃsvid idaṃ kathaṃsvid idaṃ ke vā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kathaṃ vā bhaviṣyāma ity evam asya pūrvāntaparāntamadhyeṣv ātmabhāvajijāsā svarūpeṇopāvartate. etā yamasthairye siddhayaḥ. 2.39
body.translated_text: For him there arises [the knowledge]: 'Who was I? How was I? What is this? How is this? What shall we become? How shall we become?' — thus his desire to know the self regarding the past, future, and intermediate states of existence presents itself in its true form. These are the attainments from firmness in the restraints. (2.39)

body.text: niyameṣu vakṣyāmaḥ ---

children.translated_text: From purity (<s>śauca</s>) [comes] aversion toward one's own body and non-contact with others. (YS 2.40)

body.translated_text: Regarding the observances (<s>niyama</s>), we shall speak:

body.text: svāṅge jugupsāyāṃ śaucam ārabhamāṇaḥ kāyāvadyadarśī kāyānabhiṣvaṅgī yatir bhavati. kiṃca parair asaṃsargaḥ kāyasvabhāvāvalokī svam api kāyaṃ jihāsur mṛjjalādibhir ākṣālayann api kāyaśuddhim apaśyan kathaṃ parakāyair atyantam evāprayataiḥ saṃsṛjyeta. 2.40
body.translated_text: When aversion toward one's own body [arises], one beginning the practice of purity, seeing the faults of the body, and having no attachment to the body, becomes a renunciant. Furthermore, 'non-contact with others' — seeing the true nature of the body, wishing to abandon even one's own body, and not seeing bodily purity even while cleansing with earth and water — how then would one associate with the bodies of others, which are exceedingly impure? (2.40)

body.text: kiṃca ---

children.translated_text: And [there arise] purity of <s>sattva</s> (being), cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery over the senses, and fitness for the vision of the self. (YS 2.41)

body.translated_text: Furthermore —

body.text: bhavantīti vākyaśeṣaḥ. śuceḥ sattvaśuddhis tataḥ saumanasyaṃ tata aikāgryaṃ tata indriyajayas tataś cātmadarśanayogyatvaṃ buddhisattvasya bhavatīty etac chaucasthairyād adhigamyata iti. 2.41
body.translated_text: 'They arise' — this completes the sentence. From purity comes purity of <s>sattva</s> (being); from that, cheerfulness; from that, one-pointedness; from that, mastery over the senses; from that, fitness for the vision of the self — of the <s>buddhisattva</s> (the being of intellect). This is attained through firmness in purity. (2.41)

body.text: saṃtoṣād anuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ || YS_2.42 ||
body.translated_text: From contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), [there is] the attainment of unsurpassed happiness. (YS 2.42)

body.text: tathā coktam ---
body.translated_text: And thus it has been said:

body.text: "yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham /
body.translated_text: 'Whatever sensual happiness there is in the world, and whatever great divine happiness —

body.text: tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām" iti. 2.42
body.translated_text: these are not worth a sixteenth part of the happiness of the cessation of craving.' (2.42)

body.text: kāyendriyasiddhir aśuddhikṣayāt tapasaḥ || YS_2.43 ||
body.translated_text: Perfection of the body and senses comes from the destruction of impurity through austerity (<s>tapas</s>). (YS 2.43)

body.text: nirvartyamānam eva tapo hinasty aśuddhyāvaraṇamalaṃ tadāvaraṇamalāpagamāt kāyasiddhir aṇimādyā. tathendriyasiddhir dūrāc chravaṇadarśanādyeti. 2.43
body.translated_text: Austerity, even as it is being performed, destroys the impurity, covering, and stain (<s>aśuddhyāvaraṇamala</s>). From the removal of that covering and stain come the perfections of the body — such as <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) and others. Likewise come the perfections of the senses — hearing and seeing from afar, and so on. (2.43)

body.text: svādhyāyād iṣṭadevatāsaṃprayogaḥ || YS_2.44 ||
body.translated_text: From self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) comes union with the desired deity. (YS 2.44)

body.text: devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhāś ca svādhyāyaśīlasya darśanaṃ gacchanti, kārye cāsya vartanta iti. 2.44
body.translated_text: Gods, sages, and perfected beings come into the presence of one devoted to self-study, and they engage in his work. (2.44)

body.text: samādhisiddhir īśvarapraṇidhānāt || YS_2.45 ||
body.translated_text: The perfection of <s>samādhi</s> comes from devotion to the Lord (<s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>). (YS 2.45)

body.text: īśvarārpitasarvabhāvasya samādhisiddhir yayā sarvam īpsitam avitathaṃ jānāti deśāntare dehāntare kālāntare ca. tato 'sya prajñā yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. 2.45
body.translated_text: For one who has offered all his states of being to the Lord, the perfection of <s>samādhi</s> arises, by which he knows everything desired, without error, in another place, another body, and another time. Thereby his wisdom knows things as they truly are. (2.45)

body.text: uktāḥ saha siddhibhir yamaniyamāḥ āsanādīni vakṣyāmaḥ tatra ---

children.translated_text: Posture (<s>āsana</s>) is that which is steady and comfortable. (YS 2.46)

body.translated_text: The <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> have been explained along with their perfections. We shall now expound <s>āsana</s> and the rest. Among these —

body.text: tadyathā padmāsanaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ svastikaṃ daṇḍāsanaṃ sopāśrayaṃ paryaṅkaṃ krauñcaniṣadanaṃ hastiniṣadanam uṣṭraniṣadanaṃ samasaṃsthānaṃ sthirasukhaṃ yathāsukhaṃ cety evamādīni. 2.46
body.translated_text: Such as <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), <s>bhadrāsana</s> (auspicious posture), <s>svastika</s> (cross-legged posture), <s>daṇḍāsana</s> (staff posture), <s>sopāśraya</s> (supported posture), <s>paryaṅka</s> (couch posture), <s>krauñcaniṣadana</s> (heron-seated posture), <s>hastiniṣadana</s> (elephant-seated posture), <s>uṣṭraniṣadana</s> (camel-seated posture), <s>samasaṃsthāna</s> (even posture), the steady-and-comfortable, the comfortable-as-one-pleases, and so on. (2.46)

body.text: prayatnaśaithilyānantasamāpattibhyām || YS_2.47 ||
body.translated_text: [Posture is perfected] by the relaxation of effort and by absorption in the infinite (<s>ananta</s>). (YS 2.47)

body.text: bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ prayatnoparamāt sidhyaty āsanaṃ yena nāṅgamejayo bhavati. anante vā samāpannaṃ cittam āsanaṃ nirvartayatīti. 2.47
body.translated_text: 'It comes about' — this is the completion of the sentence. By the cessation of effort, the posture is perfected, whereby there is no trembling of the limbs. Or, the mind absorbed in the infinite (<s>Ananta</s>) brings about the posture. (2.47)

body.text: tato dvandvānabhighātaḥ || YS_2.48 ||
body.translated_text: From that, there is no assault by the pairs of opposites. (YS 2.48)

body.text: śītoṣṇādibhir dvandvair āsanajayān nābhibhūyate. 2.48
body.translated_text: Through mastery of posture, one is not overcome by the pairs of opposites such as heat and cold. (2.48)

body.text: tasmin sati śvāsapraśvāsayor gativicchedaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ || YS_2.49 ||
body.translated_text: When that [posture] is accomplished, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is the regulation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. (YS 2.49)

body.text: saty āsanajaye bāhyasya vāyor ācamanaṃ śvāsaḥ, kauṣṭhyasya vāyor niḥsāraṇaṃ praśvāsaḥ, tayor gativiccheda ubhayābhāvaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ. 2.49
body.translated_text: When posture has been mastered, inhalation (<s>śvāsa</s>) is the drawing in of external air; exhalation (<s>praśvāsa</s>) is the expulsion of internal air. The regulation of their movement — the absence of both — is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. (2.49)

body.text: sa tu ---

children.translated_text: has three modes: external, internal, and suspended; it is regulated by place, time, and number, and becomes long and subtle. (YS 2.50)

children.text: yatra praśvāsapūrvako gatyabhāvaḥ sa bāhyaḥ. yatra śvāsapūrvako gatyabhāvaḥ sa ābhyantaraḥ. tṛtīyaḥ stambhavṛttir yatrobhayābhāvaḥ sakṛṭprayatnād bhavati. yathā tapte nyastam upale jalaṃ sarvataḥ saṃkocam āpadyate tathā dvayor yugapad gatyabhāva iti. trayo 'py ete deśena paridṛṣṭā iyān asya viṣayo deśa iti. kālena paridṛṣṭāḥ kṣaṇānām iyattāvadhāraṇenāvacchinnā ity arthaḥ. saṃkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭā etāvadbhiḥ śvāsapraśvāsaiḥ prathama udghātas tadvan nigṛhītasyaitāvadbhir dvitīya udghāta evaṃ tṛtīyaḥ. evaṃ mṛdur evaṃ madhya evaṃ tīvra iti saṃkhyāparidṛṣṭaḥ. sa khalv ayam evam abhyasto dīrghasūkṣmaḥ. 2.50
children.translated_text: Where there is cessation of movement preceded by exhalation, that is external. Where there is cessation of movement preceded by inhalation, that is internal. The third is the suspended mode, where both are absent, occurring by a single effort. Just as water placed on a heated stone contracts from all sides, so both movements cease simultaneously. All three are also regulated by place — 'this is its range' —

body.translated_text: Moreover, that [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] —

body.text: bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepī caturthaḥ || YS_2.51 ||
body.translated_text: The fourth [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] transcends the domain of external and internal. (YS 2.51)

body.text: deśakālasaṃkhyābhir bāhyaviṣayaparidṛṣṭa ākṣiptaḥ. tathābhyantaraviṣayaparidṛṣṭa ākṣiptaḥ. ubhayathā dīrghasūkṣmaḥ. tatpūrvako bhūmijayāt krameṇobhayor gatyabhāvaś caturthaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ. tṛtīyas tu viṣayānālocito gatyabhāvaḥ sakṛdārabdha eva deśakālasaṃkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ. caturthas tu śvāsapraśvāsayor viṣayāvadhāraṇāt krameṇa bhūmijayād ubhayākṣepapūrvako gatyabhāvaś caturthaḥ prāṇāyāma ity ayaṃ viśeṣa iti. 2.51
body.translated_text: The external domain, regulated by place, time, and number, is transcended. Likewise, the internal domain, regulated [by place, time, and number], is transcended. In both ways, it becomes long and subtle. Based on the preceding [three], through progressive mastery of stages, the cessation of both movements is the fourth <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. The third, however, is a cessation of movement without consideration of the domains, begun all at once, yet regulated by place, time, and number, becoming long and subtle. But the fourth —

body.text: tataḥ kṣīyate prakāśāvaraṇam || YS_2.52 ||
body.translated_text: From that, the covering of light is diminished. (YS 2.52)

body.text: prāṇāyāmān abhyasyato 'sya yoginaḥ kṣīyate vivekajñānāvaraṇīyaṃ karma. yat tad ācakṣate. mahāmohamayenendrajālena prakāśaśīlaṃ sattvam āvṛtya tad evākārye niyuṅkta iti. tad asya prakāśāvaraṇaṃ karma saṃsāranibandhanaṃ prāṇāyāmābhyāsād durbalaṃ bhavati pratikṣaṇaṃ ca kṣīyate. tathā coktam. "tapo na paraṃ prāṇāyāmāt tato viśuddhir malānāṃ dīptiś ca jñānasya" iti. 2.52
body.translated_text: For the <s>yogin</s> practicing <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, the <s>karma</s> that obscures discriminative knowledge is diminished. As they say: the <s>sattva</s> (pure intelligence), whose nature is illumination, is covered by a veil of great delusion like a magic trick, and that very [<s>sattva</s>] is then employed in improper activity. That <s>karma</s>, which obscures light and binds to <s>saṃsāra</s>, becomes weakened through the practice of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> and is diminished moment by moment. As it has been said: 'No austerity surpasses —'

body.text: kiṃca ---

children.translated_text: And the mind becomes fit for concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>). (YS 2.53)

body.translated_text: Furthermore —

body.text: prāṇāyāmābhyāsād eva "pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṃ vā prāṇasya" iti vacanāt. 2.53
body.translated_text: This follows from the practice of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> alone, as stated: 'Or by the expulsion and retention of breath.' (2.53)

body.text: atha kaḥ pratyāhāraḥ ---

children.translated_text: When disconnected from their own objects, the senses conforming, as it were, to the nature of the mind — that is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses). (YS 2.54)

body.translated_text: Now, what is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses)?

body.text: svaviṣayasaṃprayogābhāve cittasvarūpānukāra iveti, cittanirodhe cittavanniruddhānīndriyāṇi netarendriyajayavadupāyāntaram apekṣante. yathā madhukararājaṃ makṣikā utpatantam anūtpatanti niviśamānam anu niviśante tathendriyāṇi cittanirodhe niruddhānīty eṣa pratyāhāraḥ. 2.54
body.translated_text: In the absence of connection with their respective objects, the senses conform, as it were, to the nature of the mind. When the mind is restrained, the senses are restrained like the mind, without requiring any other means as in other methods of sense-control. Just as bees follow the queen bee when she flies and settle when she settles, so the senses are restrained when the mind is restrained — this is <s>pratyāhāra</s>. (2.54)

body.text: tataḥ paramā vaśyatendriyāṇām || YS_2.55 ||
body.translated_text: From that comes the supreme mastery of the senses. (YS 2.55)

body.text: śabdādiṣv avyasanam indriyajaya iti kecit. saktir vyasanaṃ vyasyaty enaṃ śreyasa iti. aviruddhā pratipattir nyāyyā. śabdādisaṃprayogaḥ svecchayety anye. rāgadveṣābhāve sukhaduḥkhaśūnyaṃ śabdādijñānam indriyajaya iti kecit. cittaikāgryād apratipattir eveti jaigīṣavyaḥ. tataś ca paramā tv iyaṃ vaśyatā yac cittanirodhe niruddhānīndriyāṇi netarendriyajayavat prayatnakṛtam upāyāntaram apekṣante yogina iti. 2.55
body.translated_text: Some say: the conquest of the senses is non-attachment to sounds and other objects. Attachment is passion — it casts one away from the good. The non-contradictory understanding is proper. Others say: contact with sounds and the like occurs only at one's own will. Some say: the conquest of the senses is knowledge of sounds and the like, devoid of pleasure and pain, in the absence of attachment and aversion. <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> [holds]: through one-pointedness of mind, there is simply non-apprehension. And this is the supreme mastery —

body.text:
iti śrīpātāñjale sāṃkhyapravacane yogaśāstre śrīmadvyāsabhāṣye dvitīyaḥ sādhanapādaḥ 2.
uktāni pañca bahiraṅgāni(ṇi) sādhanāni. dhāraṇā vaktavyā ---

children.translated_text: Concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) is the binding of the mind to a place. (YS 3.1)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, the <s>Sādhanapāda</s>, in the venerable <s>Vyāsa</s>'s commentary on the <s>Yoga Śāstra</s>, the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana</s> of <s>Patañjali</s>. (2) The five external means of practice have been described. <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is now to be explained —

body.text: nābhicakre hṛdayapuṇḍarīke mūrdhni jyotiṣi nāsikāgre jihvāgra ity evamādiṣu deśeṣu bāhye vā viṣaye cittasya vṛttimātreṇa bandha iti dhāraṇā. 3.1
body.translated_text: In such places as the navel center, the heart-lotus, the light at the crown of the head, the tip of the nose, the tip of the tongue, and so forth, or upon an external object — the binding of the mind through its mere activity is <s>dhāraṇā</s>. (3.1)

body.text: tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam || YS_3.2 ||
body.translated_text: Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is the continuous flow of cognition toward that [object]. (YS 3.2)

body.text: tasmin deśe dhyeyālambanasya pratyayasyaikatānatā sadṛśaḥ pravāhaḥ pratyayāntareṇāparāmṛṣṭo dhyānam. 3.2
body.translated_text: In that place, the continuity of the cognition of the object of meditation — a homogeneous flow, uninterrupted by any other cognition — is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (3.2)

body.text: tad evārthamātranirbhāsaṃ svarūpaśūnyam iva samādhiḥ || YS_3.3 ||
body.translated_text: That very [meditation], when it shines forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s>. (YS 3.3)

body.text: dhyānam eva dhyeyākārānirbhāsaṃ pratyayātmakena svarūpeṇa śūnyam iva yadā bhavati dhyeyasvabhāvāveśāt tadā samādhir ity ucyate. 3.3
body.translated_text: When meditation itself, appearing in the form of the object of meditation, becomes as if empty of its own nature as a cognition, through absorption in the essential nature of the object of meditation — then it is called <s>samādhi</s>. (3.3)

body.text: trayam ekatra saṃyamaḥ || YS_3.4 ||
body.translated_text: The three together [upon a single object] constitute <s>saṃyama</s>. (YS 3.4)

body.text: tad etad dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayam ekatra saṃyamaḥ. ekaviṣayāṇi trīṇi sādhanāni saṃyama ity ucyate. tad asya trayasya tāntrikī paribhāṣā saṃyama iti. 3.4
body.translated_text: This triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> taken together upon a single object is <s>saṃyama</s>. The three means directed toward a single object are called <s>saṃyama</s>. This is the technical term of the system: <s>saṃyama</s>. (3.4)

body.text: tajjayāt prajñālokaḥ || YS_3.5 ||
body.translated_text: From the mastery of that [<s>saṃyama</s>] comes the radiance of wisdom. (YS 3.5)

body.text: tasya saṃyamasya jayāt samādhiprajñāyā bhavaty āloko yathā yathā saṃyamaḥ sthirapado bhavati tathā tathā samādhiprajñā viśāradī bhavati. 3.5
body.translated_text: From the mastery of that <s>saṃyama</s>, the light of the wisdom born of <s>samādhi</s> arises. The more firmly established the <s>saṃyama</s> becomes, the more proficient becomes the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>. (3.5)

body.text: tasya bhūmiṣu viniyogaḥ || YS_3.6 ||
body.translated_text: Its application is in stages. (YS 3.6)

body.text: tasya saṃyamasya jitabhūmer yānantarā bhūmis tatra viniyogaḥ. na hy ajitādharabhūmir anantarabhūmiṃ vilaṅghya prāntabhūmiṣu saṃyamaṃ labhate. tadabhāvāc ca kutas tasya prajñālokaḥ. īśvaraprasādāj jitottarabhūmikasya ca nādharabhūmiṣu paracittajñānādiṣu saṃyamo yuktaḥ. kasmāt, tadarthasyānyata evāvagatatvāt. bhūmer asyā iyam anantarā bhūmir ity atra yoga evopādhyāyaḥ. katham evaṃ hy uktam. "yogena yogo jñātavyo yogo yogāt pravartate / yo 'pramattas tu yogena sa yoge ramate ciram" iti. 3.6
body.translated_text: The application of that <s>saṃyama</s> should be to the stage immediately following the one that has been conquered. For one who has not conquered the lower stage cannot leap over the next stage to practice <s>saṃyama</s> on the higher stages. And without that, where would his radiance of wisdom come from? However, for one who has conquered the higher stages by the grace of the Lord, <s>saṃyama</s> on the lower stages — such as knowledge of others' minds — is not appropriate. Why? Because that purpose is already known from another [source] —

body.text: trayam antaraṅgaṃ pūrvebhyaḥ || YS_3.7 ||
