body.translated_text: The three [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>] are internal limbs compared to the preceding ones. (YS 3.7)

body.text: tad etad dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayam antaraṅgaṃ saṃprajñātasya samādheḥ pūrvebhyo yamādibhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ sādhanebhya iti. 3.7
body.translated_text: This triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> is internal in relation to <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s>, compared to the preceding five means beginning with <s>yama</s>. (3.7)

body.text: tad api bahiraṅgaṃ nirbījasya || YS_3.8 ||
body.translated_text: But even those are external in relation to the seedless [<s>samādhi</s>]. (YS 3.8)

body.text: tad apy antaraṅgaṃ sādhanatrayaṃ nirbījasya yogasya bahiraṅgaṃ bhavati kasmāt, tadabhāve bhāvād iti. 3.8
body.translated_text: Even that triad, which is the internal means, becomes external in relation to seedless <s>yoga</s>. Why? Because it exists in its absence. (3.8)

body.text: atha nirodhacittakṣaṇeṣu calaṃ guṇavṛttam iti kīdṛśas tadā cittapariṇāmaḥ ---

children.translated_text: The transformation of cessation (<s>nirodhapariṇāma</s>) is the connection of the mind with the moment of cessation, wherein the impression of emergence is overpowered and the impression of cessation manifests. (YS 3.9)

children.text: vyutthānasaṃskārāś cittadharmā na te pratyayātmakā iti pratyayanirodhe na niruddhā nirodhasaṃskārā api cittadharmās tayor abhibhavaprādurbhāvau vyutthānasaṃskārā hīyante nirodhasaṃskārā ādhīyante. nirodhakṣaṇaṃ cittam anveti tad ekasya cittasya pratikṣaṇam idaṃ saṃskārānyathātvaṃ nirodhapariṇāmaḥ. tadā saṃskāraśeṣaṃ cittam iti nirodhasamādhau vyākhyātam. 3.9
children.translated_text: The impressions of emergence (<s>vyutthānasaṃskāra</s>) are properties of the mind, not of the cognitive content itself; therefore, when the cognitive content is ceased, they are not [automatically] ceased. The impressions of cessation (<s>nirodhasaṃskāra</s>) are also properties of the mind. The suppression and manifestation of these two [occur as follows]: the emergence-impressions diminish and the cessation-impressions increase. The moment of cessation pervades the mind. This moment-by-moment alteration of impressions in a single mind is the cessation-transformation (<s>nirodhapariṇāma</s>). Then the mind has only impressions remaining — as explained in connection with the <s>samādhi</s> of cessation. 3.9

body.translated_text: Now, since the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is in flux during the moments of the restrained mind, what is the transformation of the mind at that time?

body.text: tasya praśāntavāhitā saṃskārāt || YS_3.10 ||
body.translated_text: Its peaceful flow [comes] from the impression [of cessation]. || YS_3.10 ||

body.text: nirodhasaṃskārābhyāsapāṭavāpekṣā praśāntavāhitā cittasya bhavati. tatsaṃskāramāndye vyutthānadharmiṇā saṃskāreṇa nirodhadharmasaṃskāro 'bhibhūyata iti. 3.10
body.translated_text: Dependent upon the skill in the practice of cessation-impressions, the peaceful flow of the mind arises. When those impressions weaken, the cessation-natured impression is overwhelmed by the emergence-natured impression. 3.10

body.text: sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ kṣayodayau cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ || YS_3.11 ||
body.translated_text: The decline of all-objectness and the rise of one-pointedness of the mind is the <s>samādhi</s>-transformation. || YS_3.11 ||

body.text: sarvārthatā cittadharmaḥ. ekāgratāpi cittadharmaḥ. sarvārthatāyāḥ kṣayas tirobhāva ity arthaḥ. ekāgratāyā udaya āvirbhāva ity arthaḥ. tayor dharmitvenānugataṃ cittaṃ, tad idaṃ cittam apāyopajanayoḥ svātmabhūtayor dharmayor anugataṃ samādhīyate sa cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ. 3.11
body.translated_text: All-objectness (<s>sarvārthatā</s>) is a property of the mind. One-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) is also a property of the mind. The decline of all-objectness means its disappearance. The rise of one-pointedness means its manifestation. The mind that is pervaded by both as their substratum — this mind, pervaded by its own properties in their departure and arising, becomes concentrated — that is the <s>samādhi</s>-transformation of the mind. 3.11

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ śāntoditau tulyapratyayau cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ || YS_3.12 ||
body.translated_text: Then again, when the subsided and arisen cognitive contents are similar, that is the one-pointedness-transformation of the mind. || YS_3.12 ||

body.text: samāhitacittasya pūrvapratyayaḥ śānta uttaras tatsadṛśa uditaḥ, samādhicittam ubhayor anugataṃ punas tathaivāsamādhibhreṣād iti. sa khalv ayaṃ dharmiṇaś cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ. 3.12
body.translated_text: In the concentrated mind, the preceding cognitive content has subsided and the subsequent one, similar to it, has arisen; the <s>samādhi</s>-mind pervades both, maintaining itself without falling from <s>samādhi</s>. This is the one-pointedness-transformation of the mind as substratum. 3.12

body.text: etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ || YS_3.13 ||
body.translated_text: By this, the transformations of property (<s>dharma</s>), characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and condition (<s>avasthā</s>) in the elements and senses have been explained. || YS_3.13 ||

body.text:
etena pūrvoktena cittapariṇāmena dharmalakṣaṇāvasthārūpeṇa bhūtendriyeṣu dharmapariṇāmo lakṣaṇapariṇāmo 'vasthāpariṇāmaś cokto veditavyaḥ. tatra vyutthānanirodhayor abhibhavaprādurbhāvau dharmiṇi dharmapariṇāmaḥ. lakṣaṇapariṇāmaś ca nirodhas trilakṣaṇas tribhir adhvabhir yuktaḥ. sa khalv anāgatalakṣaṇam adhvānaṃ prathamaṃ hitvā dharmatvam anatikrānto vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannaḥ. yatrāsya svarūpeṇābhivyaktiḥ. eṣo 'sya dvitīyo 'dhvā. na cātītānāgatābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyāṃ viyuktaḥ.
  tathā vyutthānaṃ trilakṣaṇaṃ tribhir adhvabhir yuktaṃ vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ hitvā dharmatvam anatikrāntam atītalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannam. eṣo 'sya tṛtīyo 'dhvā. na cānāgatavartamānābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyāṃ viyuktam. evaṃ punar vyutthānam upasaṃpadyamānam anāgatalakṣaṇaṃ hitvā dharmatvam anatikrāntaṃ vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipannam. yatrāsya svarūpābhivyaktau satyāṃ vyāpāraḥ eṣo 'sya dvitīyo 'dhvā. na cātītānāgatābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyāṃ viyuktam iti. evaṃ punar nirodha evaṃ punar vyutthānam iti.
  tathāvasthāpariṇāmaḥ tatra nirodhakṣaṇeṣu nirodhasaṃskārā balavanto bhavanti durbalā vyutthānasaṃskārā iti. eṣa dharmāṇām avasthāpariṇāmaḥ. tatra dharmiṇo dharmaiḥ pariṇāmo dharmāṇāṃ tryadhvanāṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ pariṇāmo lakṣaṇānām apy avasthābhiḥ pariṇāma iti. evaṃ dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmaiḥ śūnyaṃ na kṣaṇam api guṇavṛttam avatiṣṭhate. calaṃ ca guṇavṛttam. guṇasvābhāvyaṃ tu pravṛttikāraṇam uktaṃ guṇānām iti. etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmadharmibhedāt trividhaḥ pariṇāmo veditavyaḥ.
  paramārthatas tv eka eva pariṇāmaḥ. dharmisvarūpamātro hi dharmo dharmivikriyaivaiṣā dharmadvārā prapañcyata iti. tatra dharmasya dharmiṇi vartamānasyaivādhvasv atītānāgatavartamāneṣu bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na tu dravyānyathātvam. yathā suvarṇabhājanasya bhittvānyathākriyamāṇasya bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na suvarṇānyathātvam iti.
  apara āha --- dharmānabhyadhiko dharmī pūrvatattvānatikramāt. pūrvāparāvasthābhedam anupatitaḥ kauṭasthyenaiva parivarteta yady anvayī syād iti.
  ayam adoṣaḥ. kasmāt. ekāntatānabhyupagamāt. tad etat trailokyaṃ vyakter apaiti nityatvapratiṣedhāt. apetam apy asti vināśapratiṣedhāt. saṃsargāc cāsya saukṣmyaṃ, saukṣmyāc cānupalabdhir iti.
  lakṣaṇapariṇāmo dharmo 'dhvasu vartamāno 'tīto 'tītalakṣaṇayukto 'nāgatavartamānābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyām aviyuktaḥ. tathānāgato 'nāgatalakṣaṇayukto vartamānātītābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyām aviyuktaḥ. tathā vartamāno vartamānalakṣaṇayukto 'tītānāgatābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyām aviyukta iti. yathā puruṣa ekasyāṃ striyāṃ rakto na śeṣāsu virakto bhavatīti.
  atra lakṣaṇapariṇāme sarvasya sarvalakṣaṇayogād adhvasaṃkaraḥ prāpnotīti parair doṣaś codyata iti. tasya parihāraḥ --- dharmāṇāṃ dharmatvam aprasādhyam. sati ca dharmatve lakṣaṇabhedo 'pi vācyo na vartamānasamaya evāsya dharmatvam. evaṃ hi na cittaṃ rāgadharmakaṃ syāt krodhakāle rāgasyāsamudācārād iti.
  kiṃca trayāṇāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ yugapad ekasyāṃ vyaktau nāsti saṃbhavaḥ. krameṇa tu svavyañjakāñjanasya bhāvo bhaved iti. uktaṃ ca rūpātiśayā vṛttyatiśayāś ca virudhyante, sāmānyāni tv atiśayaiḥ saha pravartante. tasmād asaṃkaraḥ yathā rāgasyaiva kvacit samudācāra iti na tadānīm anyatrābhāvaḥ, kiṃtu kevalaṃ sāmānyena samanvāgata ity asti tadā tatra tasya bhāvaḥ tathā lakṣaṇasyeti.
  na dharmī tryadhvā dharmās tu tryadhvānas te lakṣitā alakṣitās tatra lakṣitās tāṃ tām avasthāṃ prāpnuvanto 'nyatvena pratinirdiśyante 'vasthāntarato na dravyāntarataḥ. yathaikā rekhā śatasthāne śataṃ daśasthāne daśaikā caikasthāne yathā caikatve 'pi strī mātā cocyate duhitā ca svasā ceti.
  avasthāpariṇāme kauṭasthyaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ kaiścid uktaḥ. katham. adhvano vyāpāreṇa vyavahitatvāt. yadā dharmaḥ svavyāpāraṃ na karoti tadānāgato yadā karoti tadā vartamāno yadā kṛtvā nivṛttas tadātīta ity evaṃ dharmadharmiṇor lakṣaṇānām avasthānāṃ ca kauṭasthyaṃ prāpnotīti parair doṣa ucyate.
  nāsau doṣaḥ. kasmāt. guṇinityatve 'pi guṇānāṃ vimardavaicitryāt. yathā saṃsthānam ādimad dharmamātraṃ śabdādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ vināśyavināśinām evaṃ liṅgam ādimad dharmamātraṃ sattvādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ vināśyavināśinā tasmin vikārasaṃjñeti.
  tatredam udāharaṇaṃ mṛddharmī piṇḍākārād dharmād dharmāntaram upasaṃpadyamāno dharmataḥ pariṇamate ghaṭākāra iti. ghaṭākāro 'nāgataṃ lakṣaṇaṃ hitvā vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipadyata iti lakṣaṇataḥ pariṇamate. ghaṭo navapurāṇatāṃ pratikṣaṇam anubhavann avasthāpariṇāmaṃ pratipadyata iti. dharmiṇo 'pi dharmāntaram avasthā dharmasyāpi lakṣaṇāntaram avasthety eka eva dravyapariṇāmo bhedenopadarśita iti. evaṃ padārthāntareṣv api yojyam iti. ta ete dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā dharmisvarūpam anatikrāntā ity eka eva pariṇāmaḥ sarvān amūn viśeṣān abhiplavate. atha ko 'yaṃ pariṇāmaḥ.avasthitasya dravyasya pūrvadharmanivṛttau dharmāntarotpattiḥ pariṇāma iti. 3.13
body.translated_text: By this previously stated transformation of the mind, the threefold transformation — as property, characteristic, and condition — should be understood as having been explained with respect to the elements and senses. There, the suppression and manifestation of emergence and cessation in the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) is the property-transformation. The characteristic-transformation: cessation, possessing three characteristics, is connected with three time-phases. It first abandons the future-characteristic time-phase, without transcending its nature as a property, and enters the present-characteristic — where its manifestation in its own form occurs. This is its second time-phase. Nor is it disconnected from the past and future characteristics. Likewise, emergence — possessing three characteristics and connected with three time-phases — having abandoned the present-characteristic, without transcending its nature as a property, enters the past-characteristic. This is its third time-phase. Nor is it disconnected from the future and present characteristics. And again, emergence coming into being abandons the future-characteristic, without transcending its nature as a property, and enters the present-characteristic — where, its own form being manifest, its function occurs. This is its second time-phase. Nor is it disconnected from the past and future characteristics. Thus again cessation, and thus again emergence. The condition-transformation: at the moments of cessation, the cessation-impressions become strong and the emergence-impressions become weak. This is the condition-transformation of properties. Among these: the transformation of the substratum through its properties is the property-transformation; the transformation of properties through the three time-phases is the characteristic-transformation; and the transformation of characteristics through conditions is the condition-transformation. Thus, not even for a single moment does the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> stand still, empty of the property-, characteristic-, and condition-transformations. The activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is moving. And the inherent nature of the <s>guṇas</s> has been stated to be the cause of activity. By this, the threefold transformation in the elements and senses should be understood through the distinction of property and substratum. In the ultimate sense, however, there is only one transformation. For a property is nothing but the nature of its substratum; this modification of the substratum is elaborated through the door of property. A property, while existing in its substratum, undergoes change of state through the past, present, and future time-phases — but not change of substance. Just as a gold vessel, when broken and remade, undergoes change of state but not change of gold. Another [teacher] says: the substratum does not exceed its properties, because of the non-transgression of its prior nature. [If the substratum,] having fallen into the difference of prior and subsequent conditions, were to undergo change through absolute fixity alone, it would be a permanent entity. This is not a fault. Why? Because absolute [permanence] is not accepted. This triple world recedes from manifestation — refuting permanence. Yet even having receded, it exists — refuting destruction. Through combination, its subtlety [arises]; and through subtlety, non-perception. In the characteristic-transformation, a property existing in the time-phases, when past, possesses the past-characteristic and is not disconnected from the future and present characteristics. Likewise when future, it possesses the future-characteristic and is not disconnected from the present and past characteristics. And when present, it possesses the present-characteristic and is not disconnected from the past and future characteristics. Just as a man, being attached to one woman, is not thereby unattached to the others. Here, in the characteristic-transformation, the objection is raised by others that since everything possesses all characteristics, there would be a confusion of time-phases. The refutation: the nature-as-property of properties is not something to be established [separately]. Given that nature-as-property, the distinction of characteristics must also be stated — it is not the case that its nature-as-property belongs only to the present moment. For otherwise, the mind would not have desire as a property, since in the time of anger, desire is not in active manifestation. Moreover, the simultaneous manifestation of three characteristics in a single [entity] is impossible. But through sequence, the presence of what reveals each [characteristic] is possible. And it has been said: excesses of form and excesses of activity are mutually exclusive, but universals proceed together with excesses. Therefore there is no confusion — just as desire alone is in active manifestation in a particular case, it does not mean that at that time there is absence [of desire] elsewhere; rather, it is present there at that time merely through the universal — so too with the characteristic. The substratum does not have three time-phases, but the properties do; they are characterized or uncharacterized. Those that are characterized, reaching this or that condition, are designated as different through the condition, not through substance. Just as one line is a hundred in the hundreds-place, ten in the tens-place, and one in the ones-place; and just as a single woman is called mother, daughter, and sister. Regarding the condition-transformation, the fault of absolute fixity has been raised by some. How? Because [the property] is separated from [present] activity by [other] time-phases. When a property does not perform its function, it is future; when it performs it, it is present; when it has performed it and ceased, it is past — thus, they say, both property and substratum, characteristics and conditions, attain absolute fixity. This is not a fault. Why? Because even though the possessor-of-qualities is permanent, the qualities undergo the variety of mutual pressure. Just as configuration is a property with a beginning, subject to destruction and destruction's destroyer, of qualities such as sound, etc. — so too the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is a property with a beginning, of qualities such as <s>sattva</s>, etc., subject to destruction and destruction's destroyer — in this, the designation 'modification' applies. Here is the illustration: clay as substratum, transforming from the property of lump-shape to another property — transforms in terms of property into pot-shape. Pot-shape, having abandoned the future-characteristic and entering the present-characteristic — transforms in terms of characteristic. The pot, experiencing newness and oldness moment by moment, undergoes condition-transformation. A condition is another property of the substratum; a condition is another characteristic of the property — thus the single transformation of substance has been shown through [its] distinctions. This should be applied to other categories as well. These property-, characteristic-, and condition-transformations do not transcend the nature of the substratum — thus a single transformation encompasses all these distinctions. Now, what is this transformation? When a prior property of an abiding substance ceases and another property arises — that is transformation. 3.13

body.text: tatra ---

children.translated_text: The substratum is that which is pervaded by the subsided, arisen, and as-yet-uncharacterizable properties. || YS_3.14 ||

body.translated_text: Among these —

body.text:
yogyatāvacchinnā dharmiṇaḥ śaktir eva dharmaḥ. sa ca phalaprasavabhedānumita ekasyānyo 'nyaś ca paridṛṣṭaḥ. tatra vartamānaḥ svavyāpāram anubhavan dharmī dharmāntarebhyaḥ śāntebhyaś cāvyapadeśyebhyaś ca bhidyate. yadā tu sāmānyena samanvāgato bhavati tadā dharmisvarūpamātratvāt ko 'sau kena bhidyeta.
  tatra ye khalu dharmiṇo dharmāḥ śāntā uditā avyapadeśyāś ceti, tatra śāntā ye kṛtvā vyāpārānuparatāḥ savyāpārā uditās te cānāgatasya lakṣaṇasya samanantarā vartamānasyānantarā atītāḥ kimartham atītasyānantarā na bhavanti vartamānāḥ, pūrvapaścimatāyā abhāvāt. yathānāgatavartamānayoḥ pūrvapaścimatā naivam atītasya. tasmān nātītasyāsti samanantaraḥ tadanāgata eva samanantaro bhavati vartamānasyeti.
  athāvyapadeśyāḥ ke sarvaṃ sarvātmakam iti. yatroktam --- jalabhūmyoḥ pāriṇāmikaṃ rasādivaiśvarūpyaṃ sthāvareṣu dṛṣṭam. tathā sthāvarāṇāṃ jaṅgameṣu jaṅgamānāṃ sthāvareṣv ity evaṃ jātyanucchedena sarvaṃ sarvātmakam iti.
  deśakālākāranimittāpabandhān na khalu samānakālam ātmanām abhivyaktir iti. ya eteṣv abhivyaktānabhivyakteṣu dharmeṣv anupātī sāmānyaviśeṣātmā so 'nvayī dharmī. yasya tu dharmamātram evedaṃ niranvayaṃ tasya bhogābhāvaḥ. kasmāt, anyena vijñānena kṛtasya karmaṇo 'nyat kathaṃ bhoktṛtvenādhikriyate. tatsmṛtyabhāvaś ca nānyadṛṣṭasya smaraṇam anyasyāstīti. vastupratyabhijñānāc ca sthito 'nvayī dharmī yo dharmānyathātvam abhyupagataḥ pratyabhijñāyate tasmān nedaṃ dharmamātraṃ niranvayam iti. 3.14
body.translated_text: A property (<s>dharma</s>) is simply a capacity of the substance (<s>dharmin</s>), delimited by fitness. And it is inferred from the difference in the fruits it produces — one [capacity] is different from another, as observed. Therein, the present [property], undergoing its own function, differs from other properties that are quiescent and from those that are indescribable. But when it is endowed with the universal [nature] —

body.text: kramānyatvaṃ pariṇāmānyatve hetuḥ || YS_3.15 ||
body.translated_text: The difference in sequence is the cause of the difference in transformation. [<s>YS</s> 3.15]

body.text:
ekasya dharmiṇa eka eva pariṇāma iti prasakte kramānyatvaṃ pariṇāmānyatve hetur bhavatīti. tadyathā cūrṇamṛtpiṇḍamṛdghaṭamṛtkapālamṛtkaṇamṛd iti ca kramaḥ. yo yasya dharmasya samanantaro dharmaḥ sa tasya kramaḥ. piṇḍaḥ pracyavate ghaṭa upajāyata iti dharmapariṇāmakramaḥ. lakṣaṇapariṇāmakramo ghaṭasyānāgatabhāvād vartamānabhāvaḥ kramaḥ. tathā piṇḍasya vartamānabhāvād atītabhāvaḥ kramaḥ. nātītasyāsti kramaḥ. kasmāt. pūrvaparatāyāṃ satyāṃ samanantaratvaṃ, sā tu nāsty atītasya tasmād dvayor eva lakṣaṇayoḥ kramaḥ. tathāvasthāpariṇāmakramo 'pi ghaṭasyābhinavasya prānte purāṇatā dṛśyate. sā ca kṣaṇaparamparānupātinā krameṇābhivyajyamānā parāṃ vyaktim āpadyata iti. dharmalakṣaṇābhyāṃ ca viśiṣṭo 'yaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pariṇāma iti.
  ta ete kramā dharmadharmibhede sati pratilabdhasvarūpāḥ. dharmo 'pi dharmī bhavaty anyadharmasvarūpāpekṣayeti. yadā tu paramārthato dharmiṇy abhedopacāras taddvāreṇa sa evābhidhīyate dharmas tadāyam ekatvenaiva kramaḥ pratyavabhāsate.

children.text: cittasya dvaye dharmā paridṛṣṭāś cāparidṛṣṭāś ca. tatra pratyayātmakāḥ paridṛṣṭā vastumātrātmakā aparidṛṣṭāḥ. te ca saptaiva bhavanty anumānena prāpitavastumātrasadbhāvāḥ.
children.translated_text: The properties of the mind (<s>citta</s>) are twofold: observed and unobserved. Among them, those consisting of cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>) are observed, while those consisting merely of objective reality (<s>vastumātra</s>) are unobserved. And those are precisely seven, their objective reality established through inference.
'Suppression (<s>nirodha</s>), property, latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), transformation, then vitality,

children.text: ceṣṭā śaktiś ca cittasya dharmā darśanavarjitāḥ //" iti. 3.15
children.translated_text: activity, and capacity — these are the properties of the mind beyond [ordinary] perception.' [3.15]

body.translated_text: When it is supposed that there is only one transformation of a single substance, the difference in sequence becomes the cause of the difference in transformation. For example: clay as powder, clay as lump, clay as pot, clay as shard, clay as particle — such is the sequence. Whatever property immediately follows another property — that is its sequence. The lump passes away; the pot arises.

body.text: ato yogina upāttasarvasādhanasya bubhutsitārthapratipattaye saṃyamasya viṣaya upakṣipyate ---

children.translated_text: Through <s>saṃyama</s> on the three [kinds of] transformation, knowledge of the past and future [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.16]

body.translated_text: Therefore, for the yogin who has taken up all the means, in order to attain the desired object, the domain of <s>saṃyama</s> is introduced —

body.text: dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmeṣu saṃyamād yogināṃ bhavaty atītānāgatajñānam. dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayam ekatra saṃyama uktaḥ. tena pariṇāmatrayaṃ sākṣātkriyamāṇam atītānāgatajñānaṃ teṣu saṃpādayati. 3.16
body.translated_text: Through <s>saṃyama</s> on the transformations of property (<s>dharma</s>), characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and condition (<s>avasthā</s>), knowledge of the past and future arises for yogins. The triad of concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and <s>samādhi</s> applied to a single [object] has been called <s>saṃyama</s>. By that, directly realizing the three [kinds of] transformation, one accomplishes knowledge of the past and future regarding them. [3.16]

body.text: śabdārthapratyayānām itaretarādhyāsāt saṃkaras tatpravibhāgasaṃyamāt sarvabhūtarutajñānam || YS_3.17 ||
body.translated_text: Due to the superimposition of word, meaning, and cognition upon one another, there is confusion; through <s>saṃyama</s> on their distinction, knowledge of the sounds of all beings [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.17]

body.text:
tatra vāgvarṇeṣv evārthavatī. śrotraṃ ca dhvanipariṇāmamātraviṣayam. padaṃ punar nādānusaṃhārabuddhinirgrāhyam iti. varṇā ekasamayāsaṃbhavitvāt parasparaniranugrahātmānas te padam asaṃspṛśyānupasthāpyāvirbhūtās tirobhūtāś ceti pratyekam apadasvarūpā ucyante.
  varṇaḥ punar ekaikaḥ padātmā sarvābhidhānaśaktipracitaḥ sahakārivarṇāntarapratiyogitvād vaiśvarūpyam ivāpannaḥ pūrvaś cottareṇottaraś ca pūrveṇa viśeṣe 'vasthāpita ity evaṃ bahavo varṇāḥ kramānurodhino 'rthasaṃketenāvacchinnā iyanta ete sarvābhidhānaśaktiparivṛtā gakāraukāravisarjanīyāḥ sāsnādimantam arthaṃ dyotayantīti.
  tad eteṣām arthasaṃketenāvacchinnānām upasaṃhṛtadhvanikramāṇāṃ ya eko buddhinirbhāsas tatpadaṃ vācakaṃ vācyasya saṃketyate. tad ekaṃ padam ekabuddhiviṣaya ekaprayatnākṣiptam abhāgam akramam avarṇaṃ bauddham antyavarṇapratyayavyāpāropasthāpitaṃ paratra pratipipādayiṣayā varṇair evābhidhīyamānaiḥ śrūyamāṇaiś ca śrotṛbhir anādivāgvyavahāravāsanānuviddhayā lokabuddhyā siddhavatsaṃpratipattyā pratīyate.
  tasya saṃketabuddhitaḥ pravibhāga etāvatām evaṃjātīyako 'nusaṃhāra ekasyārthasya vācaka iti. saṃketas tu padapadārthayor itaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ smṛtyātmako yo 'yaṃ śabdaḥ so 'yam artho yo 'yam arthaḥ so 'yaṃ śabda iti. evam itaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ saṃketo bhavatīti. evam ete śabdārthapratyayā itaretarādhyāsāt saṃkīrṇā gaur iti śabdo gaur ity artho gaur iti jñānam. ya eṣāṃ pravibhāgajñaḥ sa sarvavit.
  sarvapadeṣu cāsti vākyaśaktivṛkṣa ity ukte 'stīti gamyate. na sattāṃ padārtho vyabhicaratīti. tathā na hy asādhanā kriyāstīti.
  tathā ca pacatīty ukte sarvakārakāṇām ākṣepo niyamārtho 'nuvādaḥ kartṛkaraṇakarmaṇāṃ caitrāgnitaṇḍulānām iti. dṛṣṭaṃ ca vākyārthe padaracanaṃ śrotriyaś chando 'dhīte, jīvati prāṇān dhārayati. tatra vākye padārthābhivyaktis tataḥ padaṃ pravibhajya vyākaraṇīyaṃ kriyāvācakaṃ vā kārakavācakaṃ vā. anyathā bhavaty aśvo 'jāpaya ity evamādiṣu nāmākhyātasārūpyād anirjñātaṃ kathaṃ kriyāyāṃ kārake vā vyākriyeteti.
  teṣāṃ śabdārthapratyayānāṃ pravibhāgaḥ. tadyathā śvetate prāsāda iti kriyārthaḥ, śvetaḥ prāsāda iti kārakārthaḥ śabdaḥ, kriyākārakātmā tadarthaḥ pratyayaś ca. kasmāt so 'yam ity abhisaṃbandhād ekākāra eva pratyayaḥ saṃketa iti.
  yas tu śveto 'rthaḥ sa śabdapratyayayor ālambanībhūtaḥ. sa hi svābhir avasthābhir vikriyamāṇo na śabdasahagato na buddhisahagataḥ. evaṃ śabda evaṃ pratyayo netaretarasahagata ity anyathā śabdo 'nyathārtho 'nyathā pratyaya iti vibhāgaḥ. evaṃ tatpravibhāgasaṃyamād yoginaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñānaṃ saṃpadyata iti. 3.17
body.translated_text: Therein, speech is meaningful only in its phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>). And the ear has as its object only the transformation of sound vibrations. But a word is grasped by the intellect through the integration of sounds. Since phonemes cannot occur simultaneously and are by nature not mutually supporting, they — each individually not having the nature of a word — without touching [each other], without presenting [each other], whether manifest or unmanifest —

body.text: saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇāt pūrvajātijñānam || YS_3.18 ||
body.translated_text: Through direct perception of latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), knowledge of previous births [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.18]

body.text:
dvaye khalv amī saṃskārāḥ smṛtikleśahetavo vāsanārūpā vipākahetavo dharmādharmarūpāḥ. te pūrvabhavābhisaṃskṛtāḥ pariṇāmaceṣṭānirodhaśaktijīvanadharmavad aparidṛṣṭāś cittadharmāḥ. teṣu saṃyamaḥ saṃskārasākṣātkriyāyai samarthaḥ. na ca deśakālanimittānubhavair vinā teṣām asti sākṣātkaraṇam. tad itthaṃ saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇāt pūrvajātijñānam utpadyate yoginaḥ. paratrāpy evam eva saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇāt parajātisaṃvedanam.
  atredam ākhyānaṃ śrūyate --- bhagavato jaigīṣavyasya saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇād daśasu mahāsargeṣu janmapariṇāmakramam anupaśyato vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ prādurabhūt. atha bhagavān āvaṭyas tanudharas tam uvāca --- daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvād anabhibhūtabuddhisattvena tvayā narakatiryaggarbhasaṃbhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃpaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥ punar utpadyamānena sukhaduḥkhayoḥ kim adhikam upalabdham iti. bhagavantam āvaṭyaṃ jaigīṣavya uvāca. daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvād anabhibhūtabuddhisattvena mayā narakatiryagbhavaṃduḥkhaṃ saṃpaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥ punar utpadyamānena yat kiṃcid anubhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ duḥkham eva pratyavaimi. bhagavān āvaṭya uvāca. yad idam āyuṣmataḥ pradhānavaśitvam anuttamaṃ ca saṃtoṣasukhaṃ kim idam api duḥkhapakṣe nikṣiptam iti. bhavagāñ jaigīṣavya uvāca --- viṣayasukhāpekṣayaivedam anuttamaṃ saṃtoṣasukham uktam. kaivalyasukhāpekṣayā duḥkham eva. buddhisattvasyāyaṃ dharmas triguṇas triguṇaś ca pratyayo heyapakṣe nyasta iti. duḥkharūpas tṛṣṇātantuḥ. tṛṣṇāduḥkhasaṃtāpāpagamāt tu prasannam abādhaṃ sarvānukūlaṃ sukham idam uktam iti. 3.18
body.translated_text:
These <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) are indeed of two kinds: those in the form of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent tendencies) that are causes of memory and afflictions, and those in the form of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> that are causes of fruition (<s>vipāka</s>). They are properties of the mind, conditioned by previous existences, imperceptible—like the powers of transformation, activity, cessation, and the vital functions. <s>Saṃyama</s> (concentration) on these is capable of directly perceiving the <s>saṃskāras</s>. And there is no direct perception of them without [the experience of] place, time, and cause. Thus, from the direct perception of <s>saṃskāras</s> in this manner, knowledge of previous births arises for the yogin. In others' cases too, from the direct perception of <s>saṃskāras</s> in exactly the same way, knowledge of their births [is gained].
  Here, this narrative is told: Through the direct perception of <s>saṃskāras</s>, as the blessed <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> observed the sequence of transformations across births through ten great creations, knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja-jñāna</s>) arose in him. Then the blessed <s>Āvaṭya</s>, who was an embodied being, asked him: 'Having existed through ten great creations, with your <s>buddhi-sattva</s> unconquered, as you have observed the suffering of birth in hells, animal wombs, and other states, and as you have been born again and again among gods and humans—have you found more pleasure or more pain?' The blessed <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> replied to <s>Āvaṭya</s>: 'Having existed through ten great creations, with my <s>buddhi-sattva</s> unconquered, as I have observed the suffering of existence in hells and animal states, and as I have been born again and again among gods and humans—whatever I have experienced, all of that I understand to be nothing but suffering.' The blessed <s>Āvaṭya</s> said: 'What of this unsurpassed bliss of contentment and this mastery over <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) that you possess—is this too placed in the category of suffering?' The blessed <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> replied: 'This unsurpassed bliss of contentment is spoken of only in comparison to the pleasure of sense objects. In comparison to the bliss of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), it is indeed suffering. This property of <s>buddhi-sattva</s> is constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, and any cognition constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s> is placed in the category of what is to be abandoned.' The thread of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is of the nature of suffering. But with the cessation of the torment of craving and suffering, that [bliss] is called serene, unobstructed, and entirely agreeable—this is what is meant. [3.18]

body.text: pratyayasya paracittajñānam || YS_3.19 ||
body.translated_text: [From <s>saṃyama</s>] on cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>), [arises] knowledge of another's mind. [YS 3.19]

body.text: pratyaye saṃyamāt pratyayasya sākṣātkaraṇāt tataḥ paracittajñānam. 3.19
body.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on cognition, through the direct perception of cognition, therefrom arises knowledge of another's mind. [3.19]

body.text: na ca tat sālambanaṃ tasyāviṣayībhūtatvāt || YS_3.20 ||
body.translated_text: But not its object-support, because that [object] has not become the yogin's content. [YS 3.20]

body.text: raktaṃ pratyayaṃ jānāty amuṣminn ālambane raktam iti na jānāti. parapratyayasya yad ālambanaṃ tad yogicittena nālambanīkṛtaṃ parapratyayamātraṃ tu yogicittasyālambanībhūtam iti. 3.20
body.translated_text: One knows the colored cognition [of another], but does not know 'it is colored with regard to this particular object.' The object that is the support of another's cognition has not been made the support of the yogin's mind; only the other's cognition itself has become the support of the yogin's mind. [3.20]

body.text: kāyarūpasaṃyamāt tadgrāhyaśaktistambhe cakṣuḥprakāśāsaṃprayoge 'ntardhānam || YS_3.21 ||
body.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the form of the body, upon the suspension of the power of being grasped, when there is disconnection from the light of the eyes, invisibility [results]. [YS 3.21]

body.text: kāyasya rūpe saṃyamād rūpasya yā grāhyā śaktis tāṃ pratiṣṭabhnāti. grāhyaśaktistambhe sati cakṣuṣprakāśāsaṃprayoge 'ntardhānam utpadyate yoginaḥ. etena śabdādyantardhānam uktaṃ veditavyam. 3.21
body.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the form of the body, one suspends the graspable power of that form. When the graspable power is suspended, since there is no connection with the light of the eyes, invisibility arises for the yogin. By this, it should be understood that the disappearance of sound and the other [sense objects] is also explained. [3.21]

body.text: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamād aparāntajñānam ariṣṭebhyo vā || YS_3.22 ||
body.translated_text: Karma is of two kinds: with active fruition (<s>sopakrama</s>) and without active fruition (<s>nirupakrama</s>). From <s>saṃyama</s> on that, knowledge of the final end [death] arises; or from portents (<s>ariṣṭas</s>). [YS 3.22]

body.text:
āyurvipākaṃ karma dvividhaṃ sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca. tatra yathārdraṃ vastraṃ vitānitaṃ laghīyasā kālena śuṣyet tathā sopakramam. yathā ca tad eva saṃpiṇḍitaṃ cireṇa saṃśuṣyed evaṃ nirupakramam. yathā vāgniḥ śuṣke kakṣe mukto vātena samantato yuktaḥ kṣepīyasā kālena dahet tathā sopakramam. yathā vā sa evāgnis tṛṇarāśau kramaśo 'vayaveṣu nyastaś cireṇa dahet tathā nirupakramam. tadaikabhavikam āyuṣkaraṃ karma dvividhaṃ sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca. tatsaṃyamād aparāntasya prāyaṇasya jñānam.
  ariṣṭebhyo veti trividham ariṣṭam ādhyātmikam ādhibhautikam ādhidaivikaṃ ceti. tatrādhyātmikaṃ ghoṣaṃ svadehe pihitakarṇo na śṛṇoti, jyotir vā netre 'vaṣṭabdhe na paśyati. tathādhibhautikaṃ yamapuruṣān paśyati, pitṝn atītān akasmāt paśyati. tathādhidaivikaṃ svargam akasmāt siddhān vā paśyati. viparītaṃ vā sarvam iti anena vā jānāty aparāntam upasthitam iti. 3.22
body.translated_text:
Life-span-determining <s>karma</s> is of two kinds: with active fruition (<s>sopakrama</s>) and without active fruition (<s>nirupakrama</s>). Just as a wet cloth, spread out, dries in a shorter time—so is the <s>sopakrama</s> [type]. And just as that same cloth, bunched together, takes a long time to dry—so is the <s>nirupakrama</s> [type]. Or, just as fire, released in dry brush and aided by wind from all sides, burns in a very short time—so is the <s>sopakrama</s>. And just as that same fire, placed gradually in parts of a heap of grass, takes a long time to burn—so is the <s>nirupakrama</s>. That life-determining <s>karma</s>, pertaining to a single existence, is of two kinds: <s>sopakrama</s> and <s>nirupakrama</s>. From <s>saṃyama</s> on that, knowledge of the final end, of death, [arises].
  'Or from portents': portents are threefold—personal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), external (<s>ādhibhautika</s>), and celestial (<s>ādhidaivika</s>). Among these, the personal [portent]: one does not hear the sound within one's own body when the ears are blocked, or one does not see the light when the eyes are held firm. The external [portent]: one sees the messengers of <s>Yama</s>, or one suddenly sees deceased ancestors. The celestial [portent]: one suddenly sees heaven or <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings). Or everything [appears] reversed. By this too, one knows that the final end has arrived. [3.22]

body.text: maitryādiṣu balāni || YS_3.23 ||
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṃyama</s>] on friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) and so forth, powers [arise]. [YS 3.23]

body.text: maitrī karuṇā muditeti tisro bhāvanās tatra bhūteṣu sukhiteṣu maitrīṃ bhāvayitvā maitrībalaṃ labhate. duḥkhiteṣu karuṇāṃ bhāvayitvā karuṇābalaṃ labhate. puṇyaśīleṣu muditāṃ bhāvayitvā muditābalaṃ labhate. bhāvanātaḥ samādhir yaḥ sa saṃyamas tato balāny avandhyavīryāṇi jāyante. pāpaśīleṣūpekṣā na tu bhāvanā. tataś ca tasyāṃ nāsti samādhir ity ato na balam upekṣātas tatra saṃyamābhāvād iti. 3.23
body.translated_text: Friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>)—these are three cultivations (<s>bhāvanās</s>). Among beings who are happy, by cultivating friendliness, one obtains the power of friendliness. Among those who are suffering, by cultivating compassion, one obtains the power of compassion. Among those of virtuous conduct, by cultivating sympathetic joy, one obtains the power of sympathetic joy. From the cultivation, there arises <s>samādhi</s>, which constitutes <s>saṃyama</s>; from that, powers arise whose efficacy is unfailing. Toward the sinful, there is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), but not cultivation. Therefore, from equanimity there is no <s>samādhi</s>, and hence no power arises from equanimity—since there is no <s>saṃyama</s> therein. [3.23]

body.text: baleṣu hastibalādīni || YS_3.24 ||
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṃyama</s>] on powers, [arise] the strength of an elephant and so forth. [YS 3.24]

body.text: hastibale saṃyamād dhastibalo bhavati.vainateyabale saṃyamād vainateyabalo bhavati. vāyubale saṃyamād vāyubalo bhavatīty evamādi. 3.24
body.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the strength of an elephant, one becomes strong as an elephant. From <s>saṃyama</s> on the strength of <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), one becomes strong as <s>Vainateya</s>. From <s>saṃyama</s> on the strength of the wind, one becomes strong as the wind—and so on. [3.24]

body.text: pravṛttyālokanyāsāt sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭajñānam || YS_3.25 ||
body.translated_text: From directing the light of higher sensory activity (<s>pravṛttyāloka</s>), knowledge of the subtle, the concealed, and the distant [arises]. [YS 3.25]

body.text: jyotiṣmatī pravṛttir uktā manasas tasyā ya ālokas taṃ yogī sūkṣme vā vyavahite vā viprakṛṣṭe vārthe vinyasya tam artham adhigacchati. 3.25
body.translated_text: The luminous activity (<s>jyotiṣmatī pravṛtti</s>) of the mind has been described. The yogin, directing its light upon an object that is subtle, or concealed, or distant, apprehends that object. [3.25]

body.text: bhuvanajñānaṃ sūrye saṃyamāt || YS_3.26 ||
body.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the sun, knowledge of the worlds [arises]. [YS 3.26]

children.text: tatprastāraḥ sapta lokāḥ. tatrāvīceḥ prabhṛti merupṛṣṭhaṃ yāvad ity evaṃ bhūrlokaḥ. merupṛṣṭhād ārabhya --- ādhruvād grahanakṣatratārāvicitro 'ntarikṣalokaḥ. tataḥ paraḥ svarlokaḥ pañcavidho māhendras tṛtīyo lokaḥ. caturthaḥ prājāpatyo maharlokaḥ. trividho brāhmaḥ tadyathā --- janalokas tapolokaḥ satyaloka iti.
children.translated_text: The exposition of that: there are seven worlds. Among these, from <s>Avīci</s> [hell] up to the summit of <s>Meru</s>—this is the earth-world (<s>bhūrloka</s>). Beginning from the summit of <s>Meru</s>, up to the Pole Star, adorned with planets, <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations), and stars—this is the mid-space world (<s>antarikṣaloka</s>). Beyond that is the heaven-world (<s>svarloka</s>). The third world, of five kinds, is of <s>Mahendra</s>. The fourth is of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the great world (<s>maharloka</s>). The world of <s>Brahmā</s> is threefold, namely: <s>Janaloka</s>, <s>Tapoloka</s>, and <s>Satyaloka</s>.
"The world of <s>Brahmā</s>, comprising three levels; then the great [world] of <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: māhendraś ca svar ity ukto divi tārā bhuvi prajāḥ //"
children.translated_text: and that of <s>Mahendra</s>, called heaven (<s>svar</s>)—in the sky are the stars, on earth are the creatures."

body.text:
iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ.
  tatrāvīcer upary upari niviṣṭāḥ ṣaṇmahānarakabhūmayo ghanasalilānalānilākāśatamaḥpratiṣṭhā mahākālāmbarīṣarauravamahārauravakālasūtrāndhatāmisrāḥ. yatra svakarmopārjitaduḥkhavedanāḥ prāṇinaḥ kaṣṭam āyur dīrgham ākṣipya jāyante. tato mahātalarasātalātalasutalavitalatalātalapātālākhyāni sapta pātālāni. bhūmir iyam aṣṭamī saptadvīpā vasumatī, yasyāḥ sumerur madhye parvatarājaḥ kāñcanaḥ. tasya rājatavaidūryasphaṭikahemamaṇimayāni śṛṅgāṇi. tatra vaidūryaprabhānurāgān nīlotpalapatraśyāmo nabhaso dakṣiṇo bhāgaḥ, śvetaḥ pūrvaḥ, svacchaḥ paścimaḥ, kuraṇṭakābha uttaraḥ. dakṣiṇapārśve cāsya jambūr yato 'yaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ. tasya sūryapracārād rātriṃdivaṃ lagnam iva vartate. tasya nīlaśvetaśṛṅgavanta udīcīnās trayaḥ parvatā dvisāhasrāyāmāḥ. tadantareṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nava nava yojanasāhasrāṇi ramaṇakaṃ hiraṇmayam uttarāḥ kurava iti. niṣadhahemakūṭahimaśailā dakṣiṇato dvisāhasrāyāmāḥ. tadantareṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nava nava yojanasāhasrāṇi harivarṣaṃ kiṃpuruṣaṃ bhāratam iti. sumeroḥ prācīnā bhadrāśvamālyavatsīmānaḥ pratīcīnāḥ ketumālā gandhamādanasīmānaḥ. madhye varṣamilāvṛtam. tad etad yojanaśatasāhasraṃ sumeror diśidiśi tadardhena vyūḍham.
  sa khalv ayaṃ śatasāhasrāyāmo jambūdvīpas tato dviguṇena lavaṇodadhinā valayākṛtinā veṣṭitaḥ. tataś ca dviguṇā dviguṇāḥ śākakuśakrauñcaśālmalagomedha(plakṣa) puṣkaradvīpāḥ, samudrāś ca sarṣaparāśikalpāḥ savicitraśailāvataṃsā ikṣurasasurāsarpirdadhimaṇḍakṣīrasvādūdakāḥ. sapta samudrapariveṣṭitā valayākṛtayo lokālokaparvataparivārāḥ pañcāśad yojanakoṭiparisaṃkhyātāḥ. tad etat sarvaṃ supratiṣṭhitasaṃsthānamaṇḍamadhye vyūḍham. aṇḍaṃ ca pradhānasyāṇur avayavo yathākāśe khadyota iti.
  tatra pātāle jaladhau parvateṣv eteṣu devanikāyā asuragandharvakiṃnarakiṃpuruṣayakṣarākṣasabhūtapretapiśācāpasmārakāpsarobrahmarākṣasakūṣmāṇḍavināyakāḥ prativasanti. sarveṣu dvīpeṣu puṇyātmāno devamanuṣyāḥ.
  sumerus tridaśānām udyānabhūmiḥ tatra miśravanaṃ nandanaṃ caitrarathaṃ sumānasam ity udyānāni. sudharmā devasabhā sudarśanaṃ puram. vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ. grahanakṣatratārakās tu dhruve nibaddhā vāyuvikṣepaniyamenopalakṣitapracārāḥ sumeror upary upari saṃniviṣṭā divi viparivartante.
  māhendranivāsinaḥ ṣaḍdevanikāyāḥ --- tridaśā agniṣvāttā yāmyās tuṣitā aparinirmitavaśavartinaḥ parinirmitavaśavartinaś ceti. sarve saṃkalpasiddhā aṇimādyaiśvaryopapannāḥ kalpāyuṣo vṛndārakāḥ kāmabhogina aupapādikadehā uttamānukūlābhir apsarobhiḥ kṛtaparicārāḥ.
  mahati loke prājāpatye pañcavidho devanikāyaḥ --- kumudā ṛbhavaḥ pratardanā añjanābhāḥ pracitābhā iti. ete mahābhūtavaśino dhyānāhārāḥ kalpasahasrāyuṣaḥ. prathame brahmaṇo janaloke caturvidho devanikāyo brahmapurohitā brahmakāyikā brahmamahākāyikā amarā iti. te bhūtendriyavaśino dviguṇadviguṇottarāyuñaḥ.
  dvitīye tapasi loke trividho devanikāyaḥ --- ābhāsvarā mahābhāsvarāḥ satyamahābhāsvarā iti. te bhūtendriyaprakṛtivaśino dviguṇadviguṇottarāyuṣaḥ sarve dhyānāhārā ūrdhvaretasa ūrdhvam apratihatajñānā adharabhūmiṣv anāvṛtajñānaviṣayāḥ. tṛtīye brahmaṇaḥ satyaloke catvāro devanikāyā akṛtabhavananyāsāḥ svapratiṣṭhā uparyuparisthitāḥ pradhānavaśino yāvat sargāyuṣaḥ.
  tatrācyutāḥ savitarkadhyānasukhāḥ, śuddhanivāsāḥ savicāradhyānasukhāḥ, satyābhā ānandamātradhyānasukhāḥ, saṃjñāsaṃjñinaś cāsmitāmātradhyānasukhāḥ. te 'pi trailokyamadhye pratitiṣṭhanti. ta ete sapta lokāḥ sarva eva brahmalokāḥ. videhaprakṛtilayās tu mokṣapade vartanta iti na lokamadhye nyastā iti. etad yoginā sākṣātkaraṇīyaṃ sūryadvāre saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā, tato 'nyatrāpi evaṃ tāvad abhyased yāvad idaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭam iti. 3.26
body.translated_text: This is the summary verse. Therein, above <s>Avīci</s>, one above another, are situated the six great hell-realms: earth, water, fire, wind, space, and darkness are their foundations — <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, and <s>Andhatāmisra</s>. There, beings who have acquired suffering through their own <s>karma</s> are born, enduring a painful and long lifespan.

body.text: candre tārāvyūhajñānam || YS_3.27 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the moon, knowledge of the arrangement of the stars [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.27]

body.text: candre saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā tārāṇāṃ vyūhaṃ vijānīyāt. 3.27
body.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the moon, one may know the arrangement of the stars. [3.27]

body.text: dhruve tadgatijñānam || YS_3.28 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the pole star, knowledge of their movement [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.28]

body.text: tato dhruve saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā tārāṇāṃ gatiṃ vijānīyāt ūrdhvavimāneṣu kṛtasaṃyamas tāni vijānīyāt. 3.28
body.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the pole star, one may know the movement of the stars. Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the celestial vehicles above, one may know them. [3.28]

body.text: nābhicakre kāyavyūhajñānam || YS_3.29 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the navel center, knowledge of the arrangement of the body [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.29]

body.text: nābhicakre saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā kāyavyūhaṃ vijānīyāt vātapittaśleṣmāṇas trayo doṣāḥ. dhātavaḥ sapta tvaglohitamāṃsasnāyvasthimajjāśukrāṇi pūrvaṃ pūrvam eṣāṃ bāhyam ity eṣa vinyāsaḥ. 3.29
body.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the navel center (<s>nābhicakra</s>), one may know the arrangement of the body. The three defects (<s>doṣa</s>) are wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), and phlegm (<s>śleṣma</s>). The seven constituents (<s>dhātu</s>) are skin, blood, flesh, sinew, bone, marrow, and semen. Each preceding one is more external than the next — this is the arrangement. [3.29]

body.text: kaṇṭhakūpe kṣutpipāsānivṛttiḥ || YS_3.30 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the throat-well, the cessation of hunger and thirst [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.30]

body.text: jihvāyā adhastāt tantus tantor adhastāt kaṇṭhas tato 'dhastāt kūpas tatra saṃyamāt kṣutpipāse na bādhete. 3.30
body.translated_text: Below the tongue is a cord; below the cord is the throat; below that is the well (<s>kūpa</s>). Through <s>saṃyama</s> on that, hunger and thirst do not afflict [the yogin]. [3.30]

body.text: kūrmanāḍyāṃ sthairyam || YS_3.31 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the <s>kūrma</s> channel, steadiness [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.31]

body.text: kūpād adha urasi kūrmākārā nāḍī, tasyāṃ kṛtasaṃyamaḥ sthirapadaṃ labhate yathā sarpo godhā veti. 3.31
body.translated_text: Below the well, in the chest, is a channel (<s>nāḍī</s>) in the shape of a tortoise (<s>kūrma</s>). One who has performed <s>saṃyama</s> on it attains the ground of steadiness — like a serpent or a monitor lizard. [3.31]

body.text: mūrdhajyotiṣi siddhadarśanam || YS_3.32 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the light at the crown of the head, the vision of perfected beings [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.32]

body.text: śiraḥkapāle 'ntaś chidraṃ prabhāsvaraṃ jyotis tatra saṃyamaṃ kṛtvā siddhānāṃ dyāvāpṛthivyor antarālacāriṇāṃ darśanam. 3.32
body.translated_text: Inside the skull there is an aperture with a luminous light. Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on that, one has the vision of perfected beings (<s>siddha</s>) who move in the space between heaven and earth. [3.32]

body.text: prātibhād vā sarvam || YS_3.33 ||
body.translated_text: Or, [one knows] everything through intuitive insight (<s>prātibha</s>). [<s>YS</s> 3.33]

body.text: prātibhaṃ nāma tārakaṃ tadvivekajasya jñānasya pūrvarūpam. yathodaye prabhā bhāskarasya. tena vā sarvam eva jānāti yogī prātibhasya jñānasyotpattāv iti. 3.33
body.translated_text: <s>Prātibha</s> is called the 'deliverer' (<s>tāraka</s>); it is the precursor of knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>). Like the radiance of the sun at its rising. By this, the yogin knows everything — upon the arising of intuitive knowledge. [3.33]

body.text: hṛdaye cittasaṃvit || YS_3.34 ||
body.translated_text: [Through <s>saṃyama</s>] on the heart, understanding of the mind [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.34]

body.text: yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma tatra vijñānaṃ tasmin saṃyamāc cittasaṃvit. 3.34
body.translated_text: In this 'city of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmapura</s>), [the heart], there is a small lotus-abode; there is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Through <s>saṃyama</s> on that, understanding of the mind arises. [3.34]

body.text: sattvapuruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthāt svārthasaṃyamāt puruṣajñānam || YS_3.35 ||
body.translated_text: Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is a cognition that does not distinguish between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, though they are utterly distinct. Through <s>saṃyama</s> on what exists for its own sake, as distinct from what exists for another's sake, knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s> [arises]. [<s>YS</s> 3.35]

body.text:
buddhisattvaṃ prakhyāśīlaṃ samānasattvopanibandhane rajastamasī vaśīkṛtya sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayena pariṇatam. tasmāc ca sattvāt pariṇāmino 'tyantavidharmā viśuddho 'nyaś citimātrarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ. tayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ puruṣasya darśitaviṣayatvāt sa bhogapratyayaḥ sattvasya parārthatvād dṛśyaḥ.
  yas tu tasmād viśiṣṭaś citimātrarūpo 'nyaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ pratyayas tatra saṃyamāt puruṣaviṣayā prajñā jāyate. na ca puruṣapratyayena buddhisattvātmanā puruṣo dṛśyate puruṣa eva taṃ pratyayaṃ svātmāvalambanaṃ paśyati tathā hy uktam --- "vijñātāram are kena vijānīyāt" iti. 3.35
body.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s>, whose nature is luminosity (<s>prakhyā</s>), having subordinated <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — which are connected with <s>sattva</s> of the same [level] — is transformed by a cognition of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. And <s>Puruṣa</s>, utterly different from that transforming <s>sattva</s>, is another — pure, of the nature of consciousness alone (<s>citimātrarūpa</s>). Experience is a cognition that does not distinguish between these two, though utterly distinct; <s>Puruṣa</s> —

body.text: tataḥ prātibhaśrāvaṇavedanādarśāsvādavārtā jāyante || YS_3.36 ||
body.translated_text: From that arise intuitive hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell [of a divine nature]. [<s>YS</s> 3.36]

body.text: prātibhāt sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭātītānāgatajñānam. śrāvaṇād divyaśabdaśravaṇam. vedanād divyasparśādhigamaḥ. ādarśād divyarūpasaṃvit āsvādād divyarasasaṃvit vārtāto divyagandhavijñānam ity etāni nityaṃ jāyante. 3.36
body.translated_text: From intuitive insight (<s>prātibha</s>), knowledge of the subtle, the hidden, the remote, the past, and the future. From [intuitive] hearing (<s>śrāvaṇa</s>), hearing of divine sounds. From [intuitive] touch (<s>vedanā</s>), attainment of divine touch. From [intuitive] sight (<s>ādarśa</s>), perception of divine forms. From [intuitive] taste (<s>āsvāda</s>), perception of divine flavors. From [intuitive] smell (<s>vārtā</s>), knowledge of divine fragrances. These always arise. [3.36]

body.text: te samādhāv upasargā vyutthāne siddhayaḥ || YS_3.37 ||
body.translated_text: These are obstacles in <s>samādhi</s>, but accomplishments (<s>siddhi</s>) in the outward-turned [state]. [<s>YS</s> 3.37]

body.text: te prātibhādayaḥ samāhitacittasyotpadyamānā upasargās taddarśanapratyanīkatvāt vyutthitacittasyotpadyamānāḥ siddhayaḥ. 3.37
body.translated_text: Those [powers] beginning with intuitive insight, when they arise for one whose mind is concentrated, are obstacles, being contrary to [the vision of] that [<s>Puruṣa</s>]. When they arise for one whose mind is outward-turned, they are accomplishments (<s>siddhi</s>). [3.37]

body.text: bandhakāraṇaśaithilyāt pracārasaṃvedanāc ca cittasya paraśarīrāveśaḥ || YS_3.38 ||
body.translated_text: Through the loosening of the cause of bondage and through the awareness of the channels of movement of the mind, [one achieves] entry into another's body. [<s>YS</s> 3.38]

body.text: lolībhūtasya manaso 'pratiṣṭhasya śarīre karmāśayavaśād bandhaḥ pratiṣṭhety arthaḥ tasya karmaṇo bandhakāraṇasya śaithilyaṃ samādhibalād bhavati. pracārasaṃvedanaṃ ca cittasya samādhijam eva karmabandhakṣayāt svacittasya pracārasaṃvedanāc ca yogī cittaṃ svaśarīrān niṣkṛṣya śarīrāntareṣu nikṣipati. nikṣiptaṃ cittaṃ cendriyāṇy anu patanti. yathā madhukararājānaṃ makṣikā utpatantam anūtpatanti niviśamānam anu niviśante tathendriyāṇi paraśarīrāveśe cittam anu vidhīyanta iti. 3.38
body.translated_text: The meaning is: for the restless mind that has no stable foundation in the body, bondage is the foundation [arising] from the power of the residue of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>). The loosening of that <s>karma</s> which is the cause of bondage occurs through the power of <s>samādhi</s>. And the awareness of the passages [of the mind] also arises from <s>samādhi</s> itself. Through the destruction of the <s>karma</s>-bondage and through the awareness of the passages of one's own mind, the <s>yogin</s> withdraws the mind from his own body and places it in other bodies. When the mind is placed [in another body], the senses follow it. Just as bees fly up when the queen bee flies up and settle down when she settles down, so the senses conform to the mind when entering another body. 3.38

body.text: udānajayāj jalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣv asaṅga utkrāntiś ca || YS_3.39 ||
body.translated_text: Through mastery of <s>udāna</s>, [there arises] non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and the ascent [at death]. || <s>YS</s> 3.39 ||

body.text: samastendriyavṛttiḥ prāṇādilakṣaṇā jīvanaṃ, tasya kriyā pañcatayī prāṇo mukhanāsikāgatir āhṛdayavṛttiḥ. samaṃ nayanāt samānaś cānābhivṛttiḥ. apanayanād apāna āpādatalavṛttiḥ unnayanād udāna āśirovṛttiḥ vyāpī vyāna iti. eṣāṃ pradhānaṃ prāṇaḥ udānajayāj jalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣv asaṅga utkrāntiś ca prāyaṇakāle bhavati tāṃ vaśitvena pratipadyate. 3.39
body.translated_text: The total activity of the senses, characterized by the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>) and the rest, is the life-force. Its function is fivefold: <s>prāṇa</s> is the movement through the mouth and nostrils, operating up to the heart. <s>Samāna</s>, from its equalizing [function], operates at the navel. <s>Apāna</s>, from its downward movement, operates from the feet to the soles. <s>Udāna</s>, from its upward movement, operates up to the head. <s>Vyāna</s> is all-pervading. Among these, <s>prāṇa</s> is the chief. Through mastery of <s>udāna</s>, there is non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and the ascent at the time of death occurs, which one attains through mastery. 3.39

body.text: samānajayāj jvalanam || YS_3.40 ||
body.translated_text: Through mastery of <s>samāna</s>, effulgence [arises]. || <s>YS</s> 3.40 ||

body.text: jitasamānas tejasa upadhmānaṃ kṛtvā jvalayati. 3.40
body.translated_text: Having conquered <s>samāna</s>, one fans the fire (<s>tejas</s>) and causes it to blaze. 3.40

body.text: śrotrākāśayoḥ saṃbandhasaṃyamād divyaṃ śrotram || YS_3.41 ||
body.translated_text: Through <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the ear and space, divine hearing [arises]. || <s>YS</s> 3.41 ||

body.text:
sarvaśrotrāṇām ākāśaṃ pratiṣṭhā sarvaśabdānāṃ ca yathoktam --- tulyadeśaśravaṇānām ekadeśaśrutitvaṃ sarveṣāṃ bhavatīti tac caitad ākāśasya liṅgam.
  anāvaraṇaṃ coktam. tathāmūrtasyānāvaraṇadarśanād vibhutvam api prakhyātam ākāśasya. śabdagrahaṇānumitaṃ śrotram. badhirābadhirayor ekaḥ śabdaṃ gṛhṇāty aparo na gṛhṇātīti tasmāc chrotram eva śabdaviṣayam śrotrākāśayoḥ saṃbandhe kṛtasaṃyamasya yogino divyaṃ śrotraṃ pravartate. 3.41
body.translated_text: Space is the support of all hearing and of all sounds, as stated: 'For those who hear in the same place, the hearing of one place belongs to all' — and this is the mark of space. It has also been stated that [space] is unobstructed. Similarly, since it is formless and unobstructed, the all-pervasiveness of space is also well known. The ear is inferred from the grasping of sound: of a deaf and a non-deaf person, one grasps sound and the other does not — therefore the ear alone has sound as its object. For the <s>yogin</s> who has performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the ear and space, divine hearing arises. 3.41

body.text: kāyākāśayoḥ saṃbandhasaṃyamāl laghutūlasamāpatteś cākāśagamanam || YS_3.42 ||
body.translated_text: Through <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the body and space, and through absorption (<s>samāpatti</s>) on light cotton, movement through space [arises]. || <s>YS</s> 3.42 ||

body.text: yatra kāyas tatrākāśaṃ tasyāvakāśadānāt kāyasya tena saṃbandhaḥ prāptis tatra kṛtasaṃyamo jitvā tatsaṃbandhaṃ laghuṣu vā tūlādiṣv ā paramāṇubhyaḥ samāpattiṃ labdhvā jitasaṃbandho laghur bhavati. laghutvāc ca jale pādābhyāṃ viharati tatas tūrṇanābhitantumātre vihṛtya raśmiṣu viharati tato yatheṣṭam ākāśagatir asya bhavatīti. 3.42
body.translated_text: Where the body is, there is space — because it provides room for the body. That is the relationship, the contact. Having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on that and conquered that relationship, or having attained absorption on light things such as cotton, down to the atoms, one who has conquered the relationship becomes light. And from lightness, one walks upon water with one's feet; then, having walked upon the thread of a spider web, one walks upon the rays of light; then movement through space becomes possible at will. 3.42

body.text: bahir akalpitā vṛttir mahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ || YS_3.43 ||
body.translated_text: The external, unimaginable mental activity is the 'great disembodied [state]'; from that, the destruction of the covering of light. || <s>YS</s> 3.43 ||

body.text: śarīrād bahir manaso vṛttilābho videhā nāma dhāraṇā. sā yadi śarīrapratiṣṭhasya manaso bahirvṛttimātreṇa bhavati sā kalpitety ucyate. yā tu śarīranirapekṣā bahirbhūtasyaiva manaso bahirvṛttiḥ sā khalv akalpitā tatra kalpitayā sādhayanty akalpitāṃ mahāvidehām iti. yayā paraśarīrāṇy āviśanti yoginaḥ, tataś ca dhāraṇātaḥ prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya yadāvaraṇaṃ kleśakarmavipākatrayaṃ rajastamomūlaṃ tasya ca kṣayo bhavati. 3.43
body.translated_text: The attainment of mental activity outside the body is the concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) called 'disembodied' (<s>videhā</s>). If it occurs merely through the external activity of the mind while it is still established in the body, it is called 'imagined' (<s>kalpitā</s>). But the external activity of the mind that is truly outside the body and independent of the body — that is indeed 'unimaginable' (<s>akalpitā</s>). Through the imagined, they accomplish the unimaginable — the 'great disembodied state' (<s>mahāvidehā</s>). Through this, <s>yogins</s> enter other bodies. And from this concentration, there is the destruction of the covering of the luminous essence of <s>buddhi</s> (<s>buddhisattva</s>) — [the covering] consisting of the triad of afflictions, <s>karma</s>, and ripening, rooted in <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. 3.43

body.text: sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvasaṃyamād bhūtajayaḥ || YS_3.44 ||
body.translated_text: Through <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross form, essential nature, subtle [form], inherence, and purposefulness [of the elements], mastery of the elements [arises]. || <s>YS</s> 3.44 ||

body.text:
tatra pārthivādyāḥ śabdādayo viśeṣāḥ sahākārādibhir dharmaiḥ sthūlaśabdena paribhāṣitāḥ etad bhūtānāṃ prathamaṃ rūpam. dvitīyaṃ rūpaṃ svasāmānyaṃ mūrtir bhūmiḥ sneho jalaṃ vahnir uṣṇatā vāyuḥ praṇāmī sarvatogatir ākāśa ity etat svarūpaśabdenocyate.
  asya sāmānyasya śabdādayo viśeṣāḥ tathā coktam --- ekajātisamanvitānām eṣāṃ dharmamātravyāvṛttir iti.
  sāmānyaviśeṣasamudāyo 'tra dravyam. dviṣṭho hi samūhaḥ pratyastamitabhedāvayavānugataḥ śarīraṃ vṛkṣo yūthaṃ vanam iti.
  śabdenopāttabhedāvayavānugataḥ samūha ubhaye devamanuṣyāḥ samūhasya devā eko bhāgo manuṣyā dvitīyo bhāgas tābhyām evābhidhīyate samūhaḥ.
  sa ca bhedābhedavivakṣitaḥ. āmrāṇāṃ vanaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ saṃgha āmravaṇaṃ brāhmaṇasaṃgha iti.
  sa punar dvividho yutasiddhāvayavo 'yutasiddhāvayavaś ca. yutasiddhāvayavaḥ samūho vanaṃ saṃgha iti ayutasiddhāvayavaḥ saṃghātaḥ śarīraṃ vṛkṣaḥ paramāṇur iti. ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samūho dravyam iti patañjaliḥ etat svarūpam ity uktam.
  atha kim eṣāṃ sūkṣmarūpaṃ, tanmātraṃ bhūtakāraṇaṃ, tasyaiko 'vayavaḥ paramāṇuḥ sāmānyaviśeṣātmāyutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samudāya ity evaṃ sarvatanmātrāṇy etat tṛtīyam. atha bhūtānāṃ caturthaṃ rūpaṃ khyātikriyāsthitiśīlā guṇāḥ kāryasvabhāvānupātino 'nvayaśabdenoktāḥ. athaiṣāṃ pañcamaṃ rūpam arthavattvaṃ, bhogāpavargārthatā guṇeṣv evānvayinī, guṇās tanmātrabhūtabhautikeṣv iti sarvam arthavat. teṣv idānīṃ bhūteṣu pañcasu pañcarūpeṣu saṃyamāt tasya tasya rūpasya svarūpadarśanaṃ jayaś ca prādurbhavati. tatra pañca bhūtasvarūpāṇi jitvā bhūtajayī bhavati tajjayād vatsānusāriṇya iva gāvo 'sya saṃkalpānuvidhāyinyo bhūtaprakṛtayo bhavanti. 3.44
body.translated_text: Among these, the specific forms such as sound and the rest pertaining to earth and so forth, together with properties such as form and the like, are designated by the word 'gross' — this is the first aspect of the elements. The second aspect is their general [essential nature]: solidity is earth, viscosity is water, heat is fire, impulsion and omnipresence is air, openness is space — this is designated by the word 'essential nature' (<s>svarūpa</s>). The specific forms of this general are sound and the rest. And thus it is said: 'For those endowed with one common class, the distinction is by properties alone.' The aggregate of the general and the specific is the substance (<s>dravya</s>). An aggregate standing in two [aspects]: one in which distinctions are in abeyance but the parts are still present — that is body, tree, herd, forest. One in which the parts with their distinctions are taken up verbally — that is [for example] both gods and humans; gods are one part, humans the second part, and the aggregate is designated by both. That is expressed in terms of both distinction and non-distinction — [for example] 'a forest of mango trees,' 'a congregation of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.' This is again twofold: one whose parts exist separately and one whose parts cannot exist separately. An aggregate with separately existing parts: a forest, a congregation. An aggregate with inseparable parts: a composite — body, tree, atom. An aggregate following the distinction of inseparable parts is 'substance' (<s>dravya</s>) according to <s>Patañjali</s> — this is called 'essential nature.' Now what is their subtle form? The subtle element (<s>tanmātra</s>), the cause of the elements, whose one part is the atom — an aggregate following the distinction of inseparable parts having both general and specific nature — thus all subtle elements. This is the third [aspect]. The fourth aspect of the elements: the <s>guṇas</s>, whose nature is illumination, activity, and inertia, following the nature of their effects — these are designated by the word 'inherence' (<s>anvaya</s>). The fifth aspect is purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>) — the purpose of experience and liberation, which inheres in the <s>guṇas</s> alone, and the <s>guṇas</s> inhere in the subtle elements, elements, and elemental products — thus everything has purpose. Now, through <s>saṃyama</s> on the five elements in their five aspects, the vision of the nature of each aspect and mastery arises. Having thus conquered the five essential natures of the elements, one becomes a master of the elements. Through that mastery, the elemental principles become compliant to his intention, like cows following their calves. 3.44

body.text: tato 'ṇimādiprādurbhāvaḥ kāyasaṃpat taddharmānabhighātaś ca || YS_3.45 ||
body.translated_text: From that, the manifestation of the [eight powers] beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, bodily perfection, and non-obstruction by the properties [of the elements]. || <s>YS</s> 3.45 ||

body.text:
tatrāṇimā bhavaty aṇuḥ laghimā laghur bhavati mahimā mahān bhavati. prāptir aṅgulyagreṇāpi spṛśati candramasam. prākāmyam icchānabhighātaḥ bhūmāv unmajjati nimajjati yathodake. vaśitvaṃ bhūtabhautikeṣu vaśī bhavaty avaśyaś cānyeṣām īśitṛtvaṃ teṣāṃ prabhavāpyayavyūhānām īṣṭe. yatra kāmāvasāyitvaṃ satyasaṃkalpatā yathā saṃkalpas tathā bhūtaprakṛtīnām avasthānam. na ca śakto 'pi padārthaviparyāsaṃ karoti kasmāt anyasya yatra kāmāvasāyinaḥ pūrvasiddhasya tathā bhūteṣu saṃkalpād iti. etāny aṣṭāv aiśvaryāṇi.
  kāyasaṃpad vakṣyamāṇā taddharmānabhighātaś ca pṛthvī mūrtyā na niruṇaddhi yoginaḥ śarīrādikriyāṃ, śilām apy anuviśatīti. nāpaḥ snigdhāḥ kledayanti nāgnir uṣṇo dahati na vāyuḥ praṇāmī vahati anāvaraṇātmake 'py ākāśe bhavaty āvṛtakāyaḥ siddhānām apy adṛśyo bhavati. 3.45
body.translated_text: Among these: <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) — one becomes minute. <s>Laghimā</s> (lightness) — one becomes light. <s>Mahimā</s> (greatness) — one becomes great. <s>Prāpti</s> (attainment) — one touches the moon even with a fingertip. <s>Prākāmya</s> (irresistible will) — non-obstruction of desire: one plunges into and emerges from the earth as [one would] in water. <s>Vaśitva</s> (mastery) — one becomes master over the elements and elemental products, and is not subject to others. <s>Īśitṛtva</s> (lordship) — one commands the production, dissolution, and arrangement of those [elements]. <s>Yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> (fulfillment of resolve) — the truth of one's resolve: the elemental principles abide as one resolves. But even though capable, one does not reverse the order of things — why? Because of the resolve of another who has prior attainment of the 'fulfillment of resolve' with respect to the elements. These are the eight lordly powers (<s>aiśvarya</s>). Bodily perfection will be described [next]. And non-obstruction by the properties [of elements]: earth with its solidity does not obstruct the <s>yogin</s>'s bodily activities — he can enter even a rock. Waters with their viscosity do not wet him; fire with its heat does not burn him; wind with its impulsion does not carry him away; and even in space, whose nature is unobstructed, his body becomes concealed — he becomes invisible even to the <s>Siddhas</s>. 3.45

body.text: rūpalāvaṇyabalavajrasaṃhananatvāni kāyasaṃpat || YS_3.46 ||
body.translated_text: Beauty, grace, strength, and adamantine firmness of the body — this is bodily perfection. || <s>YS</s> 3.46 ||

body.text: darśanīyaḥ kāntimān atiśayabalo vajrasaṃhananaś ceti. 3.46
body.translated_text: One becomes beautiful, radiant, of surpassing strength, and with adamantine firmness of body. 3.46

body.text: grahaṇasvarūpāsmitānvayārthavattvasaṃyamād indriyajayaḥ || YS_3.47 ||
body.translated_text: Through <s>saṃyama</s> on grasping, essential nature, 'I-am-ness,' inherence, and purposefulness, mastery of the senses [arises]. || <s>YS</s> 3.47 ||

body.text: sāmānyaviśeṣātmā śabdādir grāhyaḥ teṣv indriyāṇāṃ vṛttir grahaṇam. na ca tatsāmānyamātragrahaṇākāraṃ katham anālocitaḥ sa viṣayaviśeṣa indriyeṇa manasānuvyavasīyeteti. svarūpaṃ punaḥ prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya sāmānyaviśeṣayor ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samūho dravyam indriyam. teṣāṃ tṛtīyaṃ rūpam asmitālakṣaṇo 'haṃkāraḥ. tasya sāmānyasyendriyāṇi viśeṣāḥ caturthaṃ rūpaṃ vyavasāyātmakāḥ prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlā guṇā yeṣām indriyāṇi sāhaṃkārāṇi pariṇāmaḥ. pañcamaṃ rūpaṃ guṇeṣu yad anugataṃ puruṣārthavattvam iti. pañcasv eteṣv indriyarūpeṣu yathākramaṃ saṃyamas tatra tatra jayaṃ kṛtvā pañcarūpajayād indriyajayaḥ prādurbhavati yoginaḥ. 3.47
body.translated_text: Sound and the rest, having both general and specific nature, are the graspable [objects]. The activity of the senses with respect to them is grasping (<s>grahaṇa</s>). And that is not merely the grasping of the general form — for how could a particular object, unconsidered [in its specificity], be ascertained by the sense and then by the mind? The essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) is again: of the luminous essence of <s>buddhi</s>, an aggregate following the distinction of inseparable parts having both general and specific nature — that is the substance which is the sense organ. Their third aspect is the ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) characterized by 'I-am-ness' (<s>asmitā</s>). The senses are the specifics of that general. The fourth aspect: the <s>guṇas</s>, whose nature is resolve, illumination, activity, and inertia — of which the senses together with the ego are the transformation. The fifth aspect is the purposefulness of <s>Puruṣa</s> that inheres in the <s>guṇas</s>. Through <s>saṃyama</s> in sequence on these five aspects of the senses, having achieved mastery in each, mastery of the senses (<s>indriyajaya</s>) arises from the conquest of the five aspects. 3.47

body.text: tato manojavitvaṃ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaś ca || YS_3.48 ||
body.translated_text: From that, speed of mind, the state of being without instruments [of perception], and mastery of <s>pradhāna</s> [arise]. || <s>YS</s> 3.48 ||

body.text: kāyasyānuttamo gatilābho manojavitvam. videhānām indriyāṇām abhipretadeśakālaviṣayāpekṣo vṛttilābho vikaraṇabhāvaḥ. sarvaprakṛtivikāravaśitvaṃ pradhānajaya ity etās tisraḥ siddhayo madhupratīkā ucyante etāś ca karaṇapañcarūpajayād adhigamyante. 3.48
body.translated_text: The supreme acquisition of the body is mental swiftness (<s>manojavitva</s>). The acquisition of the senses' functioning, independent of body — in relation to desired place, time, and object — is the state of acting without instruments (<s>vikaraṇabhāva</s>). Mastery over all modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s> is the conquest of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). These three perfections are called 'honey-faced' (<s>madhupratīkā</s>), and they are attained through the conquest of the fivefold instrument (the senses). (3.48)

body.text: sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ sarvajñātṛtvaṃ ca || YS_3.49 ||
body.translated_text: From mere discriminative knowledge of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> comes supremacy over all states of being and omniscience. (YS 3.49)

body.text:
nirdhūtarajastamomalasya buddhisattvasya pare vaiśāradye parasyāṃ vaśīkārasaṃjñāyāṃ vartamānasya sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrarūpapratiṣṭhasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvam. sarvātmāno guṇā vyavasāyavyavaseyātmakāḥ svāminaṃ kṣetrajñaṃ pratyaśeṣadṛśyātmatvenopasthitā ity arthaḥ. sarvajñātṛtvaṃ sarvātmanāṃ guṇānāṃ
 śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmatvena vyavasthitānām akramopārūḍhaṃ vivekajaṃ jñānam ity arthaḥ. ity eṣā viśokā nāma siddhir yāṃ prāpya yogī sarvajñaḥ kṣīṇakleśabandhano vaśī viharati. 3.49
body.translated_text: When the <s>sattva</s> of the intellect, purged of the stain of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, stands in the supreme proficiency, in the supreme state of mastery, established in the mere form of discriminative knowledge of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, and with the seeds of afflictions burned — then comes supremacy over all states of being. All the <s>guṇas</s>, whose nature is determiner and determinable, present themselves to the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field), their master, as entirely of the nature of the seen —

body.text: tadvairāgyād api doṣabījakṣaye kaivalyam || YS_3.50 ||
body.translated_text: From detachment even toward that, through the destruction of the seeds of defect, comes <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation). (YS 3.50)

body.text: yadāsyaivaṃ bhavati kleśakarmakṣaye sattvasyāyaṃ vivekapratyayo dharmaḥ sattvaṃ ca heyapakṣe nyastaṃ puruṣaś cāpariṇāmī śuddho 'nyaḥ sattvād iti. evam asya tato virajyamānasya yāni kleśabījāni dagdhaśālibījakalpāny aprasavasamarthāni tāni saha manasā pratyastaṃ gacchanti. teṣu pralīneṣu puruṣaḥ punar idaṃ tāpatrayaṃ na bhuṅkte. tad eteṣāṃ guṇānāṃ manasi karmakleśavipākasvarūpeṇābhivyaktānāṃ caritārthānāṃ pratiprasave puruṣasyātyantiko guṇaviyogaḥ kaivalyaṃ tadā svarūpapratiṣṭhā citiśaktir eva puruṣa iti. 3.50
body.translated_text: When this understanding arises in him — that upon the destruction of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s>, this discriminative cognition is a property of <s>sattva</s>, and that <s>sattva</s> is placed on the side of what is to be abandoned, while <s>Puruṣa</s> is unchanging, pure, and other than <s>sattva</s> — thus, for one becoming detached, the seeds of affliction, rendered like burnt rice-seeds, incapable of germination, together with the mind —

body.text: sthānyupanimantraṇe saṅgasmayākaraṇaṃ punar aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt || YS_3.51 ||
body.translated_text: When invited by the celestial beings of high station, there should be no attachment or pride, for there would be a return to the undesirable. (YS 3.51)

body.text:
catvāraḥ khalv amī yoginaḥ prāthamakalpiko madhubhūmikaḥ prajñājyotir atikrāntabhāvanīyaś ceti. tatrābhyāsī pravṛttamātrajyotiḥ prathamaḥ ṛtaṃbharaprajño dvitīyaḥ bhūtendriyajayī tṛtīyaḥ sarveṣu bhāviteṣu bhāvanīyeṣu kṛtarakṣābandhaḥ kartavyasādhanād imān. caturtho yas tv atikrāntabhāvanīyas tasya cittapratisarga eko 'rthaḥ saptavidhāsya prāntabhūmiprajñā.
  tatra madhumatīṃ bhūmiṃ sākṣātkurvato brāhmaṇasya sthānino devāḥ sattvaviśuddhim anupaśyantaḥ sthānair upanimantrayante bho ihāsyatām iha ramyatāṃ kamanīyo 'yaṃ bhogaḥ kamanīyeyaṃ kanyā rasāyanam idaṃ jarāmṛtyuṃ bādhate vaihāyasam idaṃ yānam amī kalpadrumāḥ puṇyā mandākinī siddhā maharṣaya uttamā anukūlā apsaraso divye śrotracakṣuṣī vajropamaḥ kāyaḥ svaguṇaiḥ sarvam idam upārjitam āyuṣmatā pratipadyatām idam akṣayam ajaram amarasthānaṃ devānāṃ priyam iti. evam abhidhīyamānaḥ saṅgadoṣān bhāvayed ghoreṣu saṃsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā jananamaraṇāndhakāre viparivartamānena kathaṃcid āsāditaḥ kleśatimiravināśī yogapradīpas tasya caite tṛṣṇāyonayo viṣayavāyavaḥ pratipakṣāḥ. sa khalv ahaṃ labdhālokaḥ katham anayā viṣayamṛgatṛṣṇayā vañcitas tasyaiva punaḥ pradīptasya saṃsārāgner ātmānam indhanīkuryām iti. svasti vaḥ svapnopamebhyaḥ kṛpaṇajanaprārthanīyebhyo viṣayebhya ity evaṃ niścitamatiḥ samādhiṃ bhāvayet.
  saṅgam akṛtvā smayam api na kuryād evam ahaṃ devānām api prārthanīya iti smayād ayaṃ susthitaṃmanyatayā mṛtyunā keśeṣu gṛhītam ivātmānaṃ na bhāvayiṣyati. tathā cāsya cchidrāntaraprekṣī nityaṃ yatnopacaryaḥ pramādo labdhavivaraḥ kleśān uttambhayiṣyati tataḥ punar aniṣṭaprasaṅgaḥ. evam asya saṅgasmayāv akurvato bhāvito 'rtho dṛḍhībhaviṣyati bhāvanīyaś cārtho 'bhimukhībhaviṣyatīti. 3.51
body.translated_text: There are indeed four types of <s>yogins</s>: the beginner (<s>prāthamakalpika</s>), the one at the 'honey stage' (<s>madhubhūmika</s>), the one with the light of wisdom (<s>prajñājyoti</s>), and the one who has transcended what is to be cultivated (<s>atikrāntabhāvanīya</s>). Among these, the first is a practitioner in whom the light has merely begun to arise; the second possesses truth-bearing wisdom (<s>ṛtaṃbharā prajñā</s>); the third has conquered the elements and the senses; the fourth, having established protection for all that has been cultivated and is to be cultivated, through the means to be accomplished —

body.text: kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṃyamād vivekajaṃ jñānam || YS_3.52 ||
body.translated_text: From <s>saṃyama</s> on the moment and its sequence comes knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>). (YS 3.52)

body.text:
yathāpakarṣaparyantaṃ dravyaṃ paramāṇur evaṃ paramāpakarṣaparyantaḥ kālaḥ kṣaṇo yāvatā vā samayena calitaḥ paramāṇuḥ pūrvadeśaṃ jahyād uttaradeśam upasaṃpadyeta sa kālaḥ kṣaṇaḥ. tatpravāhāvicchedas tu kramaḥ kṣaṇatatkramayor nāsti vastusamāhāra iti buddhisamāhāro muhūrtāhorātrādayaḥ. sa khalv ayaṃ kālo vastuśūnyo 'pi buddhinirmāṇaḥ śabdajñānānupātī laukikānāṃ vyutthitadarśanānāṃ vastusvarūpa ivāvabhāsate.
  kṣaṇas tu vastupatitaḥ kramāvalambī kramaś ca kṣaṇānantaryātmā taṃ kālavidaḥ kāla ity ācakṣate yoginaḥ. na ca dvau kṣaṇau saha bhavataḥ kramaś ca na dvayoḥ sahabhuvor asaṃbhavāt. pūrvasmād uttarabhāvino yadānantaryaṃ kṣaṇasya sa kramaḥ tasmād vartamāna evaikaḥ kṣaṇo na pūrvottarakṣaṇāḥ santīti. tasmān nāsti tatsamāhāraḥ ye tu bhūtabhāvinaḥ kṣaṇās te pariṇāmānvitā vyākhyeyāḥ tenaikena kṣaṇena kṛtsno lokaḥ pariṇāmam anubhavati. tatkṣaṇopārūḍhāḥ khalv amī sarve dharmāḥ tayoḥ kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṃyamāt tayoḥ sākṣātkaraṇam. tataś ca vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ prādurbhavati. 3.52
body.translated_text: Just as the ultimate limit of the reduction of a substance is the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), so the ultimate limit of the reduction of time is the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) — the time in which a moving atom leaves one position and reaches the next is the moment. The unbroken flow of moments is sequence (<s>krama</s>). There is no real aggregate of moment and its sequence —

body.text: tasya viṣayaviśeṣa upakṣipyate ---

children.text: jātilakṣaṇadeśair anyatānavacchedāt tulyayos tataḥ pratipattiḥ || YS_3.53 ||
children.translated_text: From that comes the discernment of two things that are alike, when they cannot be distinguished by class, characteristic, or position. (YS 3.53)

body.translated_text: The specific object of that [discriminative knowledge] is now indicated —

body.text:
tulyayor deśalakṣaṇasārūpye jātibhedo 'nyatāyā hetuḥ, gaur iyaṃ baḍaveyam iti. tulyadeśajātīyatve lakṣaṇam anyatvakaraṃ kālākṣī gauḥ svastimatī gaur iti. dvayor āmalakayor jātilakṣaṇasārūpyād deśabhedo 'nyatvakara idaṃ pūrvam idam uttaram iti. yadā tu pūrvam āmalakam anyavyagrasya jñātur uttaradeśa upāvartyate tadā tulyadeśatve pūrvam etad uttaram etad iti pravibhāgānupapattiḥ. asaṃdigdhena ca tattvajñānena bhavitavyam ity ata idam uktaṃ tataḥ pratipattir vivekajajñānād iti.
  kathaṃ, pūrvāmalakasahakṣaṇo deśa uttarāmalakasahakṣaṇād deśād bhinnaḥ te cāmalake svadeśakṣaṇānubhavabhinne. anyadeśakṣaṇānubhavas tu tayor anyatve hetur iti. etena dṛṣṭāntena paramāṇos tulyajātilakṣaṇadeśasya pūrvaparamāṇudeśasahakṣaṇasākṣātkaraṇād uttarasya paramāṇos taddeśānupapattāv uttarasya taddeśānubhavo bhinnaḥ sahakṣaṇabhedāt tayor īśvarasya yogino 'nyatvapratyayo bhavatīti.
  apare tu varṇayanti --- ye 'ntyā viśeṣās te 'nyatāpratyayaṃ kurvantīti tatrāpi deśalakṣaṇabhedo mūrtivyavadhijātibhedaś cānyatve hetuḥ. kṣaṇabhedas tu yogibuddhigamya eveti ata uktaṃ mūrtivyavadhijātibhedābhāvān nāsti mūlapṛthaktvam iti vārṣagaṇyaḥ. 3.53
body.translated_text: When two things are similar in position, characteristic, and form, the difference of class is the cause of differentiation: 'This is a cow, that is a mare.' When they are of the same position and class, the characteristic creates the distinction: 'This cow is <s>Kālākṣī</s>, that cow is <s>Svastimatī</s>.' When two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits are similar in class and characteristic, the difference of position creates the distinction: 'This is the former, that is the latter.' When —

body.text: tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam || YS_3.54 ||
body.translated_text: The knowledge born of discrimination is called 'delivering' (<s>tāraka</s>), has all things as its object, has all modes as its object, and is non-sequential. (YS 3.54)

body.text: tārakam iti svapratibhottham anaupadeśikam ity arthaḥ sarvaviṣayaṃ nāsya kiṃcid aviṣayībhūtam ity arthaḥ. sarvathāviṣayam atītānāgatapratyutpannaṃ sarvaṃ paryāyaiḥ sarvathā jānātīty arthaḥ. akramam ity ekakṣaṇopārūḍhaṃ sarvaṃ sarvathā gṛhṇātīty arthaḥ. etad vivekajaṃ jñānaṃ paripūrṇam asyaivāṃśo yogapradīpo madhumatīṃ bhūmim upādāya yāvad asya parisamāptir iti. 3.54
body.translated_text: Delivering (<s>tāraka</s>) means it arises from one's own intuition, not from instruction. 'All things as its object' means nothing remains outside its scope. 'All modes as its object' means it knows everything — past, future, and present — in all its modes. 'Non-sequential' means it grasps everything in all its modes in a single moment —

body.text: prāptavivekajajñānasyāprāptavivekajajñānasya vā ---

children.translated_text: When the purity of <s>sattva</s> equals that of <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation). (YS 3.55)

body.translated_text: For one who has attained discriminative knowledge, or for one who has not yet attained it —

body.text: yadā nirdhūtarajastamomalaṃ buddhisattvaṃ puruṣasyānyatāpratītimātrādhikāraṃ dagdhakleśabījaṃ bhavati tadā puruṣasya śuddhisārūpyam ivāpannaṃ bhavati, tadā puruṣasyopacaritabhogābhāvaḥ śuddhiḥ. etasyām avasthāyāṃ kaivalyaṃ bhavatīśvarasyānīśvarasya vā vivekajajñānabhāgina itarasya vā. na hi dagdhakleśabījasya jñāne punar apekṣā kācid asti sattvaśuddhidvāreṇaitat samādhijam aiśvaryaṃ jñānaṃ copakrāntam. paramārthatas tu jñānād adarśanaṃ nivartate tasmin nivṛtte na santy uttare kleśāḥ. kleśābhāvāt karmavipākābhāvaḥ caritādhikārāś caitasyām avasthāyāṃ guṇā na puruṣasya punar dṛśyatvenopatiṣṭhante. tatpuruṣasya kaivalyaṃ, tadā puruṣaḥ svarūpamātrajyotir amalaḥ kevalī bhavati. 3.55
