body.translated_text: When the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), its impurity of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> shaken off, has its function limited merely to the cognition of the otherness of <s>Puruṣa</s>, and its seeds of affliction are burnt — then it becomes as if it has attained a likeness to the purity of <s>Puruṣa</s>; then there is purity of <s>Puruṣa</s>, which is the absence of the figuratively attributed experience. In this state, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) occurs — whether for the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) or for one who is not the Lord but possesses knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekajajñāna</s>), or for another. For one whose seeds of affliction are burnt, there is no further need of knowledge through the gateway of the purity of <s>sattva</s> — this sovereign power and knowledge born of <s>samādhi</s> has already been attained. In ultimate reality, however, it is from knowledge that ignorance ceases; when that ceases, there are no further afflictions. From the absence of afflictions, there is the absence of the fruition of <s>karma</s>. And the <s>guṇas</s>, having fulfilled their function in this state, no longer present themselves to <s>Puruṣa</s> as objects to be seen. That is the <s>kaivalya</s> of <s>Puruṣa</s>; then <s>Puruṣa</s> abides as pure light of its own nature, stainless and alone. [YS 3.55]

body.text: iti śrīpātañjale sāṃkhyapravacane yogaśāstre vyāsabhāṣye vibhūtipādas tṛtīyaḥ 3.
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter on Supernatural Powers (<s>Vibhūtipāda</s>), in the <s>Vyāsabhāṣya</s> on the <s>Yogaśāstra</s> of the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana</s> by the venerable <s>Patañjali</s>. [3]

body.text: janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ || YS_4.1 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, austerity (<s>tapas</s>), or <s>samādhi</s>. [YS 4.1]

body.text: dehāntaritā janmanā siddhiḥ oṣadhibhir asurabhavaneṣu rasāyanenety evamādiḥ. mantrair ākāśagamanāṇimādilābhaḥ. tapasā saṃkalpasiddhiḥ, kāmarūpī yatra tatra kāmaga ity evamādi samādhijāḥ siddhayo vyākhyātāḥ. 4.1
body.translated_text: The <s>siddhi</s> arising from birth is that which belongs to one who has taken another body. That arising from herbs — for example, by means of elixirs (<s>rasāyana</s>) in the abodes of <s>Asuras</s>, and so forth. By <s>mantras</s> — the attainment of flying through the sky, <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute), and the like. By <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — the fulfillment of resolve: becoming one of any desired form, going wherever one wishes, and so forth. The <s>siddhis</s> born of <s>samādhi</s> have already been explained. [4.1]

body.text: tatra kāyendriyāṇām anyajātīyapariṇatānām ---

children.translated_text: The transformation into another class of existence (<s>jātyantarapariṇāma</s>) [occurs] through the filling in (<s>āpūra</s>) of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature). [YS 4.2]

body.translated_text: Now, regarding the body and sense organs that have transformed into a different class —

body.text: pūrvapariṇāmāpāya uttarapariṇāmopajanas teṣām apūrvāvayavānupraveśād bhavati. kāyendriyaprakṛtayaś ca svaṃ svaṃ vikāram anugṛhṇanty āpūreṇa dharmādinimittam apekṣamāṇā iti. 4.2
body.translated_text: The departure of the previous transformation and the arising of the subsequent transformation occur through the entrance of novel parts (<s>apūrvāvayava</s>). And the <s>prakṛtis</s> (natures) of the body and sense organs support their own respective modifications through the filling in, while depending on conditions such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest. [4.2]

body.text: nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat || YS_4.3 ||
body.translated_text: The incidental cause (<s>nimitta</s>) does not set the <s>prakṛtis</s> in motion; rather, from that [incidental cause comes] the removal of obstacles — like a farmer. [YS 4.3]

body.text: na hi dharmādi nimittaṃ tatprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ bhavati na kāryeṇa kāraṇaṃ pravartyata iti kathaṃ tarhi, varaṇabhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat. yathā kṣetrikaḥ kedārād apāṃ pūrṇāt kedārāntaraṃ piplāvayiṣuḥ samaṃ nimnaṃ nimnataraṃ vā nāpaḥ pāṇināpakarṣaty āvaraṇaṃ tv āsāṃ bhinatti tasmin bhinne svayam evāpaḥ kedārāntaram āplāvayanti tathā dharmaḥ prakṛtīnām āvaraṇadharmaṃ bhinatti tasmin bhinne svayam eva prakṛtayaḥ svaṃ svaṃ vikāram āplāvayanti. yathā vā sa eva kṣetrikas tasminn eva kedāre na prabhavaty audakān bhaumān vā rasān dhānyamūlāny anupraveśayituṃ, kiṃ tarhi mudgagavedhukaśyāmākādīṃs tato 'pakarṣati. apakṛṣṭeṣu teṣu svayam eva rasā dhānyamūlāny anupraviśanti, tathā dharmo nivṛttimātre kāraṇam adharmasya, śuddhyaśuddhyor atyantavirodhāt, na tu prakṛtipravṛttau dharmo hetur bhavatīti. atra nandīśvarādaya udāhāryāḥ viparyayeṇāpy adharmo dharmaṃ bādhate. tataś cāśuddhipariṇāma iti. tatrāpi nahuṣājagarādaya udāhāryāḥ. 4.3
body.translated_text: Indeed, <s>dharma</s> and the rest as incidental causes do not directly set the <s>prakṛtis</s> in motion — an effect does not impel a cause. How then? Rather, from that comes the removal of obstacles, like a farmer. Just as a farmer who wishes to irrigate one field from another field full of water — whether level, low, or lower — does not drag the water with his hand, but breaks the barrier; once that is broken, the water of its own accord floods the other field — so too <s>dharma</s> breaks the obstructive quality of the <s>prakṛtis</s>; once that is broken, the <s>prakṛtis</s> of their own accord flood their respective modifications. Or, just as that same farmer in that same field is unable to introduce the aqueous and earthy nutrients into the grain-roots, but rather removes the weeds — mung beans, barnyard millet, millet, and the like — from them; once those are removed, the nutrients of their own accord enter the grain-roots — so too <s>dharma</s> is merely the cause of the cessation of <s>adharma</s>, due to the absolute opposition between purity and impurity; but <s>dharma</s> is not the cause of the activity of <s>prakṛti</s>. Here, <s>Nandīśvara</s> and others may be cited as examples. Conversely too, <s>adharma</s> obstructs <s>dharma</s>, and thence the transformation into impurity. In that case, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, <s>Ajagara</s>, and others may be cited as examples. [4.3]

body.text: yadā tu yogī bahūn kāyān nirmimīte tadā kim ekamanaskās te bhavanty athānekamanaskā iti ---

children.translated_text: The created minds (<s>nirmāṇacittāni</s>) [arise] from the mere sense of I-am-ness (<s>asmitāmātra</s>) alone. [YS 4.4]

body.translated_text: Now, when a <s>yogin</s> creates many bodies, do they have one mind or many minds? —

body.text: asmitāmātraṃ cittakāraṇam upādāya nirmāṇacittāni karoti, tataḥ sacittāni bhavantīti. 4.4
body.translated_text: Taking the mere sense of I-am-ness (<s>asmitāmātra</s>), which is the cause of mind, as the material basis, he fashions the created minds; from that they become endowed with mind. [4.4]

body.text: pravṛttibhede prayojakaṃ cittam ekam anekeṣām || YS_4.5 ||
body.translated_text: When there is diversity of activity, the directing mind is one among the many. [YS 4.5]

body.text: bahūnāṃ cittānāṃ katham ekacittābhiprāyapuraḥsarā pravṛttir iti sarvacittānāṃ prayojakaṃ cittam ekaṇ nirmimīte, tataḥ pravṛttibhedaḥ. 4.5
body.translated_text: How do the many minds act in accordance with the intention of one mind? The one directing mind creates all the minds; from that arises the diversity of activity. [4.5]

body.text: tatra dhyānajam anāśayam || YS_4.6 ||
body.translated_text: Among these, that which is born of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is without residual deposit (<s>anāśaya</s>). [YS 4.6]

body.text: pañcavidhaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhaya iti. tatra yad eva dhyānajaṃ cittaṃ tad evānāśayaṃ tasyaiva nāsty āśayo rāgādipravṛttir nātaḥ puṇyapāpābhisaṃbandhaḥ kṣīṇakleśatvād yogina iti itareṣāṃ tu vidyate karmāśayaḥ. 4.6
body.translated_text: The created mind is of five kinds, as stated in 'The <s>siddhis</s> arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, austerity, or <s>samādhi</s>.' Among these, only the mind born of meditation is without residual deposit — it alone has no deposit of activity such as attachment and the rest; hence there is no connection with merit or demerit, because the <s>yogin</s>'s afflictions are destroyed. But for the others, there exists a residual deposit of <s>karma</s>. [4.6]

body.text: yataḥ ---

children.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> of a <s>yogin</s> is neither white nor black; for others it is of three kinds. [YS 4.7]

body.translated_text: Because —

body.text: catuṣpadī khalv iyaṃ karmajātiḥ kṛṣṇā śuklakṛṣṇā śuklāśuklākṛṣṇā ceti. tatra kṛṣṇā durātmanām, śuklakṛṣṇā bahiḥsādhanasādhyā. tatra parapīḍānugrahadvāreṇaiva karmāśayapracayaḥ śuklā tapaḥsvādhyāyadhyānavatām. sā hi kevale manasy āyattatvād abahiḥsādhanādhīnā na parān pīḍayitvā bhavati. aśuklākṛṣṇā saṃnyāsināṃ kṣīṇakleśānāṃ caramadehānām iti tatrāśuklaṃ yogina eva phalasaṃnyāsād akṛṣṇaṃ cānupādānāt itareṣāṃ tu bhūtānāṃ pūrvam eva trividham iti. 4.7
body.translated_text: This classification of <s>karma</s> is indeed fourfold: black, white-and-black, white, and neither-white-nor-black. Among these, the black belongs to the evil-natured. The white-and-black is accomplished through external means; therein, the accumulation of <s>karma</s>-deposits occurs only through the door of causing pain or benefit to others. The white belongs to those devoted to austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>); since it depends solely on the mind, it is not dependent on external means and does not come about through causing pain to others. The neither-white-nor-black belongs to renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsins</s>) whose afflictions are destroyed and who are in their final body. Among these, the 'not-white' applies to the <s>yogin</s> alone, due to renunciation of the fruit; and the 'not-black,' due to non-appropriation. But for other beings, [<s>karma</s>] is previously stated as threefold. [4.7]

body.text: tatas tadvipākānuguṇānām evābhivyaktir vāsanānām || YS_4.8 ||
body.translated_text: From that, the manifestation of only those latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) that correspond to the fruition of that [<s>karma</s>]. [YS 4.8]

body.text: tata iti trividhāt karmaṇaḥ, tadvipākānuguṇānām eveti yajjātīyasya karmaṇo yo vipākas tasyānuguṇā yā vāsanāḥ karmavipākam anuśerate tāsām evābhivyaktiḥ. na hi daivaṃ karma vipacyamānaṃ nārakatiryaṅmanuṣyavāsanābhivyaktinimittaṃ saṃbhavati kiṃtu daivānuguṇā evāsya vāsanā vyajyante nārakatiryaṅmanuṣyeṣu caivaṃ samānaś carcaḥ. 4.8
body.translated_text: "From that" means from the threefold <s>karma</s>. "Corresponding to the fruition of that" means: whatever class of <s>karma</s> has whatever fruition, the <s>vāsanās</s> that follow along with that <s>karma</s>-fruition — of those alone is there manifestation. For it is not possible that divine <s>karma</s> ripening would occasion the manifestation of <s>vāsanās</s> of hell-beings, animals, or humans; rather, only <s>vāsanās</s> corresponding to the divine [realm] become manifest. The same reasoning applies for hell-beings, animals, and humans. [4.8]

body.text: jātideśakālavyavahitānām apy ānantaryaṃ smṛtisaṃskārayor ekarūpatvāt || YS_4.9 ||
body.translated_text: Even though separated by class, place, and time, there is immediate succession [of <s>vāsanās</s>], because memory and <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) are of one form. [YS 4.9]

body.text: vṛṣadaṃśavipākodayaḥ svavyañjakāñjanābhivyaktaḥ. sa yadi jātiśatena vā dūradeśatayā vā kalpaśatena vā vyavahitaḥ punaś ca svavyañjakāñjana evodiyād drāg ity evaṃ pūrvānubhūtavṛṣadaṃśavipākābhisaṃskṛtā vāsanā upādāya vyajyeta. kasmāt, yato vyavahitānām apy āsāṃ sadṛśaṃ karmābhivyajñakaṃ nimittībhūtam ity ānantaryam eva. kutaś ca, smṛtisaṃskārayor ekarūpatvāt yathānubhavās tathā saṃskārāḥ. te ca karmavāsanānurūpāḥ yathā ca vāsanās tathā smṛtir iti jātideśakālavyavahitebhyaḥ saṃskārebhyaḥ smṛtiḥ. smṛteś ca punaḥ saṃskārā ityevam ete smṛtisaṃskārāḥ karmāśayavṛttilābhavaśād vyajyante ataś ca vyavahitānām api nimittanaimittikabhāvānucchedād ānantaryam eva siddham iti. 4.9
body.translated_text: The arising of the fruition of a bull-bite [experience] is manifested by its own manifesting stimulus. If that [experience] is separated by a hundred births, or by a distant place, or by a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (eons), and if its own manifesting stimulus arises again quickly — then the <s>vāsanā</s> conditioned by the previously experienced bull-bite fruition would become manifest, taking [that stimulus] as its basis. Why? Because even for those separated [by class, place, and time], the <s>karma</s> that is similar and serves as the manifesting cause has become the occasion, and hence there is immediate succession. And why? Because memory and <s>saṃskāras</s> are of one form — as are the experiences, so are the <s>saṃskāras</s>. And they correspond to the <s>karma</s>-<s>vāsanās</s>; and as are the <s>vāsanās</s>, so is the memory. Thus from <s>saṃskāras</s> separated by class, place, and time comes memory; and from memory come <s>saṃskāras</s> again. In this way, these memories and <s>saṃskāras</s> become manifest through the force of gaining the activity of the <s>karma</s>-deposit. Therefore, even for those separated, the relation of cause and effect is unbroken, and hence immediate succession is established. [4.9]

body.text: tāsām anāditvaṃ cāśiṣo nityatvāt || YS_4.10 ||
body.translated_text: And they (<s>vāsanās</s>) are beginningless, because the desire to live (<s>āśis</s>) is eternal. [YS 4.10]

body.text:
tāsāṃ vāsanānām āśiṣo nityatvād anāditvam. yeyam ātmāśīr mā na bhūvaṃ bhūyāsam iti.sarvasya dṛśyate sā na svābhāvikī. kasmāt jātamātrasya jantor ananubhūtamaraṇadharmakasya dveṣaduḥkhānusmṛtinimitto maraṇatrāsaḥ kathaṃ bhavet na ca svābhāvikaṃ vastu nimittam upādatte. tasmād anādivāsanānuviddham idaṃ cittaṃ nimittavaśāt kāścid eva vāsanāḥ pratilabhya puruṣasya bhogāyopāvartata iti.
  ghaṭaprāsādapradīpakalpaṃ saṃkocavikāsi cittaṃ śarīraparimāṇākāramātram ity apare pratipannāḥ tathā cāntarābhāvaḥ saṃsāraś ca yukta iti.
  vṛttir evāsya vibhunaś cittasya saṃkocavikāsinīty ācāryaḥ. tac ca dharmādinimittāpekṣam. nimittaṃ ca dvividham --- bāhyam ādhyātmikaṃ ca. śarīrādisādhanāpekṣaṃ bāhyaṃ stutidānābhivādanādi, cittamātrādhīnaṃ śraddhādy adhyātmikam. tathā coktam --- ye caite maitryādayo dhyāyināṃ vihārās te bāhyasādhananiranugrahātmānaḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ dharmam abhinirvartayanti. tayor mānasaṃ balīyaḥ. kathaṃ, jñānavairāgye kenātiśayyete, daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ ca cittabalavyatirekeṇa śārīreṇa karmaṇā śūnyaṃ kaḥ kartum utsaheta samudram agastyavad vā pibet. 4.10
body.translated_text:
Those <s>vāsanās</s> are beginningless because the desire to live is eternal. This self-desire — 'May I not cease to be! May I continue to exist!' — is seen in everyone; it is not natural [i.e., innate without cause]. Why? Because for a being just born, who has not yet experienced the nature of death, how could there be the terror of death, which is caused by the memory of the suffering of death? And a natural thing does not depend on a cause. Therefore this mind is pervaded by beginningless <s>vāsanās</s>, and through the force of causes, obtaining certain <s>vāsanās</s>, it turns to serve the experience of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Some maintain that the mind, like a pot, a palace, or a lamp, contracts and expands, being limited in size merely to the form of the body — and accordingly, intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) and the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> are tenable.
But the <s>Ācārya</s> [Vyāsa] holds that the mind is all-pervading, and it is only its function (<s>vṛtti</s>) that contracts and expands. And that depends on conditions such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest. Conditions are of two kinds — external and internal. The external depends on physical means such as the body and so forth — praise, gifts, salutation, and the like. The internal depends on the mind alone — faith and the like. And thus it has been said: Those states of abiding such as loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the rest, which are the practices of meditators, being devoid of dependence on external means, produce supreme <s>dharma</s>. Of the two, the mental is more powerful. How so? By what can knowledge and dispassion be surpassed? And who could make the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest empty by mere bodily action, without the force of the mind? Or who could drink the ocean like <s>Agastya</s>? [4.10]

body.text: hetuphalāśrayālambanaiḥ saṃgṛhītatvād eṣām abhāve tadabhāvaḥ || YS_4.11 ||
body.translated_text: Because [<s>vāsanās</s>] are held together by cause, effect, substratum, and object-support, in the absence of these, there is the absence of those [<s>vāsanās</s>]. [YS 4.11]

body.text: hetur dharmāt sukham adharmād duḥkhaṃ sukhād rāgo duḥkhād dveṣas tataś ca prayatnas tena manasā vācā kāyena vā parispandamānaḥ param anugṛhṇāty upahanti vā tataḥ punar dharmādharmau sukhaduḥkhe rāgadveṣāv iti pravṛttam idaṃ ṣaḍaraṃ saṃsāracakram. asya ca pratikṣaṇam āvartamānasyāvidyā netrī mūlaṃ sarvakleśānām ity eṣa hetuḥ. phalaṃ tu yam āśritya yasya pratyutpannatā dharmādeḥ, na hy apūrvopajanaḥ. manas tu sādhikāram āśrayo vāsanānām. na hy avasitādhikāre manasi nirāśrayā vāsanāḥ sthātum utsahante. yad abhimukhībhūtaṃ vastu yāṃ vāsanāṃ vyanakti tasyās tadālambanam. evaṃ hetuphalāśrayālambanair etaiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ sarvā vāsanāḥ eṣām abhāve tatsaṃśrayāṇām api vāsanānām abhāvaḥ. 4.11
body.translated_text: The cause: from <s>dharma</s> [comes] happiness, from <s>adharma</s> suffering; from happiness [comes] attachment, from suffering aversion; and from these, effort. Exerting oneself with mind, speech, or body, one either benefits or harms others. From that arise again <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, happiness and suffering, attachment and aversion — thus this six-spoked wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> revolves. And of this wheel, revolving moment by moment, ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the driver, the root of all afflictions — this is the cause. The fruit: the present existence of <s>dharma</s> and the rest depends on that [substratum] in which they inhere, for they do not arise from nothing. The mind, together with its function, is the substratum of the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions). For when the mind's function has ended, the <s>vāsanās</s>, being without a substratum, cannot persist. Whatever object comes before [the mind] reveals whichever <s>vāsanā</s> [corresponds to it] — that object is the support (<s>ālambana</s>) of that <s>vāsanā</s>. Thus all <s>vāsanās</s> are comprehended by these: cause, fruit, substratum, and support. In the absence of these, the <s>vāsanās</s> dependent on them also cease. 4.11

body.text: nāsty asataḥ saṃbhavaḥ, na cāsti sato vināśa iti dravyatvena saṃbhavantyaḥ kathaṃ nivartiṣyante vāsanā iti ---

children.translated_text: The past and future exist in their own form, due to the difference of time-phases of the properties. || YS_4.12 ||

body.translated_text: There is no coming into being of the non-existent, nor is there destruction of the existent. Since <s>vāsanās</s> exist as substances, how will they be eradicated? —

body.text:
bhaviṣyadvyaktikam anāgatam anubhūtavyaktikam atītaṃ svavyāpāropārūḍhaṃ vartamānaṃ, trayaṃ caitad vastu jñānasya jñeyam. yadi caitat svarūpato nābhaviṣyan nedaṃ nirviṣayaṃ jñānam udapatsyata. tasmād atītānāgataṃ svarūpato 'stīti. kiṃca bhogabhāgīyasya vāpavargabhāgīyasya vā karmaṇaḥ phalam utpitsu yadi nirupākhyam iti taduddeśena tena nimittena kuśalānuṣṭhānaṃ na yujyeta. sataś ca phalasya nimittaṃ vartamānīkaraṇe samarthaṃ nāpūrvopajanane siddhaṃ nimittaṃ naimittikasya viśeṣānugrahaṇaṃ kurute nāpūrvam utpādayatīti.
  dharmī cānekadharmasvabhāvas tasya cādhvabhedena dharmāḥ pratyavasthitāḥ na ca yathā vartamānaṃ vyaktiviśeṣāpannaṃ dravyato 'sty evam atītam anāgataṃ ca. kathaṃ tarhi, svenaiva vyaṅgyena svarūpeṇānāgatam asti. svena cānubhūtavyaktikena svarūpeṇātītam iti vartamānasyaivādhvanaḥ svarūpavyaktir iti na sā bhavaty atītānāgatayor adhvanoḥ. ekasya cādhvanaḥ samaye dvāv adhvanau dharmisamanvāgatau bhavata eveti nābhūtvā bhāvas trayāṇām adhvanām iti. 4.12
body.translated_text: The future has yet-to-be-manifested expression; the past has already-experienced expression; the present is that whose own function is operative. All three are real objects, the knowable of knowledge. If they did not exist in their own form, this knowledge would arise without an object. Therefore, the past and future exist in their own form. Moreover, if the fruit of an action — whether leading to enjoyment or to liberation — were non-existent, then purposeful practice directed toward it would be unjustified. An established cause is capable of making an existing fruit present, not of producing something entirely new. A cause confers a specific benefit upon its effect — it does not produce something from nothing. And the substratum possesses the nature of many properties, whose properties are established according to the difference of time-phases. But the past and future do not exist as substances with specific manifestation in the way the present does. How then? The future exists in its own form as that which is yet to be revealed. The past exists in its own form as that whose manifestation has been experienced. The manifestation of its own form belongs only to the present time-phase, not to the past or future time-phases. At the time of one time-phase, the other two time-phases are present as belonging to the substratum — hence there is no coming-into-being from non-being for the three time-phases. 4.12

body.text: te vyaktasūkṣmā guṇātmānaḥ || YS_4.13 ||
body.translated_text: They are manifest or subtle, and of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>. || YS_4.13 ||

children.text: te khalv amī tryadhvano dharmā vartamānā vyaktātmāno 'tītānāgatāḥ sūkṣmātmānaḥ ṣaḍaviśeṣarūpāḥ. sarvam idaṃ guṇānāṃ saṃniveśaviśeṣamātram iti paramārthato guṇātmānaḥ. tathā ca śāstrānuśāsanam ---
children.translated_text: These properties belonging to the three time-phases — the present ones have a manifest nature, and the past and future ones have a subtle nature, being in the form of the six undifferentiated [categories]. All this is nothing but a particular arrangement of the <s>guṇas</s> — hence in the ultimate sense, they are of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>. And so the scriptural teaching states —
'The supreme form of the <s>guṇas</s> does not come within the range of sight;

children.text: yat tu dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāptaṃ tan māyeva sutucchakam //" iti. 4.13
children.translated_text: what comes within the range of sight is as insignificant as an illusion.' 4.13

body.text: yadā tu sarve guṇāḥ katham ekaḥ śabda ekam indriyam iti ---

children.translated_text: The reality of an object [consists in] the unity of transformation. || YS_4.14 ||

body.translated_text: But if everything is [composed of] <s>guṇas</s>, how is there one sound and one sense-organ? —

body.text:
prakhyākriyāsthitiśīlānāṃ guṇānāṃ grahaṇātmakānāṃ karaṇabhāvenaikaḥ pariṇāmaḥ śrotram indriyaṃ, grāhyātmakānāṃ śabdatanmātrabhāvenaikaḥ pariṇāmaḥ śabdo viṣaya iti, śabdādīnāṃ mūrtisamānajātīyānām ekaḥ pariṇāmaḥ pṛthivīparamāṇus tanmātrāvayavas teṣāṃ caikaḥ pariṇāmaḥ pṛthivī gaur vṛkṣaḥ parvata ityevamādir bhūtāntareṣv api snehauṣṇyapraṇāmitvāvakāśadānāny upādāya sāmānyam ekavikārārambhaḥ samādheyaḥ.
  nāsty artho vijñānavisahacaraḥ, asti tu jñānam arthavisahacaraṃ svapnādau kalpitam ity anayā diśā ye vastusvarūpam apahnuvate jñānaparikalpanāmātraṃ vastu svapnaviṣayopamaṃ na paramārthato 'stīti ya āhus te tatheti pratyupasthitam idaṃ svamāhātmyena vastu katham apramāṇātmakena vikalpajñānabalena vastusvarūpam utsṛjya tad evāpalapantaḥ śraddheyavacanāḥ syuḥ. 4.14
body.translated_text: Of the <s>guṇas</s> — whose nature is luminosity (<s>prakhyā</s>), activity (<s>kriyā</s>), and stability (<s>sthiti</s>) — one transformation in the form of an instrument of apprehension is the sense of hearing; one transformation of the same [<s>guṇas</s>] in the form of the apprehensible, in the nature of sound-<s>tanmātra</s>, is the object of sound. One transformation of sound and the rest, being of the same class as form, is an earth-atom, a <s>tanmātra</s>-component; and one transformation of these is earth — a cow, a tree, a mountain, and so on. In the other elements too, taking up fluidity, heat, movement, and the provision of space, the generality of a single modification-product should be understood. There is no object independent of consciousness, but there is cognition independent of an [external] object, as in dreams and the like, which is merely imagined — those who, proceeding in this direction, deny the own-nature of objects, saying that reality is merely a construction of consciousness, comparable to dream-objects, and does not ultimately exist — how could they, while denying the very reality of the object that stands self-established through its own power, using the force of a conceptual cognition that itself lacks [valid] means of knowledge, be worthy of trust? 4.14

body.text: kutaś caitad anyāyyam ---

children.text: vastusāmye cittabhedāt tayor vibhaktaḥ panthāḥ || YS_4.15 ||
children.translated_text: Given the sameness of the object, because of the difference of minds, the paths of both are distinct. || YS_4.15 ||

body.translated_text: And why further is this [position] unreasonable? —

body.text:
bahucittālambanībhūtam ekaṃ vastu sādhāraṇaṃ, tat khalu naikacittaparikalpitaṃ nāpy anekacittaparikalpitaṃ kiṃtu svapratiṣṭham. kathaṃ, vastusāmye cittabhedāt dharmāpekṣaṃ cittasya vastusāmye 'pi sukhajñānaṃ bhavaty adharmāpekṣaṃ tata eva duḥkhajñānam avidyāpekṣaṃ tata eva mūḍhajñānaṃ samyagdarśanāpekṣaṃ tata eva mādhyasthyajñānam iti. kasya tac cittena parikalpitam. na cānyacittaparikalpitenārthenānyasya cittoparāgo yuktaḥ. tasmād vastujñānayor grāhyagrahaṇabhedabhinnayor vibhaktaḥ panthāḥ. nānayoḥ saṃkaragandho 'py astīti.
  sāṃkhyapakṣe punar vastu triguṇaṃ calaṃ ca guṇavṛttam iti dharmādinimittāpekṣaṃ cittair abhisaṃbadhyate. nimittānurūpasya ca pratyayasyotpadyamānasya tena tenātmanā hetur bhavati. kecid āhuḥ. jñānasahabhūr evārtho bhogyatvāt sukhādivad iti ta etayā dvārā sādhāraṇatvaṃ bādhamānāḥ pūrvottarakṣaṇeṣu vasturūpam evāpahnuvate. 4.15
body.translated_text: A single object, having become the support of many minds, is common [to all]. It is certainly not constructed by one mind alone, nor by many minds together, but rather is self-established. How so? Given the sameness of the object, due to the difference of minds: dependent on <s>dharma</s>, even when the object is the same, there arises knowledge of pleasure; dependent on <s>adharma</s>, there arises from the same [object] knowledge of suffering; dependent on ignorance, from the same [object] knowledge of confusion; dependent on right seeing, from the same [object] knowledge of equanimity. By whose mind is that [object] constructed? And it is not reasonable that one mind would be colored by an object constructed by another mind. Therefore, the paths of the object and knowledge — being distinct through the difference of the apprehensible and the apprehension — are separate. There is not even a trace of confusion between them. In the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view, moreover, an object is of the three <s>guṇas</s>, and the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is in motion — thus, dependent on conditions such as <s>dharma</s>, it is connected with minds. And the cognition, arising in accordance with the condition, becomes the cause [of experience] in this or that form. Some say: an object exists only as co-existent with consciousness, because it is an object of experience, like pleasure and the like. These, while contradicting the common accessibility [of objects] by this approach, in fact deny the very nature of the object in its preceding and succeeding moments. 4.15

body.text: na caikacittatantraṃ vastu tadapramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt || YS_4.16 ||
body.translated_text: Nor is an object dependent on a single mind; if it were unascertained [by that mind], what would it be then? || YS_4.16 ||

body.text: ekacittatantraṃ ced vastu syāt tadā citte vyagre niruddhe vāsvarūpam eva tenāparāmṛṣṭam anyasyāviṣayībhūtam apramāṇakam agṛhītasvabhāvakaṃ kenacit tadānīṃ kiṃ tat syāt. saṃbadhyamānaṃ ca punaś cittena kuta utpadyeta ye cāsyānupasthitā bhāgās te cāsya na syur evaṃ nāsti pṛṣṭham ity udaram api na gṛhyeta. tasmāt svatantro 'rthaḥ sarvapuruṣasādhāraṇaḥ svatantrāṇi ca cittāni pratipuruṣaṃ pravartante tayoḥ saṃbandhād upalabdhiḥ puruṣasya bhoga iti. 4.16
body.translated_text: If an object were dependent on a single mind, then when that mind is distracted or in cessation, the object — not apprehended by it, not being an object of any other [mind] — would be unascertained, of ungrasped nature. What would it then be? And when subsequently connected with a mind again, where would it arise from? And the parts of it not present [to that mind] would not exist — thus, [if] the back does not exist, the belly too would not be grasped. Therefore, the object is independent, common to all <s>puruṣas</s>; and minds are independent, operating for each <s>puruṣa</s>. From the connection of these two, apprehension occurs — the experience (<s>bhoga</s>) of <s>Puruṣa</s>. 4.16

body.text: taduparāgāpekṣitvāc cittasya vastu jñātājñātam || YS_4.17 ||
body.translated_text: An object is known or unknown to the mind depending on whether the mind is colored by it. || YS_4.17 ||

body.text: ayaskāntamaṇikalpā viṣayā ayaḥsadharmakaṃ cittam abhisaṃbandhyoparañjayanti. yena ca viṣayeṇoparaktaṃ cittaṃ sa viṣayo jñātas tato 'nyaḥ punar ajñātaḥ vastuno jñātājñātasvarūpatvāt pariṇāmi cittam. 4.17
body.translated_text: Objects are like a magnet; the mind, resembling iron, is connected with and colored by them. The object by which the mind is colored is known; another is unknown. Because the object has a nature that is both known and unknown, the mind is subject to change. 4.17

body.text: yasya tu tad eva cittaṃ viṣayas tasya ---

children.text: sadā jñātāś cittavṛttayas tatprabhoḥ puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvāt || YS_4.18 ||
children.translated_text: The modifications of the mind are always known to their lord, <s>Puruṣa</s>, because of His unchanging nature. || YS_4.18 ||

body.translated_text: But for that one whose very mind is the object —

body.text: yadi cittavat prabhur api puruṣaḥ pariṇamet tatas tadviṣayāś cittavṛttayaḥ śabdādiviṣayavaj jñātājñātāḥ syuḥ sadājñātatvaṃ tu manasas tatprabhoḥ puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvam anumāpayati. 4.18
body.translated_text: If the lord <s>Puruṣa</s> were also subject to change like the mind, then the mental modifications that are His objects would be known and unknown, like objects such as sound. But the fact that the mind is always known to its lord <s>Puruṣa</s> implies His unchanging nature by inference. 4.18

body.text: syād āśaṅkā cittam eva svābhāsaṃ viṣayābhāsaṃ ca bhaviṣyatīty agnivat ---

children.translated_text: The mind is not self-luminous, because it is an object of perception (<s>dṛśya</s>). || YS_4.19 ||

body.translated_text: The doubt might arise that the mind itself could be self-luminous and object-luminous, like fire —

body.text: yathetarāṇīndriyāṇi śabdādayaś ca dṛśyatvān na svābhāsāni tathā mano 'pi pratyetavyam. na cāgnir atra dṛṣṭāntaḥ na hy agnir ātmasvarūpam aprakāśaṃ prakāśayati prakāśaś cāyaṃ prakāśyaprakāśakasaṃyoge dṛṣṭaḥ. na ca svarūpamātre 'sti saṃyogaḥ kiṃca svābhāsaṃ cittam ity agrāhyam eva kasyacid iti śabdārthaḥ. tadyathā svātmapratiṣṭham ākāśaṃ na parapratiṣṭham ity arthaḥ svabuddhipracārapratisaṃvedanāt sattvānāṃ pravṛttir dṛśyate --- kruddho 'haṃ bhīto 'ham amutra me rāgo 'mutra me krodha iti etat svabuddher agrahaṇe na yuktam iti. 4.19
body.translated_text: Just as the other senses and objects such as sound are not self-luminous because they are objects of perception, so too should the mind be understood. And fire is not a valid analogy here, for fire does not illuminate its own form when it is unilluminated; this illumination is observed only in the conjunction of the illumined and the illuminator. And there is no conjunction with one's own form [alone]. Moreover, 'the mind is self-luminous' means that it is ungraspable by anyone — this is the meaning. Just as space is self-established, not established by another — such is the meaning. [But] from the self-awareness of one's own mental operations, the activity of beings is observed: 'I am angry,' 'I am afraid,' 'my attachment is toward that,' 'my anger is toward this' — this would not be possible without grasping one's own cognition. 4.19

body.text: ekasamaye cobhayānavadhāraṇam || YS_4.20 ||
body.translated_text: And there cannot be ascertainment of both [self and object] at a single moment. || YS_4.20 ||

body.text: na caikasmin kṣaṇe svapararūpāvadhāraṇaṃ yuktaṃ, kṣaṇikavādino yad bhavanaṃ saiva kriyā tad eva ca kārakam ity abhyupagamaḥ. 4.20
body.translated_text: It is not possible to ascertain both one's own form and another's form at a single moment. For those who hold the doctrine of momentariness, their position is that coming-into-being is itself the action, and that itself is the agent. 4.20

body.text: syān matiḥ svarasaniruddhaṃ cittaṃ cittāntareṇa samanantareṇa gṛhyata iti ---

children.text: cittāntaradṛśye buddhibuddher atiprasaṅgaḥ smṛtisaṃkaraś ca || YS_4.21 ||
children.translated_text: If the mind were seen by another mind, there would be an infinite regress of cognition upon cognition, and a confusion of memories. [YS 4.21]

body.translated_text: The thought might arise that the mind, ceasing spontaneously, is grasped by another mind immediately succeeding it —

body.text: atha cittaṃ cec cittāntareṇa gṛhyeta buddhibuddhiḥ kena gṛhyate, sāpy anyayā sāpy anyayety atiprasaṅgaḥ. smṛtisaṃkaraś ca, yāvanto buddhibuddhīnām anubhavās tāvatyaḥ smṛtayaḥ prāpnuvanti. tatsaṃkarāc caikasmṛtyanavadhāraṇaṃ ca syād ity evaṃ buddhipratisaṃvedinaṃ puruṣam apalapadbhir vaināśikaiḥ sarvam evākulīkṛtam. te tu bhoktṛsvarūpaṃ yatra kvacana kalpayanto na nyāyena saṃgacchante kecit tu sattvamātram api parikalpyāsti sa sattvo ya etān pañca skandhān nikṣipyānyāṃś ca pratisaṃdadhātīty uktvā tata eva punas trasyanti. tathā skandhānāṃ mahannirvedāya virāgāyānutpādāya praśāntaye guror antike brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyāmīty uktvā sattvasya punaḥ sattvam evāpahnuvate. sāṃkhyayogādayas tu pravādāḥ svaśabdena puruṣam eva svāminaṃ cittasya bhoktāram upayantīti. 4.21
body.translated_text: Now, if a mind were apprehended by another mind, by what would the cognition of that cognition be apprehended? And that by yet another, and that by yet another—thus an infinite regress. And there would be a confusion of memories: as many experiences of cognition-upon-cognition as there are, so many memories would result, and from their confusion, no single memory could be ascertained. Thus everything has been thrown into confusion by the <s>Vaināśikas</s> (Buddhists), who deny <s>Puruṣa</s> as the experiencer of cognition. They, positing the nature of the experiencer in various [constructs], do not arrive at consistency. Some, imagining a mere 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>), say: 'There is that entity which, having set aside these five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), takes on others'—and then they are again terrified of that very [assertion]. Likewise, having said 'I shall practice celibacy in the presence of a teacher for the sake of great disenchantment, dispassion, non-arising, and quiescence regarding the aggregates,' they again deny the very existence of that entity. But the doctrines of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and others, in their own terminology, accept <s>Puruṣa</s> itself as the owner, the experiencer of the mind. [4.21]

body.text: katham ---

children.translated_text: When the unchanging consciousness (<s>citi</s>) assumes the form of that [mind], there is awareness of one's own cognitions. [YS 4.22]

children.text:
apariṇāminī hi bhoktṛśaktir apratisaṃkramā ca pariṇāminy arthe pratisaṃkrānteva tadvṛttim anupatati. tasyāś ca prāptacaitanyopagrahasvarūpāyā buddhivṛtter anukārimātratayā buddhivṛttyaviśiṣṭā hi jñānavṛttir ākhyāyate. tathā coktam.
  "na pātālaṃ na ca vivaraṃ girīṇāṃ naivāndhakāraṃ kukṣayo nodadhīnām /
  guhā yasyāṃ nihitaṃ brahma śāśvataṃ buddhivṛttim aviśiṣṭāṃ kavayo vedayante" iti. 4.22
children.translated_text:
The power of the enjoyer is indeed unchanging and non-transferring; yet, as if transferred to the changing object, it follows its activity. And the cognitive activity is described as indistinguishable from the activity of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) that has assumed the form of consciousness—being merely an imitation of it. As it has been said:
  'Not in the netherworld, nor in the caverns of mountains, not in darkness, not in the bowels of the oceans—
  the cave in which the eternal <s>Brahman</s> is hidden is what the sages know as the cognitive activity indistinguishable from <s>buddhi</s>.' [4.22]

body.translated_text: How [is this]?

body.text: ataś caitad abhyupagamyate ---

children.translated_text: The mind, colored by the seer and the seen, is all-purposeful. [YS 4.23]

body.translated_text: Therefore, this is established:

body.text:
mano hi mantavyenārthenoparaktaṃ, tat svayaṃ ca viṣayatvād viṣayiṇā puruṣeṇātmīyayā vṛttyābhisaṃbaddhaṃ, tad etac cittam eva draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṃ viṣayaviṣayinirbhāsaṃ cetanācetanasvarūpāpannaṃ viṣayātmakam apy aviṣayātmakam ivācetanaṃ cetanam iva sphaṭikamaṇikalpaṃ sarvārtham ity ucyate.
  tad anena cittasārūpyeṇa bhrāntāḥ kecit tad eva cetanam ity āhuḥ apare cittamātram evedaṃ sarvaṃ nāsti khalv ayaṃ gavādir ghaṭādiś ca sakāraṇo loka iti. anukampanīyās te. kasmāt, asti hi teṣāṃ bhrāntibījaṃ sarvarūpākāranirbhāsaṃ cittam iti. samādhiprajñāyāṃ prajñeyo 'rthaḥ pratibimbībhūtas tasyālambanībhūtatvād anyaḥ. sa ced arthaś cittamātraṃ syāt kathaṃ prajñayaiva prajñārūpam avadhāryeta. tasmāt pratibimbībhūto 'rthaḥ prajñāyāṃ yenāvadhāryate sa puruṣa iti. evaṃ grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyasvarūpacittabhedāt trayam apy etaj jātitaḥ pravibhajante te samyagdarśinas tair adhigataḥ puruṣaḥ. 4.23
body.translated_text:
The mind is colored by the object to be cognized; and it itself, being an object, is connected with the subject, <s>Puruṣa</s>, through its own activity. This mind, colored by both the seer and the seen, reflecting both object and subject, having assumed both the sentient and insentient natures, though of the nature of an object yet appearing as if not an object, though insentient appearing as if sentient—like a crystal gem—is called 'all-purposeful.'
  Deluded by this semblance to the mind, some declare that it alone is sentient. Others [say]: 'All this is merely mind; this world of cows, pots, and so forth, together with its causes, does not truly exist.' They are to be pitied. Why? Because their ground for confusion is the mind, which reflects all forms and appearances. In the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>, the object to be known has become a reflection—being the support [of that wisdom], it is other [than the wisdom itself]. If that object were merely mind, how could the very form of wisdom be ascertained by wisdom itself? Therefore, the object that has become a reflection in wisdom is ascertained by <s>Puruṣa</s>—that is <s>Puruṣa</s>. Thus, from the differentiation of the mind according to its natures as grasper (<s>grahītṛ</s>), grasping (<s>grahaṇa</s>), and grasped (<s>grāhya</s>), those who see correctly distinguish all three by category, and by them <s>Puruṣa</s> is realized. [4.23]

body.text: kutaś ca ---

children.text: tad asaṃkhyeyavāsanābhiś citram api parārthaṃ saṃhatyakāritvāt || YS_4.24 ||
children.translated_text: That [mind], though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), serves another's purpose, because it acts in combination. [YS 4.24]

body.translated_text: And why [does the mind serve another's purpose]?

body.text: tad etac cittam asaṃkhyeyābhir vāsanābhir eva citrīkṛtam api parārthaṃ parasya bhogāpavargārthaṃ na svārthaṃ saṃhatyakāritvād gṛhavat. saṃhatyakāriṇā cittena na svārthena bhavitavyaṃ, na sukhacittaṃ sukhārthaṃ na jñānaṃ jñānārtham ubhayam apy etat parārtham. yaś ca bhogenāpavargeṇa cārthenārthavān puruṣaḥ sa eva paro na paraḥ sāmānyamātram. yat tu kiṃcit paraṃ sāmānyamātraṃ svarūpeṇodāhared vaināśikas tat sarvaṃ saṃhatyakāritvāt parārtham eva syāt. yas tv asau paro viśeṣaḥ sa na saṃhatyakārī puruṣa iti. 4.24
body.translated_text: That mind, even though made variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s>, serves another's purpose—the purpose of another's enjoyment and liberation—not its own purpose, because it acts in combination, like a house. The mind, acting in combination, cannot serve its own purpose; a pleasant mind does not exist for the sake of pleasure, nor knowledge for the sake of knowledge—both exist for another's purpose. And that other, who is purposeful through [both] enjoyment and liberation, is <s>Puruṣa</s> alone; it is not another that is a mere generality. Whatever other mere generality the <s>Vaināśika</s> (Buddhist) would cite by its own nature—all of that, because it acts in combination, would serve only another's purpose. But that other, which is a particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>), not acting in combination—that is <s>Puruṣa</s>. [4.24]

body.text: viśeṣadarśina ātmabhāvabhāvanānivṛttiḥ || YS_4.25 ||
body.translated_text: For the one who sees the distinction, the pondering upon the nature of self-existence ceases. [YS 4.25]

body.text: yathā prāvṛṣi tṛṇāṅkurasyodbhedena tadbījasattānumīyate tathā mokṣamārgaśravaṇena yasya romaharṣāśrupātau dṛśyete tatrāpy asti viśeṣadarśanabījam apavargabhāgīyaṃ karmābhinirvartitam ity anumīyate. tasyātmabhāvabhāvanā svābhāvikī pravartate yasyābhāvād idam uktaṃ svabhāvaṃ muktvā doṣādyeṣāṃ pūrvapakṣe rucir bhavaty aruciś ca nirṇaye bhavati tatrātmabhāvabhāvanā ko 'ham āsaṃ katham aham āsaṃ kiṃsvid idaṃ kathaṃsvid idaṃ ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ kathaṃ vā bhaviṣyāma iti. sā tu viśeṣadarśino nivartate kutaḥ cittasyaivaiṣa vicitraḥ pariṇāmaḥ, puruṣas tv asatyām avidyāyāṃ śuddhaś cittadharmair aparāmṛṣṭa iti. tato 'syātmabhāvabhāvanā kuśalasya nivartata iti. 4.25
body.translated_text: Just as in the rainy season, from the sprouting of a grass shoot, the existence of its seed is inferred, so too, when upon hearing the path to liberation one experiences horripilation and tears, there too the seed of seeing the distinction—<s>karma</s> leading to liberation (<s>apavargabhāgīya</s>)—is inferred to have been produced. For such a person, the natural pondering upon self-existence proceeds. In the absence of this [seed], it is said that those whose taste inclines toward objections, abandoning their own nature, and whose taste does not incline toward the conclusion—for them the pondering upon self-existence [takes the form]: 'Who was I? How was I? What is this? How is this? What shall we become? How shall we become?' But for the one who sees the distinction, this ceases. Why? Because this is merely the variegated transformation of the mind; <s>Puruṣa</s>, when <s>avidyā</s> is absent, is pure and untouched by the properties of the mind. Therefore, the pondering upon self-existence ceases for the proficient one. [4.25]

body.text: tadā vivekanimnaṃ kaivalyaprāgbhāraṃ cittam || YS_4.26 ||
body.translated_text: Then the mind inclines toward discrimination and gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). [YS 4.26]

body.text: tadānīṃ yad asya cittaṃ viṣayaprāgbhāram ajñānanimnam āsīt tad asyānyathā bhavati kaivalyaprāgbhāraṃ vivekajajñānanimnam iti. 4.26
body.translated_text: At that time, the mind that was formerly inclined toward sense objects and gravitating toward ignorance becomes otherwise—gravitating toward <s>kaivalya</s> and inclined toward knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja-jñāna</s>). [4.26]

body.text: tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇi saṃskārebhyaḥ || YS_4.27 ||
body.translated_text: In the intervals of that, other cognitions [arise] from <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions). [YS 4.27]

body.text: pratyayavivekanimnasya sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrapravāhiṇaś cittasya tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇy asmīti vā mameti vā jānāmīti vā na jānāmīti vā. kutaḥ, kṣīyamāṇabījebhyaḥ pūrvasaṃskārebhya iti. 4.27
body.translated_text: For the mind that is inclined toward discriminative cognition, flowing with only the perception of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>—in its intervals, other cognitions [arise]: 'I am,' 'mine,' 'I know,' or 'I do not know.' From what? From previous <s>saṃskāras</s> whose seeds are diminishing. [4.27]

body.text: hānam eṣāṃ kleśavad uktam || YS_4.28 ||
body.translated_text: The removal of these is stated to be like that of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). [YS 4.28]

body.text: yathā kleśā dagdhabījabhāvā na prarohasamarthā bhavanti tathā jñānāgninā dagdhabījabhāvaḥ pūrvasaṃskāro na pratyayaprasūr bhavati. jñānasaṃskārās tu cittādhikārasamāptim anuśerata iti na cintyante. 4.28
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>kleśas</s>, with their seeds burned, become incapable of sprouting, so too a previous <s>saṃskāra</s> whose seed has been burned by the fire of knowledge becomes incapable of producing cognitions. But the <s>saṃskāras</s> of knowledge follow through to the completion of the mind's authority—they are not a concern. [4.28]

body.text: prasaṃkhyāne 'py akusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāter dharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ || YS_4.29 ||
body.translated_text: For one who has no self-interest even in the highest discriminative knowledge, from complete discriminative perception in every way, [there arises] the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>dharma-megha</s> (cloud of <s>dharma</s>). [YS 4.29]

body.text: yadāyaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prasaṃkhyāne 'py akusīdas tato 'pi na kiṃcit prārthayate. tatrāpi viraktasya sarvathā vivekakhyātir eva bhavatīti saṃskārabījakṣayān nāsya pratyayāntarāṇy utpadyante tadāsya dharmamegho nāma samādhir bhavati. 4.29
body.translated_text: When this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (knower) has no self-interest even in discriminative knowledge (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>), desires nothing even from that—being dispassionate toward even that, only complete discriminative perception arises in every way. From the destruction of the seeds of <s>saṃskāras</s>, no other cognitions arise for him; then for him the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>dharma-megha</s> (cloud of <s>dharma</s>) arises. [4.29]

body.text: tataḥ kleśakarmanivṛttiḥ || YS_4.30 ||
body.translated_text: From that, the cessation of afflictions and <s>karma</s>. [YS 4.30]

body.text: tallābhād avidyādayaḥ kleśāḥ samūlakāṣaṃ kaṣitā bhavanti kuśalākuśalāś ca karmāśayāḥ samūlaghātaṃ hatā bhavanti. kleśakarmanivṛttau jīvann eva vidvān vimukto bhavati kasmāt, yasmād viparyayo bhavasya kāraṇam. na hi kṣīṇaviparyayaḥ kaścit kenacit kvacij jāto dṛśyata iti. 4.30
body.translated_text: From the attainment of that [<s>dharma-megha samādhi</s>], the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) beginning with <s>avidyā</s> are uprooted completely, and the stores of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> are destroyed at the root. With the cessation of afflictions and <s>karma</s>, the knower, while still living, becomes liberated. Why? Because erroneous perception (<s>viparyaya</s>) is the cause of existence (<s>bhava</s>). No one in whom erroneous perception has been destroyed is ever seen to be born anywhere, at any time, from any [cause]. [4.30]

body.text: tadā sarvāvaraṇamalāpetasya jñānasyānantyāj jñeyam alpam || YS_4.31 ||
body.translated_text: Then, with all covering impurities removed from knowledge, due to the infinity of knowledge, what is to be known becomes small. [YS 4.31]

children.text: sarvaiḥ kleśakarmāvaraṇair vimuktasya jñānasyānantyaṃ bhavati. āvarakeṇa tamasābhibhūtam āvṛtam anantaṃ jñānasattvaṃ kvacid eva rajasā pravartitam udghāṭitaṃ grahaṇasamarthaṃ bhavati. tatra yadā sarvair āvaraṇamalair apagataṃ bhavati tadā bhavaty asyānantyam. jñānasyānantyāj jñeyam alpaṃ saṃpadyate yathākāśe khadyotaḥ. yatredam uktam ---
children.translated_text: Knowledge freed from all the coverings of afflictions and <s>karma</s> becomes infinite. The infinite <s>sattva</s> of knowledge, overcome and covered by the obscuring <s>tamas</s>, only sometimes set in motion by <s>rajas</s>, is opened up and becomes capable of apprehension. When it has become free from all covering impurities, then its infinity manifests. Due to the infinity of knowledge, what is to be known becomes small—like a firefly in the sky. As it has been stated here:
"The blind one pierced the gem; the fingerless one strung it;

children.text: agrīvas taṃ pratyamuñcat tam ajihvo 'bhyapūjayat //" iti. 4.31
children.translated_text: the neckless one wore it; the tongueless one praised it." [4.31]

body.text: tataḥ kṛtārthānāṃ pariṇāmakramasamāptir guṇānām || YS_4.32 ||
body.translated_text: Then, the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, having fulfilled their purpose, comes to an end. [YS 4.32]

body.text: tasya dharmameghasyodayāt kṛtārthānāṃ guṇānāṃ pariṇāmakramaḥ parisamāpyate na hi kṛtabhogāpavargāḥ parisamāptakramāḥ kṣaṇam apy avasthātum utsahante. 4.32
body.translated_text: From the arising of that <s>dharma-megha</s> [<s>samādhi</s>], the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s> that have fulfilled their purpose comes to completion. For [the <s>guṇas</s>] that have completed their purposes of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), and whose sequence has been completed, cannot endure even for a moment. [4.32]

body.text: atha ko 'yaṃ kramo nāmeti ---

children.translated_text: Sequence (<s>krama</s>) is the correlate of moments (<s>kṣaṇas</s>), apprehensible at the termination of transformation. [YS 4.33]

body.translated_text: Now, what is this 'sequence' (<s>krama</s>)?

body.text:
kṣaṇānantaryātmā pariṇāmasyāparāntenāvasānena gṛhyate kramaḥ na hy ananubhūtakramakṣaṇā purāṇatā vastrasyānte bhavati nityeṣu ca kramo dṛṣṭaḥ.
  dvayī ceyaṃ nityatā kūṭasthanityatā pariṇāminityatā ca. tatra kūṭasthanityatā puruṣasya. pariṇāminityatā guṇānām. yasmin pariṇamyamāne tattvaṃ na vihanyate tan nityam ubhayasya ca tattvānabhighātān nityatvam. tatra guṇadharmeṣu buddhyādiṣu pariṇāmāparāntanirgrāhyaḥ kramo labdhaparyavasāno nityeṣu dharmiṣu guṇeṣv alabdhaparyavasānaḥ. kūṭasthanityeṣu svarūpamātrapratiṣṭheṣu muktapuruṣeṣu svarūpāstitā krameṇaivānubhūyata iti tatrāpy alabdhaparyavasānaḥ śabdapṛṣṭhenāstikriyām upādāya kalpita iti.
  athāsya saṃsārasya sthityā gatyā ca guṇeṣu vartamānasyāsti kramasamāptir na veti. avacanīyam etat katham asti praśna ekāntavacanīyaḥ sarvo jāto mariṣyatīti oṃ bhoḥ iti.
body.translated_text: Sequence (<s>krama</s>) consists of the unbroken succession of moments and is grasped at the final end of a transformation. For the oldness of a cloth at its end does not exist without the experienced sequence of moments. And sequence is observed in permanent entities. And this permanence is twofold: the immutable permanence (<s>kūṭasthanityatā</s>) and the permanence of the transforming (<s>pariṇāminityatā</s>). Of these, immutable permanence belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s>; the permanence of the transforming [belongs to the <s>guṇas</s>].

body.text: atha sarvo mṛtvā janiṣyata iti vibhajyavacanīyam etat. pratyuditakhyātiḥ kṣīṇatṛṣṇaḥ kuśalo na janiṣyata itaras tu janiṣyate. tathā manuṣyajātiḥ śreyasī na vā śreyasīty evaṃ paripṛṣṭe vibhajya vacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ paśūn adhikṛtya śreyasī devān ṛṣīṃś cādhikṛtya neti. ayaṃ tv avacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ saṃsāro 'yam antavān athānanta iti. kuśalasyāsti saṃsārakramasamāptir netarasyeti anyatarāvadhāraṇe doṣaḥ tasmād vyākaraṇīya evāyaṃ praśna iti. 4.33
body.translated_text: Now, [the question] 'Does everyone who dies get reborn?' — this must be answered with a distinction. One in whom discriminative knowledge has arisen and craving has been extinguished, being skillful, will not be reborn; but another will be reborn. Likewise, [the question] 'Is the human birth the best or not the best?' — when asked thus, the question must be answered with a distinction: it is the best compared to animals, but [not compared to] gods and sages.

body.text: guṇādhikārakramasamāptau kaivalyam uktaṃ tatsvarūpam avadhāryate ---

children.text: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktir iti || YS_4.34 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya</s> is the involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>, which are devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>; or [it is] the establishment of the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) in its own nature. [<s>YS</s> 4.34]

children.text: kṛtabhogāpavargāṇāṃ puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ yaḥ pratiprasavaḥ kāryakāraṇātmakānāṃ guṇānāṃ tat kaivalyaṃ, svarūpapratiṣṭhā punar buddhisattvānabhisaṃbandhāt puruṣasya citiśaktir eva kevalā, tasyāḥ sadā tathaivāvasthānaṃ kaivalyam iti. 4.34
children.translated_text: When the <s>guṇas</s>, consisting of cause and effect, have fulfilled [the purposes of] experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) and are devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, their involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) — that is <s>kaivalya</s>. And the establishment in one's own nature is the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone, due to the non-connection with the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s>; the abiding of that [power] forever in that very state — that is <s>kaivalya</s>. [4.34]

body.translated_text: Having stated that <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) [comes] at the completion of the sequence of the purpose of the <s>guṇas</s>, its true nature is now determined —

body.text: iti śrīpātañjale sāṃkhyapravacane yogaśāstre vyāsabhāṣye kaivalyapādaś caturthaḥ 4.
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the fourth chapter on Liberation (<s>Kaivalyapāda</s>), in the <s>Vyāsabhāṣya</s> on the <s>Yogaśāstra</s> of the <s>Sāṃkhyapravacana</s> by the venerable <s>Patañjali</s>.
